top_down_rules.title: Verify Ohm's Law for AC Circuits
top_down_rules.description: In AC circuits, Ohm's Law is extended to use impedance (Z) instead of resistance (R). The voltage across an element is V = I * Z, where Z can be complex.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the voltage (V) is calculated as the product of current (I) and impedance (Z). Verify that Z is expressed as a complex number in either rectangular form (R + jX) or polar form (|Z|∠θ). Confirm that the phase relationship between voltage and current is consistent with the impedance angle.
common_errors: Using resistance (R) instead of impedance (Z) in AC circuits.
Ignoring the phase angle when using complex impedance.
Incorrect conversion between polar and rectangular forms of impedance.

top_down_rules.title: Check Frequency Dependence of Reactance
top_down_rules.description: The reactance of capacitors and inductors depends on the angular frequency (ω = 2πf). Capacitive reactance is X_C = -1/(ωC), and inductive reactance is X_L = ωL.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify the correct formula for X_C and X_L, ensuring that the angular frequency (ω) and the element values (C or L) are used appropriately. Confirm that the negative sign is applied for capacitive reactance and that the units of reactance are in ohms (Ω).
common_errors: Using linear frequency (f) instead of angular frequency (ω = 2πf).
Incorrectly applying the negative sign for capacitive reactance.
Swapping the formulas for X_C and X_L.

top_down_rules.title: Validate Impedance in Series and Parallel Combinations
top_down_rules.description: For series circuits, impedances add directly (Z_eq = Z_1 + Z_2 + ...). For parallel circuits, the reciprocal rule applies (1/Z_eq = 1/Z_1 + 1/Z_2 + ...).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the correct formulas are used for combining impedances in series and parallel configurations. Ensure proper handling of complex arithmetic, including addition, reciprocals, and conversions between polar and rectangular forms.
common_errors: Incorrectly adding impedances in parallel circuits.
Forgetting to invert the result when calculating equivalent impedance for parallel circuits.
Neglecting the imaginary component when combining impedances.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Power Calculations in AC Circuits
top_down_rules.description: The real power (P), reactive power (Q), and apparent power (S) are related to the voltage, current, and impedance phase angle: P = VIcosθ, Q = VIsinθ, and S = VI.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the correct trigonometric components of the phase angle are used to calculate P, Q, and S. Confirm that the power factor (cosθ) is consistent with the impedance angle. Verify that the units of power are consistent (watts for P, VAR for Q, and VA for S).
common_errors: Confusing real power (P) with apparent power (S).
Using incorrect trigonometric functions for P and Q.
Ignoring the phase angle in power factor calculations.

top_down_rules.title: Check Resonance Condition in RLC Circuits
top_down_rules.description: In an RLC circuit, resonance occurs when the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance (X_L = |X_C|). At resonance, the total impedance is purely resistive.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that ω_res = 1/√(LC) is used to calculate the resonance angular frequency. Confirm that at resonance, Z = R (no imaginary component). Ensure that the phase angle of the impedance is zero at resonance.
common_errors: Forgetting to equalize X_L and X_C at resonance.
Misinterpreting resonance as a condition where Z = 0.
Incorrect calculation of resonance frequency using ω_res = 1/√(LC).

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency of Impedance and Reactance
top_down_rules.description: Impedance (Z) and reactance (X_L, X_C) must have the dimension of ohms (Ω). Impedance is a complex quantity, but its magnitude and components must be dimensionally consistent.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all calculations involving Z, X_L, and X_C result in units of ohms (Ω). Check the dimensional consistency of intermediate terms, such as ωL and 1/(ωC). Ensure that capacitance (C) and inductance (L) are expressed in standard units (farads and henries, respectively).
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for capacitance (C) or inductance (L).
Calculating Z or X without confirming units of intermediate terms.
Mixing incompatible units, such as radians and degrees, in calculations.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Use of RMS Values for AC Voltage and Current
top_down_rules.description: In AC circuits, root mean square (RMS) values are used for voltage and current in power and impedance calculations. RMS values relate to peak values as V_RMS = V_peak / √2 and I_RMS = I_peak / √2.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that RMS values are used in calculations unless specified otherwise. For peak values given, confirm conversion to RMS using the correct formula. Verify that RMS values are used consistently in power and impedance calculations.
common_errors: Using peak values instead of RMS values in power calculations.
Incorrect conversion between peak and RMS values.
Assuming equivalence of RMS and peak values.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Phase Angle Sign Convention
top_down_rules.description: The phase angle (θ) of impedance is positive for inductive circuits (current lags voltage) and negative for capacitive circuits (current leads voltage).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the sign of the phase angle is consistent with the type of reactance (inductive or capacitive). Ensure that angles are measured in the correct unit (radians or degrees) and that conversions between units are accurate.
common_errors: Reversing the sign of the phase angle for inductive or capacitive circuits.
Using degrees and radians interchangeably without conversion.
Incorrectly interpreting the relationship between current and voltage phase.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Quality Factor in RLC Circuits
top_down_rules.description: The quality factor (Q) of an RLC circuit is a measure of its sharpness of resonance and is defined as Q = ω_resL/R for series circuits or Q = R/(ω_resL) for parallel circuits.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the correct formula for Q is used based on the circuit configuration (series or parallel). Verify that ω_res is calculated correctly and that the units of Q are dimensionless.
common_errors: Using the wrong formula for Q based on circuit configuration.
Incorrect calculation of ω_res.
Confusing the quality factor with other parameters like power factor.

top_down_rules.title: Verify correct application of Biot-Savart Law equation
top_down_rules.description: The Biot-Savart Law states that the magnetic field dB at a point due to a current element I·dl is proportional to the cross product of the current element vector and the unit vector pointing from the current element to the observation point, divided by the square of the distance between them. This law is given as: dB = (μ₀ / 4π) * (I·dl × r̂) / r². It applies for steady currents.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the magnetic field contribution dB is calculated using the cross product (I·dl × r̂), and the denominator contains r² where r is the distance between the current element and the observation point. Verify that μ₀ / 4π is included as a constant multiplier.
common_errors: Forgetting to include the cross product in the equation
Incorrectly calculating the distance r or the unit vector r̂
Omitting the constant μ₀ / 4π
Using r instead of r² in the denominator
Using non-steady currents, which invalidates the law

top_down_rules.title: Verify correct application of Ampere's Law in integral form
top_down_rules.description: Ampere's Law relates the closed line integral of the magnetic field B around a closed loop to the current enclosed by the loop: ∮B·dl = μ₀I_enclosed. It is valid for steady currents and symmetric geometries where the magnetic field is uniform along the loop.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the line integral of B·dl is properly calculated and equated to μ₀ times the total current enclosed by the loop. Ensure the loop is chosen to align with the symmetry of the problem.
common_errors: Failure to consider the direction of the magnetic field (sign convention in B·dl)
Forgetting to enclose the current completely within the loop
Applying Ampere's Law to non-steady currents
Incorrectly assuming symmetry in situations where it does not exist

top_down_rules.title: Ensure correct use of coordinate systems and sign conventions
top_down_rules.description: Both Biot-Savart Law and Ampere's Law require consistent application of coordinate systems (Cartesian, cylindrical, or spherical) to define vectors. The right-hand rule is used to determine the direction of the magnetic field.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify the coordinate system used is consistent throughout the problem, and the right-hand rule is applied correctly for cross products and determining field directions. Ensure proper transformations are applied when switching between coordinate systems.
common_errors: Switching between coordinate systems without proper transformations
Incorrect application of the right-hand rule for the cross product
Mislabeling components of vectors in the chosen system

top_down_rules.title: Verify geometric constraints for symmetry in Ampere's Law
top_down_rules.description: Ampere's Law in integral form is most effective for symmetric geometries like infinite wires, solenoids, or toroids, where the magnetic field is uniform and constant around the chosen loop.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the geometry satisfies symmetry conditions. For instance, ensure the magnetic field is constant along the loop or the current enclosed is distributed uniformly. Verify that the chosen Amperian loop aligns with the geometry.
common_errors: Applying Ampere's Law to asymmetric geometries
Neglecting to account for non-uniformity in the magnetic field
Incorrectly selecting an Amperian loop that does not align with the geometry

top_down_rules.title: Ensure laws are applied to steady currents only
top_down_rules.description: Both Biot-Savart Law and Ampere's Law are valid only for steady (time-independent) currents. For time-varying currents, Maxwell's equations, including the displacement current, must be considered.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the problem explicitly states or implies steady currents. If currents are time-varying, flag the solution for missing displacement current contributions and suggest using Maxwell's equations.
common_errors: Applying Biot-Savart or Ampere's Law to time-varying currents
Ignoring the displacement current term in time-varying cases
Assuming steady current without verifying conditions

top_down_rules.title: Verify dimensional and unit consistency in calculations
top_down_rules.description: The magnetic field B has units of teslas (T) in the SI system, and its dimensions are [M][T]⁻²[A]⁻¹. Ensure all terms in the Biot-Savart and Ampere's Law equations conform to these units.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check each term in the equations for consistent units. For example, μ₀ has units of T·m/A, and r² should be in meters². Verify that the final magnetic field result has units of teslas.
common_errors: Omitting or miscalculating the μ₀ constant
Using incorrect units for distance (r) or current (I)
Mismatch in units between magnetic field B and other terms

top_down_rules.title: Verify magnetic field direction consistency
top_down_rules.description: The direction of the magnetic field calculated using Biot-Savart Law or Ampere's Law must conform to the right-hand rule or symmetry arguments.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the calculated field direction follows the right-hand rule for current-carrying wires or symmetry constraints for Ampere's Law. Verify that the direction is consistent with the problem's setup and assumptions.
common_errors: Incorrect use of the right-hand rule for field direction
Ignoring symmetry constraints for field direction in Ampere's Law
Reversing the field direction due to sign convention errors

top_down_rules.title: Ensure superposition principle is applied when multiple sources exist
top_down_rules.description: The magnetic field due to multiple current elements is the vector sum of the fields produced by each element, as per the superposition principle.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the magnetic field contributions from all current elements are added vectorially to find the total field. Ensure no contributions are neglected.
common_errors: Adding magnetic field contributions algebraically instead of vectorially
Neglecting contributions from some current elements
Incorrectly combining fields from different sources

top_down_rules.title: Verify boundary conditions at interfaces
top_down_rules.description: At the boundary between two media, the tangential component of the magnetic field B and the normal component of the magnetic flux density B·n must satisfy continuity conditions.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the tangential component of B is continuous across the boundary, and the normal component of B·n accounts for any surface currents or discontinuities.
common_errors: Ignoring surface currents at boundaries
Incorrectly applying continuity conditions for B
Neglecting the effect of material properties on B

top_down_rules.title: Apply Capacitance Formula for Parallel Plate Capacitors
top_down_rules.description: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is given by C = ε * A / d, where ε is the permittivity of the material between the plates, A is the area of one plate, and d is the separation between the plates.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the area (A) and separation (d) are correctly used in the formula for parallel plate capacitors, and ensure the permittivity (ε) corresponds to the material between the plates.
common_errors: Using incorrect formula for parallel plate capacitors
Confusing the area with the separation distance
Ignoring the permittivity of the dielectric material

top_down_rules.title: Calculate Energy Stored in Capacitor Correctly
top_down_rules.description: The energy stored in a capacitor is given by U = 1/2 * C * V^2, where C is the capacitance and V is the voltage across the capacitor.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the energy is calculated using the correct formula, with accurate values for capacitance (C) and voltage (V). Verify that the 1/2 factor is included.
common_errors: Omitting the 1/2 factor in the formula
Using resistance instead of capacitance
Using an incorrect voltage value for the calculation

top_down_rules.title: Account for Dielectric Constant in Capacitance
top_down_rules.description: The introduction of a dielectric increases the capacitance by a factor of the dielectric constant k, modifying the equation to C = k * ε₀ * A / d, where ε₀ is the permittivity of free space.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the presence of a dielectric is accounted for in the capacitance calculation, and verify that the dielectric constant (k) is applied correctly.
common_errors: Ignoring the increase in capacitance due to the dielectric
Applying the dielectric constant to an incorrect variable
Confusing the dielectric constant (k) with the permittivity (ε)

top_down_rules.title: Maintain Correct Sign Conventions for Potential Differences
top_down_rules.description: Voltage is defined as the potential difference where the positive terminal is at a higher potential. Correct sign conventions are crucial for determining current flow direction and energy calculations.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that potential differences are used with the correct sign conventions, and ensure polarity is assigned accurately based on the electric field direction.
common_errors: Reversing the potential difference sign
Incorrectly assigning polarity
Ignoring the direction of the electric field

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Unit Consistency in Capacitance Calculations
top_down_rules.description: Capacitance has units of farads (F), equivalent to coulomb/volt. Dimensional consistency ensures accurate calculations.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all terms in capacitance calculations use consistent units, such as meters for area dimensions, volts for voltage, and farads for capacitance.
common_errors: Mixing up area units (e.g., cm² vs m²)
Using incorrect units for the dielectric constant
Miscalculating due to voltage in incorrect units (e.g., V vs mV)

top_down_rules.title: Apply Correct Rules for Capacitors in Series or Parallel
top_down_rules.description: Capacitors in series have a reciprocal capacitance sum, while those in parallel directly add: 1/C_total = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ + ... for series; C_total = C₁ + C₂ + ... for parallel.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify the configuration of capacitors (series or parallel) and ensure the correct formula is applied for the total capacitance calculation.
common_errors: Confusing series and parallel formulae
Incorrectly summing reciprocal quantities
Misidentifying circuit sections as series or parallel

top_down_rules.title: Verify Ideal Conditions for Capacitance Calculations
top_down_rules.description: Capacitance equations assume ideal conditions: perfectly conductive plates, uniform electric field, and negligible edge effects.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that physical assumptions hold true, such as ignoring fringing effects or non-uniform fields, and verify that the plates are assumed to be perfectly conductive.
common_errors: Considering edge effects without applying corrections
Assuming a uniform field in non-ideal cases
Incorrectly applying the perfect plate assumption

top_down_rules.title: Account for Temperature Effects on Capacitance
top_down_rules.description: Capacitance can vary with temperature due to changes in the dielectric material's properties. This is particularly important for materials with high temperature coefficients.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify whether temperature effects on the dielectric constant or material properties are significant and accounted for in calculations.
common_errors: Ignoring temperature dependence of the dielectric constant
Assuming constant capacitance in varying temperature conditions
Failing to use temperature-corrected material properties

top_down_rules.title: Verify Coulomb's Law formula usage
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the formula F = k * (|q1 * q2|) / r^2 is used correctly. This equation calculates the magnitude of the force between two point charges, where k is Coulomb's constant, q1 and q2 are the charges, and r is the distance between the charges.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the force is calculated using F = k * |q1 * q2| / r^2 and that all variables are correctly substituted. Ensure that the absolute value of the product of charges is used, the distance is squared, and the correct value of Coulomb's constant is applied.
common_errors: Forgetting to square the distance (r^2)
Using q1 * q2 instead of |q1 * q2|, thus missing the absolute value
Using an incorrect value for Coulomb's constant (k)

top_down_rules.title: Verify Electric Field formula usage
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the electric field is calculated using E = F / q or E = k * |q| / r^2, where E is the electric field, F is the force experienced by a test charge q, and r is the distance from the source charge.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the electric field magnitude is calculated using E = k * |q| / r^2 or derived from E = F / q. Verify that the absolute value of the charge is used, the distance is squared, and the correct relationships between force, charge, and field are applied.
common_errors: Forgetting to divide by q when using E = F / q
Not using the absolute value of the charge in the formula
Forgetting to square the distance in E = k * |q| / r^2

top_down_rules.title: Ensure correct sign conventions for forces and fields
top_down_rules.description: Verify that the direction of the electric force and field is consistent with the charges' nature: like charges repel, and opposite charges attract. Ensure vector directions are assigned correctly in the coordinate system.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the electric field vector points away from positive charges and toward negative charges. Ensure the electric force aligns with the field for positive charges and opposes it for negative charges. Confirm that the directions are consistent with the problem's coordinate system.
common_errors: Incorrect force direction for repulsion/attraction
Electric field vector pointing toward positive charges instead of away
Forgetting to consider vector directions in calculations

top_down_rules.title: Verify consistency of coordinate system in vector representation
top_down_rules.description: Make sure all electric force and field vectors are expressed in a consistent coordinate system (Cartesian, spherical, etc.), with proper consideration of components and angles.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that vector components (e.g., x, y, z) are consistent with the chosen coordinate system and that angles are measured correctly relative to the axes. Ensure that conversions between coordinate systems, if any, are performed accurately.
common_errors: Mixing coordinate systems (e.g., Cartesian with spherical)
Incorrect calculation of vector components
Using angles in degrees when radians are required or vice versa

top_down_rules.title: Ensure geometric constraints are satisfied
top_down_rules.description: Confirm that the distance r between charges is positive and matches the stated configuration. Verify that charges are treated as point charges unless specified otherwise.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if r > 0 and consistent with the given geometry. Ensure charges are sufficiently small to approximate as point charges if Coulomb's Law is applied. Verify that the physical arrangement of charges matches the problem's description.
common_errors: Using a zero or negative distance in calculations
Applying Coulomb's Law to extended charges without proper treatment
Incorrect interpretation of the charges' physical arrangement

top_down_rules.title: Verify validity conditions for Coulomb's Law application
top_down_rules.description: Ensure Coulomb's Law is applied only under the assumption of stationary point charges in a vacuum or sufficiently low-medium dielectric constant environment.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if charges are stationary and point-like, and that the medium is either vacuum or has a specified permittivity ε consistent with the problem. Ensure that magnetic effects are not ignored if charges are moving.
common_errors: Applying Coulomb's Law to moving charges without considering magnetic effects
Using Coulomb's Law in a medium without adjusting for permittivity
Using it for non-point charges without additional approximations

top_down_rules.title: Verify dimensional and unit consistency
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that all terms in the equations have consistent units and dimensions. For Coulomb's Law, force (F) must have units of Newtons (N), charge (q) in Coulombs (C), distance (r) in meters (m), and k in N·m²/C².
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the units of the calculated force or electric field match the expected result based on the input quantities. Verify that all input quantities are converted to SI units before substitution.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for distance (e.g., cm instead of m)
Forgetting to convert charge values from microcoulombs to coulombs
Incorrect unit for Coulomb's constant

top_down_rules.title: Verify application of superposition principle
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the net electric field or force is calculated by vector addition of individual contributions from multiple charges, using E_net = ΣE_i or F_net = ΣF_i.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the contributions from all charges are calculated separately and summed as vectors, considering both magnitude and direction. Ensure that vector addition is performed correctly, including handling angles and components.
common_errors: Adding magnitudes instead of vectors when determining net field or force
Omitting contributions from one or more charges
Incorrect vector addition due to sign or angle errors

top_down_rules.title: Verify boundary conditions for electric fields
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that boundary conditions, such as the behavior of electric fields at the surface of conductors or at infinity, are correctly applied.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the electric field inside a conductor is zero and that the field at the surface is perpendicular to the surface. Verify that the field approaches zero at infinity unless specified otherwise.
common_errors: Incorrect assumption about the electric field inside a conductor
Forgetting that the electric field is perpendicular to the surface of a conductor
Incorrect treatment of the field at infinity

top_down_rules.title: Verify Ohm's Law Application
top_down_rules.description: Ohm's Law defines the relationship between current (I), voltage (V), and resistance (R): V = IR. It applies only to materials or components with linear, ohmic behavior (constant resistance).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if V = I * R in the solution and ensure the material is specified as ohmic. If the resistance varies with current or temperature, Ohm's Law cannot be applied directly.
common_errors: Assuming Ohm's Law applies to non-ohmic materials (e.g., diodes, transistors)
Incorrect rearrangement of the equation (e.g., using R = V * I instead of R = V / I)

top_down_rules.title: Validate Use of Resistance Formula
top_down_rules.description: The resistance of a uniform conductor is R = ρ * (L/A), where ρ is resistivity, L is length, and A is cross-sectional area. This formula applies to uniform, isotropic materials.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if R is calculated as R = ρ * (L/A), and check that all variables are properly defined and used. Ensure the conductor is uniform and isotropic.
common_errors: Forgetting to include the cross-sectional area (A) in the denominator
Using incorrect units for resistivity, length, or area
Applying this formula to non-uniform or anisotropic materials

top_down_rules.title: Check Sign Convention for Current Direction
top_down_rules.description: Current direction is conventionally defined as the flow of positive charge. It is opposite to the direction of electron flow. Ensure that the chosen current direction is consistent throughout the solution.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the current direction matches the problem setup or stated assumptions. If using electron flow, ensure it is explicitly noted.
common_errors: Confusing the direction of electron flow with conventional current
Inconsistently assigning current direction in circuit diagrams

top_down_rules.title: Verify Power Dissipation Equation
top_down_rules.description: The power dissipated in a resistor is given by P = IV, P = I^2R, or P = V^2/R, depending on the known quantities. These are derived from Ohm's Law.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the correct power formula is used based on the available variables (I, V, R). Verify the consistency of dimensional units in the power calculation.
common_errors: Using the wrong power formula for the given variables
Forgetting to square the current or voltage when using P = I^2R or P = V^2/R
Unit mismatch, such as not converting milliamps to amps

top_down_rules.title: Apply Kirchhoff's Voltage and Current Laws
top_down_rules.description: Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL): The sum of currents entering a junction equals the sum leaving it. Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL): The sum of voltage drops in a closed loop equals zero.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all currents at a junction satisfy KCL and all voltage drops around a loop satisfy KVL. Ensure consistent sign conventions for current and voltage.
common_errors: Missing terms in the summation for KCL or KVL
Incorrect sign convention for voltage drops or current directions
Failure to account for all branches in a circuit

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency in Equations
top_down_rules.description: Verify that all terms in the equations for current, resistance, voltage, and power have consistent units. For example, voltage (V) in volts, resistance (R) in ohms, current (I) in amperes, and power (P) in watts.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that units are consistent and correctly converted where necessary. For example, ensure that milliamps are converted to amps if necessary, and resistances in kilohms are converted to ohms.
common_errors: Using mixed units (e.g., milliamps with ohms without conversion)
Incorrect conversion of prefixes like milli, kilo, or mega
Omitting unit conversions entirely

top_down_rules.title: Verify Resistance Dependence on Temperature
top_down_rules.description: The resistance of a material changes with temperature, typically modeled as R(T) = R_0[1 + α(T - T_0)], where α is the temperature coefficient of resistance. This is crucial for non-room-temperature conditions.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if temperature dependence is accounted for when the problem involves significant temperature changes or explicitly mentions temperature effects.
common_errors: Ignoring the temperature dependence of resistance when significant
Using an incorrect value for the temperature coefficient (α)
Assuming resistance is constant without justification

top_down_rules.title: Check Circuit Boundary Conditions
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that all boundary conditions, such as total supplied voltage, current, or resistance, are satisfied for the entire circuit. Verify the sum of all branch currents matches the total current for parallel circuits, and total resistance is computed correctly.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the total voltage across a series circuit equals the sum of individual voltage drops, and the current splits correctly in parallel circuits.
common_errors: Incorrectly summing resistances for parallel or series configurations
Ignoring total supplied voltage or current constraints
Misapplying current or voltage division rules

top_down_rules.title: Apply Superposition Theorem
top_down_rules.description: The superposition theorem states that in a linear circuit with multiple sources, the current or voltage at any element is the algebraic sum of the currents or voltages produced by each source independently.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that each independent current or voltage source is considered one at a time, with all other sources turned off (replacing voltage sources with short circuits and current sources with open circuits). Then, check that the results for each source are summed to find the total response.
common_errors: Forgetting to turn off sources aside from the one being considered
Incorrectly replacing sources (e.g., using open circuit for voltage source)
Failing to sum individual contributions correctly

top_down_rules.title: Ensure sum of voltages in a closed loop equals zero
top_down_rules.description: Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) states that the algebraic sum of all voltages around a closed loop in a circuit must equal zero. This is derived from the conservation of energy principle in electrical circuits.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Sum of voltage drops and gains across all components in a closed loop must equal zero: ΣV = 0.
common_errors: Forgetting to include the polarity of voltage sources or resistors
Incorrectly summing voltage drops (e.g., forgetting negative signs for voltage drops)
Omitting a component in the loop equation

top_down_rules.title: Ensure sum of currents at a junction is zero
top_down_rules.description: Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) states that the total current entering a junction must equal the total current leaving the junction. This follows from the conservation of electric charge.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Sum of currents entering and leaving a junction must be zero: ΣI_in = ΣI_out.
common_errors: Mislabeling the direction of currents at a junction
Neglecting to include all branches connected to a junction
Incorrect signs for current entering or leaving

top_down_rules.title: Verify Ohm's Law for resistive components
top_down_rules.description: Ohm's Law states that the voltage across a resistor is directly proportional to the current flowing through it: V = IR.
top_down_rules.check_logic: For each resistive component, check if V = IR holds true.
common_errors: Using incorrect resistance values from the problem statement
Forgetting to account for series or parallel combinations of resistors
Incorrect unit conversion (e.g., kilo-ohms to ohms)

top_down_rules.title: Ensure correct resistor combination rules are applied
top_down_rules.description: Resistors in series add directly (R_eq = R1 + R2 + ...), while resistors in parallel combine as reciprocals (1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ...).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if equivalent resistance calculations for series or parallel combinations are correct.
common_errors: Using series formula for parallel resistors or vice versa
Forgetting to take the reciprocal when calculating equivalent resistance for parallel resistors
Misidentifying which resistors are in series or parallel

top_down_rules.title: Ensure power conservation in the circuit
top_down_rules.description: The total power supplied by voltage sources must equal the total power dissipated by resistors and other elements in the circuit.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Sum of power supplied (ΣP_supply = ΣV_source * I) must equal sum of power dissipated (ΣP_dissipated = ΣI^2 * R).
common_errors: Forgetting to square the current in power dissipation calculation
Misapplying the power formula for voltage sources
Ignoring power contributions from all elements in the circuit

top_down_rules.title: Verify proper sign convention usage for voltages and currents
top_down_rules.description: When applying KVL or Ohm's Law, the sign of the voltage drop or current must be consistent with the chosen direction of traversal or assumed current flow.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that voltage drops across resistors are consistent with the assumed current direction and that voltage gains are correctly identified.
common_errors: Incorrectly assigning signs to voltage drops or gains
Using inconsistent current directions for different components
Forgetting to reverse signs when changing the traversal direction in a loop

top_down_rules.title: Check for dimensional and unit consistency
top_down_rules.description: All equations involving voltages, currents, resistances, and powers must have consistent units: volts (V), amperes (A), ohms (Ω), and watts (W).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the units in all calculations are consistent and correctly converted if necessary.
common_errors: Mixing up units (e.g., using kilo-ohms instead of ohms without proper conversion)
Using incorrect prefixes for units (e.g., mA instead of A)
Failing to check unit consistency in derived quantities like power (P = VI)

top_down_rules.title: Ensure the validity of Kirchhoff's Laws
top_down_rules.description: Kirchhoff's Laws are valid only for circuits with steady-state currents (DC circuits) and lumped elements. They cannot be applied directly to circuits with high-frequency AC signals or distributed elements like transmission lines.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the circuit operates under DC conditions and consists of lumped elements.
common_errors: Applying Kirchhoff's Laws to circuits with high-frequency AC signals
Ignoring the distributed nature of components in non-lumped systems
Using Kirchhoff's Laws in non-steady-state conditions

topics.topic: Displacement Current and Its Role in Maxwell's Equations

top_down_rules.title: Verify Ampère-Maxwell Law Incorporates Displacement Current
top_down_rules.description: The Ampère-Maxwell Law modifies Ampère's Law by including the displacement current term (ε₀ ∂E/∂t). This ensures continuity of the magnetic field in time-varying electric fields.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the displacement current term (ε₀ ∂E/∂t) is correctly added to the conduction current (∇ × B = μ₀(J + ε₀ ∂E/∂t)) in the presence of a time-varying electric field.
common_errors: Omitting the displacement current term in time-varying fields.
Using the wrong sign for the displacement current term.
Confusion between conduction current (J) and displacement current (ε₀ ∂E/∂t).

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Correct Sign Convention for Displacement Current
top_down_rules.description: The displacement current term (ε₀ ∂E/∂t) must have the correct sign relative to the direction of ∂E/∂t in the coordinate system used.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that ε₀ ∂E/∂t is included with the appropriate sign based on the chosen coordinate system and Maxwell's equations. Ensure consistency with the right-hand rule for curl operations.
common_errors: Using inconsistent signs for displacement current in the curl equation.
Incorrectly applying coordinate system conventions (e.g., left-hand vs. right-hand rule).

top_down_rules.title: Verify Continuity Equation for Charge Conservation
top_down_rules.description: The displacement current ensures consistency with the continuity equation (∇·J = -∂ρ/∂t). This is crucial for charge conservation in scenarios with time-varying electric fields.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the displacement current term balances the continuity equation for a varying charge density (∇·J + ∂ρ/∂t = 0). Ensure that the inclusion of ε₀ ∂E/∂t maintains charge conservation.
common_errors: Ignoring the role of displacement current in maintaining charge conservation.
Misinterpreting the relationship between ∂ρ/∂t and ∇·J.

top_down_rules.title: Check Dimensional Consistency of Displacement Current Term
top_down_rules.description: The displacement current term ε₀ ∂E/∂t must have the same units as the conduction current density J (Amps per square meter).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that ε₀ ∂E/∂t has the correct dimensions (A/m²). Confirm that ε₀ has units of F/m, and ∂E/∂t has units of V/m·s.
common_errors: Wrong units for ε₀ or ∂E/∂t.
Inconsistent units between conduction and displacement currents.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Boundary Conditions for Displacement Current
top_down_rules.description: At the boundary between two materials, the normal component of the displacement current must be continuous if there are no free surface charges or currents.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the boundary conditions for ε₀ ∂E/∂t are applied correctly, ensuring continuity of the normal component across interfaces. Account for any discontinuities in ε₀ or ∂E/∂t due to material properties.
common_errors: Ignoring boundary conditions for displacement current at material interfaces.
Incorrect treatment of discontinuities in ε₀ or ∂E/∂t.

top_down_rules.title: Check Validity Conditions for Maxwell's Equations
top_down_rules.description: Maxwell's equations, including the displacement current, are valid in classical electrodynamics. They assume continuous fields and neglect quantum effects.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that Maxwell's equations are being applied only in conditions where classical electrodynamics is valid (e.g., no quantum or relativistic effects). Ensure that the fields are continuous and differentiable.
common_errors: Applying Maxwell's equations in quantum or microscopic domains without appropriate modifications.
Assuming fields are continuous in scenarios where they are not.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Consistency Between Faraday's Law and Displacement Current
top_down_rules.description: Faraday's Law implies that a time-varying magnetic field induces a curl in the electric field (∇ × E = -∂B/∂t). Displacement current must not violate this relationship.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the introduction of the displacement current term does not lead to inconsistencies with Faraday's Law. Ensure that ∂B/∂t and ∂E/∂t are coupled correctly in Maxwell's equations.
common_errors: Ignoring the coupling between ∂B/∂t and ∂E/∂t in Maxwell's equations.
Introducing mathematical inconsistencies between Faraday's Law and the Ampère-Maxwell Law.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Geometric Constraints on Displacement Current
top_down_rules.description: The displacement current is significant only in regions where the electric field changes with time. In regions with static fields, it must be zero.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that ε₀ ∂E/∂t is correctly set to zero in regions of static electric fields or where ∂E/∂t = 0. Ensure that the displacement current is only included in time-varying scenarios.
common_errors: Including displacement current in regions with static fields.
Failing to identify regions where ∂E/∂t = 0.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Contribution of Displacement Current to Energy Density
top_down_rules.description: The displacement current contributes to the electromagnetic energy density through the electric field. This must be consistent with the Poynting vector and energy conservation.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the displacement current term is correctly accounted for in the electromagnetic energy density (u = 1/2 ε₀E² + 1/2 μ₀B²) and the Poynting vector (S = E × H).
common_errors: Ignoring the contribution of the displacement current to energy density.
Inconsistent treatment of energy conservation involving displacement current.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Dipole Moment Calculation
top_down_rules.description: Check the calculation of the electric dipole moment, defined as the product of charge separation distance and charge magnitude for two opposite charges.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure dipole moment p = q * d, where q is the charge and d is the separation vector between charges. Verify that the direction of d points from the negative charge to the positive charge.
common_errors: Confusing dipole moment with electrical force
Incorrect vector direction for d
Incorrect charge magnitude used

top_down_rules.title: Validate Electric Field from Dipole
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the electric field due to a dipole is calculated using the correct formula for a field point and considering the dipole axis.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify E = (1/(4πϵ₀)) * (p/r³) * (2cosθ * r̂ + sinθ * θ̂), where p is the dipole moment, r is the distance from the dipole, and θ is the angle with the dipole axis. Confirm that the unit vectors r̂ and θ̂ are correctly defined in spherical coordinates.
common_errors: Ignoring angle θ in field calculation
Incorrect unit vectors usage
Using r² instead of r³

top_down_rules.title: Check Conditions for Multipole Expansion
top_down_rules.description: Multipole expansion is valid when the distance to the field point is much larger than the typical length of the charge distribution.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that r >> d, where r is the distance to the field point and d is the size of the dipole. Verify that higher-order terms are included if r is not sufficiently large.
common_errors: Applying multipole expansion for r ~ d
Ignoring higher-order terms when r is not sufficiently large

top_down_rules.title: Verify Spherical Coordinate System
top_down_rules.description: Ensure proper sign conventions and angles are used in spherical coordinates when calculating electric fields and potentials.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that θ is measured from the positive z-axis and ϕ from the positive x-axis in the xy-plane. Confirm that the coordinate system is right-handed.
common_errors: Using incorrect reference axes for θ and ϕ
Misinterpreting the angle conventions leading to incorrect field vectors
Using a left-handed coordinate system instead of right-handed

top_down_rules.title: Check Potential Energy of Dipole in Electric Field
top_down_rules.description: Ensure the calculation of potential energy of an electric dipole in a uniform electric field is correct based on U = -p · E.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify U = -p * E * cosθ, where p is the dipole moment, E is the uniform electric field strength, and θ is the angle between p and E. Confirm that the negative sign is correctly applied to indicate energy minimization.
common_errors: Using plus sign instead of minus in calculation
Incorrect angle used for calculation
Ignoring vector nature leading to scalar multiplication errors

top_down_rules.title: Check Dimensional Consistency in Dipole Calculations
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that dimensions related to electric dipole and its effects are consistent with electromagnetic principles.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all quantities have correct dimensions, e.g., dipole moment in Cm, electric field in N/C, potential energy in J. Confirm that unit conversions are correctly applied when necessary.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for dipole moment
Misaligning units for energy and field interactions
Neglecting conversion between units when necessary

top_down_rules.title: Evaluate Small Angle Approximation
top_down_rules.description: Check if small angle approximation is used correctly in the context of dipole interaction particularly for close to polar angles.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure sinθ ≈ θ and cosθ ≈ 1 for small θ in calculations involving dipole fields. Verify that the approximation is not applied for large angles.
common_errors: Using approximation incorrectly for large angles
Assuming approximation without verifying angle size
Ignoring terms that contribute when approximation limits are exceeded

top_down_rules.title: Verify Torque on Dipole in Electric Field
top_down_rules.description: Ensure the calculation of torque on an electric dipole in a uniform electric field is correct.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify τ = p × E, where τ is the torque, p is the dipole moment, and E is the electric field. Confirm that the direction of torque follows the right-hand rule.
common_errors: Incorrect cross product calculation
Ignoring vector nature of torque
Using incorrect angle between p and E

top_down_rules.title: Check Energy Stability of Dipole in Electric Field
top_down_rules.description: Ensure the stability of the dipole's orientation in an electric field is correctly analyzed based on potential energy.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the dipole aligns with the electric field to minimize potential energy (U = -p · E). Confirm that misalignment leads to restoring torque.
common_errors: Misinterpreting stable and unstable equilibrium
Ignoring restoring torque for misaligned dipoles
Incorrectly analyzing energy minimization

top_down_rules.title: Verify Electric Potential Definition
top_down_rules.description: Electric potential at a point is the work done per unit charge in bringing a positive test charge from infinity to that point without acceleration. It is defined as V = W/q, where V is the potential, W is work done, and q is the charge.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the electric potential is calculated using V = W/q, where W is the work done and q is the charge, consistently applying the unit volt (V = J/C).
common_errors: Using incorrect formula for potential
Not accounting for work done by conservative electrostatic forces only

top_down_rules.title: Verify Electric Potential Energy Formula
top_down_rules.description: Electric potential energy (U) between two point charges is U = k * q1 * q2 / r, where k is Coulomb's constant, q1 and q2 are the charges, and r is the separation distance.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure U is calculated using U = k * q1 * q2 / r correctly, verify unit consistency with joules (J), and confirm r is the correct distance.
common_errors: Incorrect distance 'r' usage
Confusing potential energy with electric potential

top_down_rules.title: Check Sign Convention in Electric Potential
top_down_rules.description: Electric potential and potential energy are positive when work is done against the electric field (e.g., bringing like charges together) and negative when work is done by the electric field.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify potential and potential energy signs correctly depending on system conditions; positive for repulsion in like charges and negative for attraction in unlike charges.
common_errors: Incorrectly assigned signs for potential and potential energy
Ignoring convention for direction of electric field forces

top_down_rules.title: Coordinate System Consistency
top_down_rules.description: Electric field vectors and calculations often use spherical or Cartesian coordinates. Consistency is crucial for calculating electric potential.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all potential and electric field calculations adhere to the chosen coordinate system and respect symmetry conditions.
common_errors: Mixing spherical and Cartesian coordinate systems
Ignoring radial symmetry in spherical coordinates

top_down_rules.title: Check Conditions for Electrostatic Equations
top_down_rules.description: Electrostatic equations apply in the absence of magnetic fields and assume charges are stationary or moving very slowly.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm all scenarios involve stationary charges or those moving sufficiently slowly; ensure no significant time-variant magnetic fields are present.
common_errors: Using electrostatic equations for high-velocity charge systems
Ignoring the influence of time-changing magnetic fields

top_down_rules.title: Verify Geometric Constraints in Charge Configurations
top_down_rules.description: Charge distributions affect electric field and potential calculations; symmetry must be considered, such as with line charges or planes of charge.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure symmetry is considered for charge distributions, correctly affecting field line orientation and potential differences.
common_errors: Neglecting symmetry in field and potential calculations
Incorrectly assuming uniform field without symmetry basis

top_down_rules.title: Dimensional and Unit Consistency
top_down_rules.description: Ensure physical quantities have correct dimensions: electric potential (V) in volts (J/C) and potential energy (U) in joules (J).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify all calculations respect dimensional consistency and correct unit conversions, maintaining J/C for electric potential and J for potential energy.
common_errors: Incorrect unit conversion between systems
Using inconsistent dimensions in equations

top_down_rules.title: Verify Reference Point in Electric Potential Calculations
top_down_rules.description: The reference point for electric potential is often taken at infinity, but it should be clearly defined for each specific problem or configuration.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the reference point for potential calculations is explicitly stated and correctly used in the computations.
common_errors: Omitting reference point definition
Assuming incorrect reference points without specification

top_down_rules.title: Verify correctness of Faraday's Law in integral form
top_down_rules.description: Faraday's Law in integral form states that the line integral of the electric field around a closed loop is equal to the negative rate of change of magnetic flux through the surface bounded by the loop: ∮E·dl = -dΦB/dt. This applies to any closed loop and surface that are geometrically consistent.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the calculated line integral of E (∮E·dl) equals -dΦB/dt, where ΦB = ∫B·dA. Check that the chosen surface matches the loop and that the time variation of B is correctly accounted for.
common_errors: Using the wrong sign for the rate of change of magnetic flux.
Incorrectly calculating the magnetic flux ΦB.
Misalignment between the loop and the chosen surface.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure correct application of Lenz's Law for induced EMF
top_down_rules.description: Lenz's Law states that the direction of the induced EMF opposes the change in magnetic flux that caused it, reflected in the negative sign in Faraday's Law.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the direction of the induced current (or EMF) is consistent with opposing the change in magnetic flux. Confirm that the calculated direction fits with the problem's coordinate system.
common_errors: Reversing the direction of induced EMF or current.
Ignoring the negative sign in Faraday's Law.
Inconsistent use of coordinate system conventions.

top_down_rules.title: Check correctness of magnetic flux calculation
top_down_rules.description: Magnetic flux (ΦB) is defined as ΦB = ∫B·dA, where B is the magnetic field and dA is the infinitesimal area vector. Ensure that the integration is correctly performed over the surface of interest.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that B and dA are properly aligned, and the dot product is computed correctly. Ensure the integration bounds match the chosen surface.
common_errors: Overlooking the angle between B and dA in the dot product.
Using incorrect integration limits for the surface.
Mixing up scalar and vector forms of magnetic flux.

top_down_rules.title: Verify induced EMF in moving conductors using v × B
top_down_rules.description: For a conductor moving through a magnetic field, the induced EMF is given by E = v × B, where v is the velocity of the conductor and B is the magnetic field.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the cross product v × B is calculated correctly. Check that the direction of the induced EMF matches the right-hand rule and is consistent with the problem's coordinate system.
common_errors: Incorrectly computing the cross product.
Using the wrong sign or direction for the velocity vector.
Failing to account for all components of the magnetic field.

top_down_rules.title: Check dimensional consistency for EMF calculations
top_down_rules.description: The induced EMF has the unit of voltage (V), equivalent to joules per coulomb (J/C). Ensure all terms in the equations for EMF result in consistent dimensions.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that both sides of the equation for EMF have consistent units. For example, ensure v × B has units of voltage (V) when applied to a conductor of length l in a magnetic field.
common_errors: Mixing up units of velocity, magnetic field, and EMF.
Failing to include the length of the conductor in motion-induced EMF problems.
Incorrectly simplifying unit expressions.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure validity conditions for Faraday's Law
top_down_rules.description: Faraday's Law is valid only in the absence of relativistic effects and in non-quantum mechanical contexts. It assumes the magnetic and electric fields are well-defined and continuous.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that the problem does not involve relativistic speeds or quantum mechanical effects. Confirm that the magnetic and electric fields are continuous and well-behaved within the region of interest.
common_errors: Applying Faraday's Law in cases involving relativistic effects.
Ignoring discontinuities in the magnetic or electric fields.

top_down_rules.title: Verify consistency of closed loop geometry
top_down_rules.description: The loop used in Faraday's Law must be a closed curve. The surface bound by the loop must be well-defined and consistent with the loop geometry.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the chosen loop is closed and that the surface for magnetic flux calculation is properly bounded by the loop.
common_errors: Using an open curve instead of a closed loop.
Mismatch between the loop and the surface geometry.

top_down_rules.title: Check time dependence of magnetic flux for induced EMF
top_down_rules.description: The induced EMF depends on the time rate of change of magnetic flux (dΦB/dt). Ensure that time dependence is correctly included in problems involving time-varying magnetic fields.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that dΦB/dt is calculated accurately by differentiating the magnetic flux concerning time. Ensure the time-dependent quantities (e.g., B(t) or the area A(t)) are properly expressed.
common_errors: Forgetting to differentiate the magnetic flux concerning time.
Omitting time dependence of the magnetic field or area.
Using incorrect expressions for time-varying quantities.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Maxwell's wave equation for electric and magnetic fields
top_down_rules.description: The electric field (E) and magnetic field (B) components of an electromagnetic wave must satisfy Maxwell's wave equation in free space: ∇²E = (1/c²)(∂²E/∂t²) and ∇²B = (1/c²)(∂²B/∂t²), where c is the speed of light in vacuum. This applies to harmonic plane waves in free space.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the second spatial derivatives of the fields (E and B) are proportional to the second time derivatives, with the proportionality constant being 1/c². Verify this for harmonic plane waves in free space.
common_errors: Not including the 1/c² factor in the wave equation.
Incorrectly applying the wave equation to non-harmonic fields.
Omitting the time-dependent component in wave analysis.

top_down_rules.title: Validate the Poynting vector calculation
top_down_rules.description: The Poynting vector (S = E × B/μ₀) represents the energy flux density of an electromagnetic wave. It should be perpendicular to both E and B and point in the direction of wave propagation. This applies to plane electromagnetic waves in free space.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the Poynting vector is calculated as the cross product of E and B. Ensure its direction aligns with the propagation direction and its magnitude corresponds to the energy flux. Confirm the division by μ₀ is correctly applied.
common_errors: Using incorrect cross-product order (e.g., B × E instead of E × B).
Forgetting the division by μ₀ for the Poynting vector magnitude.
Misidentifying the direction of wave propagation.

top_down_rules.title: Check orthogonality of E, B, and wave propagation direction
top_down_rules.description: In an electromagnetic wave, the electric field (E), magnetic field (B), and wave propagation direction (k) must be mutually perpendicular. This holds true for plane waves in homogeneous, isotropic media.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the dot products E · B, E · k, and B · k are all zero. Confirm that the cross-product relationships between E, B, and k are consistent with the right-hand rule.
common_errors: Assuming E and B are parallel instead of perpendicular.
Incorrectly identifying the propagation direction.
Failing to verify orthogonality conditions.

top_down_rules.title: Validate the speed of electromagnetic waves in a vacuum
top_down_rules.description: The speed of electromagnetic waves in a vacuum is given by c = 1/√(ε₀μ₀), where ε₀ is the permittivity and μ₀ is the permeability of free space. This is a fundamental constant of nature.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify the calculated wave speed matches c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s within reasonable tolerances. Ensure the correct values for ε₀ and μ₀ are used.
common_errors: Using incorrect values for ε₀ or μ₀.
Assuming the wave speed differs in a vacuum.
Failing to account for medium properties if not in a vacuum.

top_down_rules.title: Verify energy density expressions
top_down_rules.description: The total energy density of an electromagnetic wave is the sum of the electric field energy density (u_E = 1/2 ε₀ E²) and the magnetic field energy density (u_B = 1/2 B²/μ₀). This applies to monochromatic plane waves in free space.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that the total energy density u = u_E + u_B is used and that u_E and u_B are correctly calculated from E and B. Confirm that the energy densities are consistent with the wave's properties.
common_errors: Forgetting to square the E or B field in the energy density expressions.
Neglecting the 1/2 factor in the energy density formulas.
Incorrectly equating u_E and u_B without justification.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure dimensional consistency in wave equations
top_down_rules.description: All terms in the wave equations, energy density formulas, and Poynting vector must have consistent dimensions. For example, the Poynting vector has dimensions of power per unit area (W/m²), and energy densities have dimensions of energy per unit volume (J/m³).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify units in all equations and results. For instance, check that the Poynting vector has dimensions of W/m² and energy densities are in J/m³. Ensure that derived quantities match their expected physical dimensions.
common_errors: Mixing up the units of E and B fields.
Failing to convert units of energy density or flux correctly.
Not checking that all terms in equations have consistent dimensions.

top_down_rules.title: Check boundary conditions for electromagnetic waves
top_down_rules.description: At the interface between two media, the tangential components of E and H (H = B/μ) must be continuous, and the normal components of D (D = εE) and B must also satisfy boundary conditions based on the properties of the media.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure appropriate continuity conditions are applied at boundaries. Verify calculations for transmitted and reflected waves, ensuring they satisfy Snell's law and Fresnel equations where applicable.
common_errors: Forgetting to apply boundary conditions at interfaces.
Incorrectly matching tangential or normal components.
Neglecting the material properties (ε, μ) in boundary conditions.

top_down_rules.title: Validate polarization state of the wave
top_down_rules.description: An electromagnetic wave can be linearly, circularly, or elliptically polarized, depending on the relative phase and amplitudes of the electric field components. The polarization direction is orthogonal to the propagation direction.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify the relative phase and amplitude of electric field components to determine the polarization state. Ensure polarization direction is orthogonal to the wave vector. Confirm the phase difference is consistent with the stated polarization type.
common_errors: Confusing linear polarization with circular or elliptical.
Incorrectly identifying the polarization direction.
Neglecting the phase difference between field components.

top_down_rules.title: Verify wave impedance in free space
top_down_rules.description: The wave impedance in free space is given by Z₀ = √(μ₀/ε₀), which relates the magnitudes of the electric and magnetic fields in an electromagnetic wave.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the ratio of E to B in free space matches Z₀ ≈ 377 Ω. Verify calculations involving wave impedance are consistent with this value.
common_errors: Using incorrect values for μ₀ or ε₀.
Failing to verify the E/B ratio matches the wave impedance.
Confusing wave impedance with characteristic impedance of a medium.

experience_rules.title: 驻波边界条件量子化
experience_rules.trigger: 题目要求在有限空间（如盒、腔、管）边界处场强为零

experience_rules.trigger: 题目涉及信号乘法器（Multiplier）后接低通滤波（DC component）时
experience_rules.check_logic: 利用积化和差公式，仅当输入频率与参考频率相等（ωi = ω）时，差频项变为常数（cos(φ)），产生非零直流输出。

symbolic_hint.canonical: V_out = 0.5 * V_i0 * V_R0 * cos(phi) if omega_i == omega

experience_rules.trigger: 已知有功功率 P、电压 U 和功率因子 cosφ 求电流
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须使用 I = P / (U * cosφ) 而非 I = P / U，确保电流计算考虑了无功分量对线损的影响。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / AC Circuits (Impedance and Reactance)
experience_rules.title: 输电损耗电阻定义核验
experience_rules.trigger: 题目给出“wire resistance r”且未明确说明是“每根导线”或“单位长度”时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查公式 P_loss = I^2 * R 中 R 的取值。若无明确双线描述，应直接使用给定值 r 而非 2r，避免重复计算回路长度。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / AC Circuits (Impedance and Reactance)
experience_rules.title: 区分有效值与平均值
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及交流电（AC）充电、电解或电镀等电量累积过程时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否错误地将有效值（RMS）直接用于电量计算。电量累积 Q=I_avg*t，必须先将有效值转换为峰值，再计算半波或全波整流后的平均值。

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / Biot-Savart Law and Ampere's Law

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Biot-Savart Law and Ampere's Law
experience_rules.title: 有效电流源磁场耦合检查
experience_rules.trigger: 题目定义有效电流 J = k * B_ext 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查计算感应场 B_ind 时是否错误地重复计入产生 B_ext 的源项（如线圈匝数、原电流），防止物理量阶数冗余。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Biot-Savart Law and Ampere's Law
experience_rules.title: 磁场公式角度一致性检查
experience_rules.trigger: 计算有限或半无限长直导线产生的磁场 B 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查公式 B = (μ0*i / 4πd)*(cosθ1 + cosθ2) 中的角度定义：d 必须是点到导线所在直线的垂直距离，θ 是点与导线两端连线与导线方向的夹角。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Biot-Savart Law and Ampere's Law
experience_rules.title: 电流分布与磁场对称性匹配
experience_rules.trigger: 存在非电荷移动产生的“有效电流” J 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 识别 J 的矢量方向（如环向、径向、轴向），根据安培定律确定其产生的磁场 B_eff 方向，验证其是否能产生穿过目标回路的有效通量。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Biot-Savart Law and Ampere's Law
experience_rules.title: 三角恒等式目标导向校验
experience_rules.trigger: 已知结果包含 tan(α/2) 或 cot(α/2) 等半角形式时
experience_rules.check_logic: 若中间过程出现 (1±cosα)/sinα 结构，应优先识别为半角公式 tan(α/2) 或 cot(α/2)，而非强行展开为 sinα/cosα。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Capacitance and Dielectrics
experience_rules.title: 电力耦合临界失稳判定
experience_rules.trigger: 出现弹性薄膜/弹簧与平行板电容器电荷/电压耦合，且提及‘临界值’或‘失稳’时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否应用了静电引力 F=Q^2/(2εA) 与弹性力 F=kΔx 的平衡，并确认是否识别出位移达到间隙 1/3 时的失稳特性。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Capacitance and Dielectrics
experience_rules.title: 静电常数与介电常数转换校验
experience_rules.trigger: 题目给出静电常数 k 而非介电常数 ε₀ 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查电容公式是否正确使用了 C = A / (4πkd) 形式，避免直接将 k 替换 ε₀ 导致 4π 系数丢失。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Capacitance and Dielectrics
experience_rules.title: 多层平行板电容层数判定
experience_rules.trigger: 出现 N 片动片与 N+1 片定片交错排列时
experience_rules.check_logic: 总电容层数（有效电场区域）应为 2N，而非 N 或 N+1。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Capacitance and Dielectrics
experience_rules.title: 功与势能转化一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 题目要求计算‘泵’或‘外力’做的功，且系统包含电场能与弹性势能时
experience_rules.check_logic: 核实功是否等于系统总势能的增量 ΔE = ΔU_spring + ΔU_elec，特别注意电荷注入过程中的能量积分。

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / Coulomb's Law and Electric Fields

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Coulomb's Law and Electric Fields
experience_rules.title: 积分区间与奇异点一致性检查
experience_rules.trigger: 计算连续分布电荷在直线延伸方向的场强，且场点距离r > 半长度l时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查积分变量x的取值范围[a, b]是否包含分母为零的点r。若r在区间外，严禁拆分积分并在r处取极限。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Coulomb's Law and Electric Fields
experience_rules.title: 非对称场点矢量分量补全规则
experience_rules.trigger: 场点不在带电体对称轴或对称中心上时（如导线端点垂面）
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须分别计算垂直分量E_perp和平行分量E_parallel，严禁直接假设场强沿径向或轴向。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Coulomb's Law and Electric Fields
experience_rules.title: 内心对称性场强判定
experience_rules.trigger: 多边形/三角形各边电荷密度相等，且求解目标点为内心（Incenter）
experience_rules.check_logic: 内心到各边距离相等，均匀带电边在内心产生的场强方向必垂直于边指向内心。若各边贡献的场强幅值相等且矢量闭合（如正多边形或三角形内心），则合场强为零。

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / Current, Resistance, and Ohm's Law

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Current, Resistance, and Ohm's Law
experience_rules.title: 超导电流稳定性建模
experience_rules.trigger: 题目涉及超导线圈、电流变化率（或不变量）及时间跨度
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须使用RL回路方程 L(dI/dt) + RI = 0，结合电流变化精度 ΔI/I ≈ (R/L)Δt 进行电阻率上限估算。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Current, Resistance, and Ohm's Law
experience_rules.title: 孤立导体电阻极限检查
experience_rules.trigger: 当题目涉及双电极系统且其中一个边界趋于无穷远时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查电阻表达式在b→∞时是否收敛于有限值（如球对称下的ρ/4πa），而非发散，这符合孤立导体接地电阻的物理特性。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Current, Resistance, and Ohm's Law
experience_rules.title: 微观参数关联检查
experience_rules.trigger: 已知条件包含电子数密度n、质量m、电荷e但未直接给出几何尺寸
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否需要利用惯性电感（Kinetic Inductance）概念，即 L_k ∝ m/(n*e^2) 来抵消几何参数或构建电阻率表达式。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Current, Resistance, and Ohm's Law
experience_rules.title: 级联放大系统总功耗建模
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及多级放大（如倍增管、多级电路）且每级有增益和电压差时
experience_rules.check_logic: 总功耗应为各级功耗之和 Σ(N_i * e * V_i)，其中 N_i 随级数 i 按几何级数增长，不能简单取单级能耗或平均值。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Current, Resistance, and Ohm's Law
experience_rules.title: 几何级数求和项缺失检查
experience_rules.trigger: 出现 'n dynodes' 或 'n stages' 且存在增益因子 δσ > 1 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查最终表达式是否包含 (δσ)^n 项及其求和后的分母 (δσ - 1) 的高阶形式，若结果仅为 n 的线性函数则必错。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Current, Resistance, and Ohm's Law
experience_rules.title: 区分结构尺寸与间距参数
experience_rules.trigger: 题目同时给出物体高度h、直径δ及间距表达式L=αh时
experience_rules.check_logic: 核实电阻计算公式R=ρl/A中的l是否对应电流流经的物理长度（通常为跨度h），而非分布间距L。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Current, Resistance, and Ohm's Law
experience_rules.title: 连续介质电阻积分法
experience_rules.trigger: 计算具有特定几何对称性（球、柱）且填充均匀电阻率介质的电阻时
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证是否通过电流密度J=I/A(r)推导电场E=ρJ，再对E进行路径积分得到电势差V，最后由R=V/I求解。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Current, Resistance, and Ohm's Law
experience_rules.title: 电阻定义路径校验法
experience_rules.trigger: 计算形状复杂的导体电阻（如圆环、薄壳）时
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须明确电流流向。若电流沿周长流动，则L=2πr，A=宽度×厚度；若电流沿轴向流动，则L=高度，A=环形截面积。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Current, Resistance, and Ohm's Law
experience_rules.title: 电导率与电阻率量纲辨析
experience_rules.trigger: 题目给出σ（电导率）或要求电阻表达式包含σ时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查公式是否满足 R = L / (σ * A)。若σ出现在分子位置且无其他倒数项，则必然存在逻辑错误。

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / DC Circuits and Kirchhoff's Laws

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / DC Circuits and Kirchhoff's Laws
experience_rules.title: 电压表测量对象判定准则
experience_rules.trigger: 题目描述“电压表通过变阻器连接到电池组”或类似串并联混淆表述时
experience_rules.check_logic: 确认电压表是测量路端电压 U=E-Ir 还是测量特定电阻电压 U=IR。若计算出电阻为负，必为测量对象判定错误。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / DC Circuits and Kirchhoff's Laws
experience_rules.title: 理想电表等效建模准则
experience_rules.trigger: 题目出现“ideal ammeter”或“ideal voltmeter”连接特定节点时
experience_rules.check_logic: 理想电流表应视为短路（导线），理想电压表应视为断路。必须重新绘制等效电路图，确认节点电势变化，而非直接套用原网络阻值。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / DC Circuits and Kirchhoff's Laws
experience_rules.title: 对称性分析边界检查
experience_rules.trigger: 使用“Due to symmetry”或“symmetric network”简化计算时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查电流分配比例是否满足 KCL。若最终结果不含网络拓扑常数（如本题的1/9），需警惕是否过度简化为 1:1 分流。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / DC Circuits and Kirchhoff's Laws
experience_rules.title: RC电路稳态节点电势判定
experience_rules.trigger: 题目包含电阻、电容混合网络且要求求解“stabilized potentials”时
experience_rules.check_logic: 禁止直接剔除电容支路。需建立节点电荷守恒方程：对孤立节点，所有相连电容的电荷代数和为初始值（通常为0），即 Σ C_i * (V_node - V_neighbor_i) = 0。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / DC Circuits and Kirchhoff's Laws
experience_rules.title: 电压表读数变化语义判定
experience_rules.trigger: 题目描述‘电压表读数增加n倍’或‘增加到n倍’
experience_rules.check_logic: 需区分‘增加n倍’(V2=V1+n*V1)与‘增加到n倍’(V2=n*V1)。若计算出现负电阻，优先检查此语义转化及电压表是否测量路端电压。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / DC Circuits and Kirchhoff's Laws
experience_rules.title: 路端电压单调性校验
experience_rules.trigger: 外电路电阻R减小时
experience_rules.check_logic: 根据闭合电路欧姆定律，外电阻R减小时，总电流I增大，内电压Ir增大，路端电压U=E-Ir必减小。若模型推导出U增大，则建模必错。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / DC Circuits and Kirchhoff's Laws
experience_rules.title: 变化倍数语义解析校验
experience_rules.trigger: 出现“增加n倍” (increases by n times) 与“增加到n倍” (increases to n times) 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 严格区分 V2 = V1 * (1+n) 与 V2 = n * V1。本题中“increases by 1 time”应解析为 V2 = 2*V1。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / DC Circuits and Kirchhoff's Laws
experience_rules.title: 区分直流稳态下的电流与电势
experience_rules.trigger: 出现“capacitors act as open circuits”或“no current flows”表述时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否因“无电流”推导出“无电势差”或“支路无效”。无电流仅意味着电阻两端等电势，电容两端仍可存在电势差。

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / Displacement Current and Its Role in Maxwell's Equations

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Displacement Current and Its Role in Maxwell's Equations
experience_rules.title: 能流积分守恒校验
experience_rules.trigger: 要求计算“total electromagnetic energy that flows out”
experience_rules.check_logic: 需通过坡印廷矢量 (S = E x H) 在电容器侧面进行时间与面积的双重积分，检查最终能量是否与静电能改变量 (1/2 * Q^2/C) 保持量纲一致及系数合理性。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Displacement Current and Its Role in Maxwell's Equations
experience_rules.title: 非均匀介质磁场校验
experience_rules.trigger: 题目提及“metal ring”、“outside the ring”或特定几何约束下的电容器充放电
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否直接套用平行板电容器均匀场公式；若存在环状结构，需根据边界条件重新积分电流密度或位移电流密度，而非简单代入 E=V/d。

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Dipoles and Multipole Expansion

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Dipoles and Multipole Expansion
experience_rules.title: 极化率与偶极矩相位对齐
experience_rules.trigger: 出现诱导偶极矩 p = alpha * E 且 E 为简谐场时
experience_rules.check_logic: 需区分瞬时极化率与复极化率。若 alpha 为实数常量，则 p 与 E 必须同相；若存在阻尼导致相位差，alpha 应体现为复数模长。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Dipoles and Multipole Expansion
experience_rules.title: 光强与场强平方转换系数校验
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及光强 I 与电场幅值 E0 的能量转换或势能计算时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查公式 I = 1/2 * ε0 * c * E0^2 的代入过程，特别是在计算时间平均势能 <U> = -1/2 * p * E 时，注意 1/2 因子是否重复计算或遗漏。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Dipoles and Multipole Expansion
experience_rules.title: 受迫振动振幅一致性检查
experience_rules.trigger: 处理带有阻尼项的二阶常微分方程（如电子云受迫振动）时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查振幅项是否满足 x0 = F0 / (m * sqrt((w0^2 - w^2)^2 + (gamma*w)^2))，若分母无根号或平方项缺失则必错。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Dipoles and Multipole Expansion
experience_rules.title: 偶极子场动力学建模完备性检查
experience_rules.trigger: 题目涉及点电荷在偶极子（Dipole）场中运动且要求具体速度分量时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否代入了偶极子电势 V ∝ (cos θ / r²) 或电场强度分量，而非仅保留抽象势能符号 U(r, θ)。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Dipoles and Multipole Expansion
experience_rules.title: 坐标系分量投影一致性检查
experience_rules.trigger: 在矢量场分解（如En, Eτ）与标准坐标系（如Er, Eθ）转换时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查定义的Normal/Tangential方向是否与Radial/Polar方向对齐，防止三角函数名（sin/cos）因基向量定义错误而互换。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Dipoles and Multipole Expansion
experience_rules.title: 非中心力场分量求解逻辑
experience_rules.trigger: 当系统明确指出角动量不守恒（angular momentum is not conserved）时
experience_rules.check_logic: 需寻找除能量外的第二守恒量或运动常数（如广义角动量修正项），不能仅靠能量守恒方程解出两个独立速度分量。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Dipoles and Multipole Expansion
experience_rules.title: 偶极子电势符号校验
experience_rules.trigger: 计算电偶极子在远处的电势 φ 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 需严格核实偶极矩矢量 p (从负到正) 与观测点位矢 r 的夹角 θ。若 p 与 r 同向，电势为正；若反向，电势为负。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Dipoles and Multipole Expansion
experience_rules.title: 偶极子场极坐标分量校验
experience_rules.trigger: 计算电偶极子在极坐标(r, θ)下的场强分量时
experience_rules.check_logic: 需确保径向分量Er正比于2cosθ，极角分量Eθ正比于sinθ，且两者系数比例为2:1。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Dipoles and Multipole Expansion
experience_rules.title: 周期平均余弦乘积项系数检查
experience_rules.trigger: 计算 <cos(wt) * cos(wt + phi)> 等时间平均物理量时
experience_rules.check_logic: 确认积化和差后的常数项 1/2 * cos(phi) 是否正确保留，并与势能定义中的系数（如 -1/2）正确相乘。

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 优先使用题目给定模型而非外部经验常数
experience_rules.trigger: 题目提供“simplified curve”、“idealized model”或特定函数图像时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查解题步骤是否提取了图像的几何特征（如面积、斜率）或模型参数，禁止在有明确模型时引入外部经验数值（如典型闪电电流）。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 镜像法能量减半规则
experience_rules.trigger: 计算点电荷与接地导体平面（或导体球）之间的相互作用能或移动做功时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否直接套用两点电荷公式。正确能量应为对应两点电荷系统能量的一半，因为导体感应电荷建立的场是随原电荷移动而变化的。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 壳层内外场强电势突变检查
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及均匀带电球壳或球面对点电荷的功与能问题
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证是否正确应用壳内场强为零（等势体）及壳外等效为点电荷的性质，确保进入壳内后速度恒定。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 均匀带电体中心场强线性律
experience_rules.trigger: 均匀带电对称几何体（立方体、球体）中心附近的微小振动
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否应用 E = (ρ/3ε0)r 的局部等效性。对于立方体中心，由高斯定理微分形式 ∇·E = ρ/ε0 及对称性可知 Ex = (ρ/3ε0)x。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 简谐运动周期量纲一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 求解小位移振动周期 T
experience_rules.check_logic: 核实周期公式是否满足 T = 2π√(m/k) 形式，其中 k 为回复力系数（F=-kx）。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 非守恒量求解完备性检查
experience_rules.trigger: 题目明确指出“角动量不守恒”但要求求解速度分量时
experience_rules.check_logic: 禁止直接假设径向速度为零或保留导数项。必须寻找替代的守恒量（如能量）或对力矩方程进行时间积分以建立速度分量间的代数关系。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 离散与连续电荷分布功的极限一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 当分批次数n趋于无穷大时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查离散求和结果的极限是否等于连续积分结果（即电容器储能增量形式）。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 量级估算题需严格对齐已知约束条件
experience_rules.trigger: 题目要求“estimate of an order of magnitude”并给出多个物理常量时
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证是否所有给出的已知量（如h, E0, N_people）都参与了计算链条，漏用关键约束通常导致量级偏差。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 电势叠加原理一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 多个带电体处于对称几何位置且分步充电
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证电荷计算是否满足 V = Σ(k*q_i/r_i) 的线性叠加，而非简单认为各步电荷独立。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 临界穿越条件能量守恒验证
experience_rules.trigger: 电荷从无穷远运动至带同号电荷的有限分布区域
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查临界条件是否满足初动能大于等于电势能峰值（通常在边界处），防止忽略势垒导致建模错误。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 泰勒展开阶数匹配规则
experience_rules.trigger: 题目要求计算至“最低阶非零项（lowest non-zero power）”且涉及小量近似时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查最终表达式是否包含了除常数项外第一个含变量的幂次项。若常数项为零，则取第一项；若常数项非零，则需保留至第一个含参项。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 区分相互作用能与外场能
experience_rules.trigger: 题目要求计算“移动电荷做的功”或“系统的静电能”
experience_rules.check_logic: 若场源包含感应电荷（非固定电荷分布），必须通过积分库仑力或使用能量密度积分，不能简单使用 U=qV，除非 V 是恒定外场。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 等势连接递推规则
experience_rules.trigger: 物体依次与恒定电势源连接
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否考虑了已带电物体对当前连接物体电势的叠加贡献，通常电荷量呈等比数列关系。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 电偶极子势能幂次校验
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及点电荷在远距离电偶极子场中的运动或能量分析时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查势能 U 是否正比于 r⁻²，电场 E 是否正比于 r⁻³。若出现 r⁻³ 的势能项通常意味着量纲错误或模型误用。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 分批搬运电荷功累加规则
experience_rules.trigger: 题目涉及将电荷q分为n份逐一移向带电体Q时
experience_rules.check_logic: 需考虑第i次搬运时，目标体电荷已变为Q+(i-1)q/n，总功应为各步功之和而非单次功的n倍。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electric Potential and Potential Energy
experience_rules.title: 复合函数近似展开顺序
experience_rules.trigger: 处理分式形式的根号近似，如 1/sqrt(R^2+z^2) 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 优先提取主导项使括号内变为 (1+x)^n 形式，再依次应用幂级数展开，避免在分母位置直接保留复杂多项式导致计算冗余。

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 动生与感生电动势叠加检查
experience_rules.trigger: 当磁感应强度 B(t) 随时间变化且回路面积 A(t) 随运动变化时
experience_rules.check_logic: 需检查 dΦ/dt = (dB/dt)A + B(dA/dt) 两项的符号。若磁场减弱 (dB/dt < 0) 且面积增大 (dA/dt > 0)，两项对电动势的贡献可能抵消或叠加，需结合楞次定律校验总电流方向。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: RL回路感应电流稳态分析
experience_rules.trigger: 题目涉及互感电动势驱动含有自感L和电阻R的闭合回路时
experience_rules.check_logic: 电流必须满足 L(di/dt) + Ri = -M(dI_source/dt)。稳态解应包含阻抗模分母 √(R² + ω²L²) 及相位偏移。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 电磁轨道加速动态平衡检查
experience_rules.trigger: 题目涉及导体棒在恒定电压源驱动下的磁场运动
