experience_rules.check_logic: 必须检查电流表达式是否包含动生电动势项 (V - BLv)/R，而非仅使用 Ohm 定律静态形式 V/R。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 旋转回路感应电流平均场校验
experience_rules.trigger: 闭合回路在恒定磁场中旋转并求解中心磁场偏转
experience_rules.check_logic: 需区分瞬时电动势与等效直流电流。中心磁场贡献需对周期内电流产生的磁场分量进行时间平均积分，而非直接代入峰值或恒定值。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 变力运动方程解构校验
experience_rules.trigger: 加速度表达式中包含速度变量 v 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 禁止直接套用匀变速直线运动公式，需通过微分方程 dv/dt = f(v) 求解速度与位移函数。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 相位差定义域一致性检查
experience_rules.trigger: 要求计算两个正弦量（如原副线圈电流）的相位差 tan δ 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 需明确 δ 是相对于驱动源还是感应电动势。若定义为电流间相位差，需结合法拉第定律的 -π/2 偏移与 RL 电路的阻抗角进行矢量合成。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 安培力平衡条件动态一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 题目要求“维持匀速直线运动”且磁场随时间变化时
experience_rules.check_logic: 外力 F 必须实时等于安培力 F_B(t) = B(t)I(t)L。需验证 F 是否为时间的函数，而非仅计算 t=0 时刻的瞬时值。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 旋转框架感应电流对称性校验
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及对称几何框架（如立方体、正方形）在匀强磁场中绕轴旋转
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查各支路电流是否满足基尔霍夫电流定律（KCL）及电势降闭合性，不能简单假设各边电流独立且仅由自身切割产生。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 磁通量投影角度校验
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及平面线圈在匀强磁场中转动计算磁通量时
experience_rules.check_logic: 核实磁场矢量与线圈平面法矢量的夹角。若磁场垂直向上且线圈水平，夹角为0或π，磁通量取极值而非零。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 旋转切割电动势结构检查
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及半径为 a、角速度为 ω 的圆盘在匀强磁场中旋转切割时
experience_rules.check_logic: 感应电动势的标准形式应比例于 (1/2) * B * ω * a²，需核对系数 1/2 及长度的平方项。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 积分限与边长符号匹配检查
experience_rules.trigger: 计算矩形区域通量且涉及对数项 ln((L+d)/d) 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 核实积分方向对应的边长（即垂直于电流方向的宽度）是否作为对数分子中的增量，而平行于电流的边长作为系数。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 磁势场边界条件一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及薄层导体（Thin film）与移动磁源的相互作用。
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证镜像电荷/磁荷的符号与位置是否满足边界处的连续性或消隐条件。导体薄层通常产生随时间演化的“拖尾”镜像分布。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 区分体扩散与薄层响应模型
experience_rules.trigger: 题目强调厚度 d 极小（thin film）且忽略位移电流时
experience_rules.check_logic: 不应直接套用三维扩散方程，而应通过跨越薄层的磁场跳变条件（边界条件）建立演化方程。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 无限大薄导体层感应场平移律
experience_rules.trigger: 出现“conducting thin film”、“h >> d”且涉及源点突变或移动时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查感应磁场是否满足 B(r, t) = B_image(r + v*t*n) 的形式，其中 v 与薄层电阻率成正比。

symbolic_hint.canonical: B_{ind}(\rho, z, t) = f(\rho, z + v_0 t)

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 断路状态动力学判定
experience_rules.trigger: 题目出现‘disconnected’、‘open circuit’或‘断开’等描述导体回路时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否错误计算了安培力或电磁力矩。若回路断开，感应电流为零，安培力项必须为零，运动仅受重力、弹力等机械力驱动。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 磁通量变化率余弦项校验
experience_rules.trigger: 出现 'rotating around axis' 与 'constant magnetic field'
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查电动势是否表达为 dΦ/dt = B*S*ω*sin(ωt)。若直接使用 vBL 且未处理有效切割长度，通常会导致系数错误。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 螺线管参数量纲校验
experience_rules.trigger: 题目同时给出总匝数 N 和长度 l 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 磁感应强度公式应使用 B = μ₀(N/l)i 而非 B = μ₀Ni，需检查最终表达式中 N 与 l 的组合是否满足 [N/L] 量纲。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 动态镜像法积分触发
experience_rules.trigger: 题目给出含时间参数的复杂分式积分公式，且涉及源点匀速运动。
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否将离散求和极限化为时间积分。若存在 $x+vt$ 或 $z+v_0t$ 结构，应优先构造积分模型而非离散镜像点叠加。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 动生电动势投影分量完整性
experience_rules.trigger: 计算旋转导线切割磁感线产生的电动势
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须使用 E = ∫(v × B) · dl，确认速度矢量、磁感应强度矢量与导线矢量三者的空间几何关系，通常涉及 sinθ 与 cosθ 的组合。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
experience_rules.title: 理想导体表面磁通量判定
experience_rules.trigger: 题目提及“perfect conductor”或“conducting thin film”且要求计算穿过其表面的磁通量
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否应用了边界条件 B·n = 0。若表面与导体边界重合，则该面磁通量恒为0。

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Waves and Energy Transport

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Waves and Energy Transport
experience_rules.title: 电磁场动量与能量流密度转换一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 要求推导电磁波体动量密度 p_V 与坡印廷矢量 S 的关系时
experience_rules.check_logic: 核实是否满足 p_V = S / c^2。若使用介质参数，需检查是否满足 p_V = epsilon_0 * (E x B) 的等价性。

symbolic_hint.canonical: p_V = S / c^2 = epsilon_0 * (E x B)

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Waves and Energy Transport
experience_rules.title: 雷达探测深度常识校验
experience_rules.trigger: 计算地质雷达（GPR）或电磁波地下探测深度时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查结果量级。若计算出的探测深度（1/α）处于微米（μm）量级，通常意味着将高频趋肤效应公式误用或计算项倒置。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electromagnetic Waves and Energy Transport
experience_rules.title: 有损介质波传播近似校验
experience_rules.trigger: 题目给出 (σ/ωε)² << 1 或低损耗介质条件时
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证α与β的近似关系：α ≈ (σ/2) * sqrt(μ/ε)，β ≈ ω * sqrt(με)。需注意σ在分子位置而非分母。

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / Electrostatics in Conductors and Insulators

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electrostatics in Conductors and Insulators
experience_rules.title: 多板静电平衡电荷分配
experience_rules.trigger: 出现“多个平行带电板”、“接触/碰撞”、“电荷重新分布”时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否仅对接触两板求和平分；必须考虑其余固定带电体在接触点产生的背景电场，确保接触两板外侧电场强度相等或满足电势相等方程。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electrostatics in Conductors and Insulators
experience_rules.title: 静电压力法求合力
experience_rules.trigger: 求解带电导体受到的静电斥力或维持平衡所需的最小外力
experience_rules.check_logic: 利用静电压力 P = σ²/(2ε₀) 对有效投影面积进行积分，而非直接对全表面积积分。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electrostatics in Conductors and Insulators
experience_rules.title: 空腔导体球心电势叠加准则
experience_rules.trigger: 计算含有内点电荷的空腔导体球心电势时
experience_rules.check_logic: 球心总电势 = 点电荷产生的电势 (kQ/r) + 导体壳内壁感应电荷产生的电势 (k(-Q)/R1) + 导体壳外表面电荷产生的电势 (k(Q+q)/R2)。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electrostatics in Conductors and Insulators
experience_rules.title: 库仑常数与介电常数转换
experience_rules.trigger: 答案选项包含 k 或 ε₀ 但计算过程中使用了另一种常数
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否满足 k = 1 / (4πε₀) 的代换关系，确保数值与量纲一致。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electrostatics in Conductors and Insulators
experience_rules.title: 孤立系统电荷守恒校验
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及电荷转移、中和或重新分布的过程
experience_rules.check_logic: 核实参与电荷交换的子系统（如板β和γ）的总电荷在交换前后是否保持恒定，防止在建模初期遗漏初始电荷项。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Electrostatics in Conductors and Insulators
experience_rules.title: 导体壳电荷守恒与等势体判定
experience_rules.trigger: 题目给出导体壳净电荷 q 且内部有电荷 Q 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 确认外表面电荷量为 Q+q。导体壳内部（含空腔壁）电势由外表面电荷在球心产生的电势 k(Q+q)/R2 统一贡献基准值。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Gauss's Law and Applications
experience_rules.title: 地表电场对称性选择
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及地球表面（R >> h）的静电场计算时
experience_rules.check_logic: 优先采用无限大带电平面模型（一维坐标系），严禁引入与高度无关的水平向径向通量计算。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Gauss's Law and Applications
experience_rules.title: 一维高斯定理梯度关联律
experience_rules.trigger: 题目给出不同高度/位置的电场强度并要求求解体电荷密度时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否利用高斯定理的微分形式 ρ = ε₀ * (dE/dz) 或积分形式 ΔE * A = Q/ε₀，而非单一位置电场值。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Gauss's Law and Applications
experience_rules.title: 实体边界场强分段检查
experience_rules.trigger: 计算具有物理半径（如 r0, R）的带电体产生的电场时
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须明确区分区域（r < R 与 r > R）。对于导体，内部场强应显式标注为 0，除非题目另有说明。

symbolic_hint.canonical: E(r) = { f(r) for r >= r0; 0 for r < r0 }

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Gauss's Law and Applications
experience_rules.title: 高斯面选取与通量简化
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及无限长直线、无限大平面或球对称电荷分布求场强时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查所选高斯面是否与场强矢量处处垂直或平行，确保积分项可简化为标量乘积 E*A。

symbolic_hint.canonical: E * (2 * pi * r * L) = (lambda * L) / epsilon_0

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / Lenz's Law and Eddy Currents

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Lenz's Law and Eddy Currents
experience_rules.title: 涡流磁矩厚度依赖性
experience_rules.trigger: 计算薄壳（thickness D）在变化磁场中的感应电流或磁矩时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查最终表达式是否包含厚度D的一次项。对于薄壳模型，总电流正比于横截面积，即正比于D。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Lenz's Law and Eddy Currents
experience_rules.title: 导体薄膜涡流特征速度判定
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及磁偶极子在薄层导体（thin film）上方运动并产生阻尼/悬浮力时
experience_rules.check_logic: 需区分扩散极限（低速）与镜像极限（高速）。特征速度 v0 通常由扩散常数决定（v0 = 2/(μ0σd)），不应随运动速度 v 变化。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Lenz's Law and Eddy Currents
experience_rules.title: 趋肤效应临界速度判定
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及运动磁源在导体薄膜上方感应涡流且提及趋肤深度与厚度关系时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否建立 $\delta = d$ 的等式，并利用特征频率 $\omega \approx v/h$ 将扩散方程转化为速度相关的代数方程。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Lenz's Law and Eddy Currents
experience_rules.title: 矢量投影完整性校验
experience_rules.trigger: 题目要求提供xyz投影且涉及矢量变化率（如B_dot）与主轴夹角时
experience_rules.check_logic: 禁止预设变化率沿单一坐标轴。必须保留夹角参数（如sin alpha, cos alpha）并映射至指定坐标系。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Lenz's Law and Eddy Currents
experience_rules.title: 物理常数与变量函数关系审计
experience_rules.trigger: 题目要求求解某个带有 'characteristic'（特征）前缀的物理量时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查该量是否被错误地表达为输入自变量的函数。特征量通常由系统内禀参数（如电导率、厚度、高度）决定。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Lenz's Law and Eddy Currents
experience_rules.title: 电磁感应特征频率估算
experience_rules.trigger: 匀速运动源产生的时变磁场问题
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证是否使用 $\omega \sim v/L$（L为特征距离，如高度h）作为等效角频率来处理准静态近似下的色散或趋肤问题。

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Dipoles and Magnetic Materials

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Dipoles and Magnetic Materials
experience_rules.title: 磁偶极子模型极性校验
experience_rules.trigger: 题目涉及两个磁单极子（magnetic monopoles）构成的系统或磁场计算时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否默认磁单极子电荷量 qm 异号（一南一北）。若题目未明确同号，通常应按偶极子模型处理，磁场贡献应为矢量差而非简单标量和。

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 磁输运稳态分量方程校验
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及洛伦兹力、电场力与线性阻力（-mv/τ）的2D稳态平衡时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查x/y分量方程是否满足耦合形式：vx = (eτ/m)Ex - ωτvy 且 vy = (eτ/m)Ey + ωτvx，注意电荷符号。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 等效电流与频率关系校验
experience_rules.trigger: 将圆周运动电荷等效为环形电流时
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证电流 $I = qf = q\frac{\omega}{2\pi}$，注意电子电荷 $q=-e$ 在计算电流大小时取绝对值，但在矢量运算中保留符号。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 复杂几何磁场建模校验
experience_rules.trigger: 题目给出托卡马克/环形腔（Toroidal）且包含多个几何参数（R0, r0, alpha0）时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否直接套用简单柱坐标磁场。若方程中缺失题目给定的特征常数（如alpha0），则物理建模必然缺失分量。

symbolic_hint.canonical: F = q(v x B) -> m*a_i = sum(q*v_j*B_k)

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 量纲一致性预判
experience_rules.trigger: 答案选项或目标表达式包含物理常数（如k, B, m, e）时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查推导过程是否引入了所有必要的物理常数；若题目涉及电荷间距不变，缺失静电力常数k必然导致量纲错误。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 分量周期等效性校验
experience_rules.trigger: 题目描述特定速度分量（如 vx, vy）的周期性变化时
experience_rules.check_logic: 在匀强磁场中，速度矢量在垂直磁场平面内的投影做匀速圆周运动，其任一正交分量的振荡周期等于整体回旋周期。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 飞行时间质谱空间聚焦建模
experience_rules.trigger: 出现“generated at different positions... arrive as simultaneously as possible”或“minimize influence of ΔS”
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须建立总飞行时间 T 关于初始位置变量 s 的函数，并令其一阶导数 dT/ds = 0 以求解结构参数。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 相对论束缚角与时间尺度一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及辐射锥角 theta ~ 1/gamma 的扫掠过程
experience_rules.check_logic: 区分粒子转过锥角的时间 dt_emit 与观测者接收时间 dt_obs，两者满足 dt_obs = dt_emit * (1 - beta cos(theta))

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 区分定义式与平衡态解
experience_rules.trigger: 题目在给出物理量定义（Recall that...）后询问该物理量表达式
experience_rules.check_logic: 优先检查是否只需返回该物理量的基本定义式，而非通过受力平衡或动力学方程求解具体数值。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 磁场垂直进出几何约束
experience_rules.trigger: 粒子垂直进入并垂直离开矩形磁场区域，且给出进出口间距 l
experience_rules.check_logic: 此时粒子在磁场中转过 90 度，进出口间距 l 为圆弧弦长，满足 l = sqrt(2) * r，而非直径或弧长。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 直线电流场距离建模校验
experience_rules.trigger: 题目涉及“长直导线”与“圆周运动”且给定导线到圆心距离 d 和半径 R 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查粒子到导线的距离是否被错误地处理为到圆心的距离或点对点距离。正确距离应为 d 与 R 在垂直导线方向投影的代数和。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 阻力项符号一致性检查
experience_rules.trigger: 公式中同时出现主动力（电磁力）与耗散力（阻力）时
experience_rules.check_logic: 确保阻力项（-mv/τ）在移项至等号另一侧时，其符号必须与速度方向相反，避免出现速度无限增加的非物理结果。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 质谱仪基本方程一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及电场加速后进入匀强磁场偏转的动力学问题
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否满足 M = (q * B^2 * r^2) / (2 * U)，其中 r 需根据题目几何条件（如本题的 l）进行代换。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 多带电粒子约束运动建模
experience_rules.trigger: 出现“distance between two charged particles remains constant”或类似距离约束表述时
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须同时计入外场力（如磁场洛伦兹力）和粒子间相互作用力（库仑力），并利用相对速度在连线方向分量为零的条件。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 磁力线参数化代换
experience_rules.trigger: 题目给出 r = r_Eq cos² λ 且定义 L = r_Eq / R_E 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查 r 是否正确替换为 L * R_E * cos² λ，并注意在 B ∝ r⁻³ 中代入后产生的 cos⁶ λ 分母项

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 磁路节点磁通守恒律
experience_rules.trigger: 题目涉及高磁导率材料连接件（如球、接头）与磁体组成的闭合结构时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否应用了类比基尔霍夫电流定律（KCL）的磁通平衡，即进入节点的磁通等于离开节点的磁通，而非简单加总。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 多级场运动顺序一致性检查
experience_rules.trigger: 题目描述包含多个电场区域（E1, E2...）及漂移区（Drift Region/L）
experience_rules.check_logic: 核对物理过程顺序：通常为 [电离/加速] -> [加速] -> [漂移] -> [探测]，严禁随意调换漂移区与加速区的先后位置。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 回旋运动磁矩方向判定
experience_rules.trigger: 计算带电粒子在磁场中圆周运动产生的等效磁矩时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查磁矩方向是否满足 $\vec{\mu} = -\frac{E_{k\perp}}{B^2}\vec{B}$，即无论电荷正负，其轨道磁矩总是削弱原磁场（抗磁性）。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 区分宏观感应与微观粒子收集建模
experience_rules.trigger: 题目描述卫星在等离子体环境中运动并‘收集’(collect) 离子/电子产生电流时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否使用了微观电流公式 I = n*e*v*S 而非简单的闭合回路欧姆定律 I = E/R。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 运动方程分量耦合检查
experience_rules.trigger: 在正交坐标系（r, phi, z）下求解洛伦兹力运动方程
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证每个坐标轴的加速度项是否完整包含了向心力/科氏力项（如 r*phi_dot^2）以及磁场所有分量产生的交叉乘积项。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 同步辐射脉冲宽度压缩律
experience_rules.trigger: 计算超相对论粒子（gamma >> 1）在磁场中产生的同步辐射脉冲持续时间
experience_rules.check_logic: 脉冲宽度应包含几何扫掠时间 (1/gamma / omega) 与多普勒压缩因子 (1/gamma^2) 的乘积效应，最终量级应正比于 1/(gamma^2 * omega_c)

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 磁场中荷电系统动量修正校验
experience_rules.trigger: 题目要求在均匀磁场B中求解系统的“修正动量”或“广义动量”守恒量时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查公式是否满足 d/dt(M*v_CM) = F_ext = (Σq_i*v_i) x B 的积分形式，确保电荷分布项（如 q*l）与磁场的叉乘系数与运动方程一致。

symbolic_hint.canonical: P = M*v_CM - Σ(q_i * r_i x B)

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 磁单极子镜像法对称性校验
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及磁单极子（Monopole）在无限大平面导体/薄膜附近的场强计算
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查镜像电荷的极性与位置。对于理想导磁或特定边界，镜像点应位于 z=-h，且总场应满足边界处的法向或切向连续性条件。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 洛伦兹力充当向心力条件校验
experience_rules.trigger: 出现“centripetal force equals the force exerted by the magnetic field”
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须满足 qvB = m(v^2/R)。需校验 B 的表达式中距离 r 是否位于分母，并确认电流 I 与 B 的比例系数 k 的定义（kI/r 或 mu_0*I/2pi*r）。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 多质点系统动能分解一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及质心运动与绕质心转动的复合运动能量表达时
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须区分总质量M与单质点质量m。总动能应严格遵循柯尼希定理：E = 1/2*M*v_CM^2 + E_rot，检查M是否等于Σm_i。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 区分路程与位移模长
experience_rules.trigger: 题目同时出现阻力（耗散）与磁场（偏转），并询问“距起点距离”时
experience_rules.check_logic: 磁场不改变速率演化（dv/dt仅由阻力决定），总路程s不变；需建立矢量运动方程 m*dv/dt = -kv + q(vXB)，对时间积分求位移矢量x。

symbolic_hint.canonical: m(v_f - v_0) = -k(x_f - x_0) + q(x_f - x_0) 	imes B

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 阻力位移矢量线性关系
experience_rules.trigger: 受线性阻力 f=-kv 的粒子停止运动过程
experience_rules.check_logic: 利用冲量定理积分：mΔv = -kΔx + ∫F_other dt。若F_other为洛伦兹力，则积分项变为 q(Δx × B)。

symbolic_hint.canonical: L = sqrt(x^2 + y^2), where x + iy = (mv_0)/(k + iqB)

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 稳态不等于受力平衡
experience_rules.trigger: 题目描述中出现 'steady state' 且涉及电磁场中的载流子运动
experience_rules.check_logic: 稳态指物理量不随时间变化（d/dt=0），不代表合外力为零，需区分流体稳态与质点平衡。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 磁路定义域一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 出现 Φ_F / Φ_C 等关于不同部件磁通量比例的询问时
experience_rules.check_logic: 确认 Φ_F 和 Φ_C 是否指代同一闭合回路中的通量。若磁场完全约束在材料内，穿过截面的磁通量在无分支处应相等。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 矢量场分量展开一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 将径向矢量场分解为面内（In-plane）和垂直（Out-of-plane）分量时
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证分量合并后是否能还原为 (r - r_source) 的矢量形式，特别是分母的距离幂次（3/2次）与分子矢量维度的对应关系。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 绝热不变性半径关联
experience_rules.trigger: 磁场“缓慢变化”（slowly changing）且涉及带电粒子圆周运动半径
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否利用磁通量守恒或角动量守恒推导出 r ∝ B^(-1/2) 的幂次关系，而非简单维持速度不变。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 偶极子磁场模长化简
experience_rules.trigger: 磁场表达式包含分量 (-2 sin λ u_r + cos λ u_λ) 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证模长因子是否化简为 sqrt(1 + 3 sin² λ)，注意 sin² + cos² = 1 的恒等变换

symbolic_hint.canonical: B = B_0 * sqrt(1 + 3 sin^2 λ) / r^3

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 磁场周期与速度无关性
experience_rules.trigger: 题目提及带电粒子在磁场中的“振荡周期”或“运动周期”且速度为非相对论时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否直接使用了回旋周期公式 T = 2πm/qB，需确认周期 T 与发射速度 v 及角度 θ 无关。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Magnetic Fields and Lorentz Force
experience_rules.title: 轨道衰减动力学能量守恒一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及卫星受阻力(Drag)导致轨道高度下降(Descent rate)的计算
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证是否正确关联了阻力做功功率与轨道总能量(动能+势能)的变化率，而非仅考虑动能变化。

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / Poynting Vector and Radiation Pressure

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Poynting Vector and Radiation Pressure
experience_rules.title: 跨数量级乘除法量级校验
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及 10^n 与 10^-m 形式的大跨度数值乘除运算时
experience_rules.check_logic: 单独提取指数部分进行运算（n - m），再与有效数字乘积的量级合并，防止因中间步骤估算导致的一位数量级偏差。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Poynting Vector and Radiation Pressure
experience_rules.title: 辐射压力反射系数确认
experience_rules.trigger: 题目提及“平滑/镜面”或“吸收/黑体”表面计算辐射压力时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查动量变化因子：完全反射为 2p/c，完全吸收为 p/c。若未说明性质，需根据物理常识（如金属板通常视为高反射）或题目隐含条件判定。

topics.topic: Electromagnetism / RL, RC, and RLC Circuits

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / RL, RC, and RLC Circuits
experience_rules.title: 物理约束边界非默认解
experience_rules.trigger: 题目给出“不超过某值”的约束条件且中间过程缺失时
experience_rules.check_logic: 禁止直接选取边界值作为答案；必须检查是否存在极值点或由电路参数确定的特定物理量。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / RL, RC, and RLC Circuits
experience_rules.title: 动态过程优先于静态平衡
experience_rules.trigger: 电路中包含无损耗储能元件（L, C）且存在非线性开关/二极管
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否直接使用了静态KVL。若存在L和C，必须分析电流为零时刻的能量状态或电荷极值，而非稳态直流等效。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / RL, RC, and RLC Circuits
experience_rules.title: 无初电荷LC振荡相位判定
experience_rules.trigger: 初始时刻电容器不带电且电感具有初始电流
experience_rules.check_logic: 电流函数应采用余弦形式 I(t) = I_0 cos(ωt)，确保 t=0 时电流最大且电容器电压（电荷量）为零。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / RL, RC, and RLC Circuits
experience_rules.title: 机电耦合系统线性化建模
experience_rules.trigger: 题目涉及可动极板电容器与电路元件（电感/电阻）耦合且要求简谐振动频率时
experience_rules.check_logic: 需同时对力学方程（F=ma）和电路方程（KVL）在平衡点(X1, Q0)处进行一阶泰勒展开，确保耦合项（如电场力中的dq和回路方程中的dx）同时出现。

symbolic_hint.canonical: m*ddx = -k*x + f(q,x), L*ddq + R*dq + q/C(x) = U

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / RL, RC, and RLC Circuits
experience_rules.title: 电容器静电力公式选择
experience_rules.trigger: 计算充电电容器极板间相互作用力时
experience_rules.check_logic: 若电荷量q随时间变化，应优先使用 F = q² / (2*epsilon0*S) 以简化变量耦合；若使用电压U表示，需注意极板间距变化会导致电容变化，从而影响受力。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / RL, RC, and RLC Circuits
experience_rules.title: 磁通量突变转化为初始电流
experience_rules.trigger: 题目描述磁场在极短时间内消失且回路包含电感L
experience_rules.check_logic: 利用磁链守恒或能量等效关系确定初始电流 I(0) = Φ/L，而非通过法拉第电磁感应定律求瞬时电动势。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / RL, RC, and RLC Circuits
experience_rules.title: 非线性弛张振荡周期判定
experience_rules.trigger: 题目涉及非线性元件（如晶闸管、隧道二极管）在IV特性分支间跳变时
experience_rules.check_logic: 应通过积分计算电容器在两个跳变电压阈值之间的充放电时间，而非使用线性RLC谐振频率公式。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / RL, RC, and RLC Circuits
experience_rules.title: 多储能元件激励突变分析
experience_rules.trigger: 电路包含L和C且外部电动势（如磁通量变化率）发生阶跃或停止时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否利用了初值定理（iL(0+)=iL(0-)，uC(0+)=uC(0-)）作为微分方程的边界条件，而非直接切换到DC等效电路。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / RL, RC, and RLC Circuits
experience_rules.title: LC二极管回路峰值锁定
experience_rules.trigger: 理想电感L、电容C与二极管串联接恒压源E
experience_rules.check_logic: 最终电压应为电荷泵浦后的峰值电压 V_max = 2(E - V_0)，而非简单的压降平衡值 E - V_0。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / RL, RC, and RLC Circuits
experience_rules.title: 暂态过程时间尺度判定
experience_rules.trigger: 题目要求在激励变化后的极短时间内（如ms级）求解瞬时值时
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须比较观察时间t与电路时间常数τ（RC或L/R）。若t与τ同数量级，严禁使用稳态（短路/断路）模型，必须列出微分方程求解。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Self-Inductance and Mutual Inductance
experience_rules.title: 圆环自感系数公式校验
experience_rules.trigger: 计算细圆环电感 $L$ 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否误用了中心磁感应强度公式 $B$。圆环自感与截面半径 $a$ 有关，不能仅由圆环半径 $r$ 决定。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Self-Inductance and Mutual Inductance
experience_rules.title: 阻抗定义域一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 计算回路阻抗角或相位差时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否错误地将互感系数M计入本回路的自感阻抗中。M仅决定感生电动势的大小，不改变回路本身的阻抗结构（R+jωL）。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Self-Inductance and Mutual Inductance
experience_rules.title: RL感应回路相位判定
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及互感电动势驱动的RL回路电流相位差计算时
experience_rules.check_logic: 需区分电动势相位（-dΦ/dt）与电流相位。电流i滞后于电动势ε的角度为arctan(ωL/R)，总相位差需叠加电动势相对于原电流的π/2偏移。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Self-Inductance and Mutual Inductance
experience_rules.title: 互感系数与磁通量比例关系
experience_rules.trigger: 题目给出两线圈自感 L 且说明磁感线穿过比例时
experience_rules.check_logic: 互感系数 M 可由自感 L 乘以穿过比例系数确定，即 M = (Φ21/Φ11) * L1。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Self-Inductance and Mutual Inductance
experience_rules.title: 含源电路端电压多解性检查
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及感应电动势与外加电源共同作用的回路电压计算
experience_rules.check_logic: 需考虑感应电动势方向与电流方向、电源极性的两种组合（顺向或逆向），确保不遗漏解。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Self-Inductance and Mutual Inductance
experience_rules.title: RL电路微小衰减建模
experience_rules.trigger: 题目涉及超导体或高品质电感中的电流随时间极微小变化（如一年变化量）
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须使用指数衰减的一阶近似 $\Delta I / I_0 \approx (R/L) \Delta t$，而非简单的能量守恒代换。

experience_rules.topic: Electromagnetism / Self-Inductance and Mutual Inductance
experience_rules.title: 回路电动势平衡方程一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 题目要求在含有电阻R和自感L的闭合回路中表达感应电动势时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查公式是否满足基尔霍夫电压定律（KVL），即感应电动势（源）应等于电阻压降与自感压降之和。

top_down_rules.title: Apply Gauss's Law to conductors
top_down_rules.description: Gauss's Law states that the electric flux through a closed surface is proportional to the enclosed charge. For conductors in electrostatics, the electric field inside the conductor is zero, and all excess charges reside on the surface.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the electric field inside a conductor is set to zero and that surface charge density calculations are consistent with the total charge on the conductor. Ensure that the Gaussian surface is chosen appropriately to exploit symmetry.
common_errors: Incorrectly assuming a nonzero electric field inside a conductor
Forgetting that charges in conductors reside only on the surface
Misapplying Gauss’s Law to regions inside the conductor
Choosing an inappropriate Gaussian surface for the problem

top_down_rules.title: Analyze charge distribution in insulators
top_down_rules.description: In insulators, charges are fixed and do not move freely. The electric field inside and outside the insulator depends on the specific charge distribution (volume, surface, or line).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the electric field is calculated using the correct charge density (e.g., volume density for bulk insulators) and the correct integration method for irregular distributions. Ensure that the charge distribution is consistent with the problem's symmetry.
common_errors: Assuming charges in insulators behave like those in conductors
Using incorrect charge density (e.g., using surface density for a volume distribution)
Neglecting the role of symmetry in simplifying field calculations
Failing to account for non-uniform charge distributions in calculations

top_down_rules.title: Apply boundary conditions for electric fields
top_down_rules.description: At the boundary between two materials, the perpendicular component of the electric field changes proportional to the surface charge density, while the parallel component remains continuous.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the boundary conditions are applied correctly: the normal electric field accounts for surface charge density, and tangential components match on both sides. Ensure that the permittivity of the materials is considered when calculating field discontinuities.
common_errors: Forgetting that the tangential component of the electric field is continuous
Ignoring the surface charge contribution to the normal electric field
Misinterpreting the orientation of the electric field vectors at the boundary
Failing to account for differences in permittivity between materials

top_down_rules.title: Verify constant potential inside a conductor
top_down_rules.description: In electrostatics, the electric potential is constant throughout the volume of a conductor and on its surface because the electric field inside is zero.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the potential inside the conductor does not vary and matches the value on the conductor's surface. Verify that the potential is continuous across the boundary of the conductor.
common_errors: Incorrectly assuming a varying potential inside the conductor
Forgetting to match the surface potential with the internal potential
Not accounting for boundary conditions when calculating potential
Assuming discontinuities in potential at the conductor's surface

top_down_rules.title: Use correct sign conventions for electric fields and potentials
top_down_rules.description: Electric fields point away from positive charges and toward negative charges. Electric potential decreases in the direction of the electric field.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that electric field vectors are drawn with the correct direction and that potential differences respect the orientation of the field. Ensure that the relationship between electric field and potential gradient is correctly applied.
common_errors: Reversing the direction of the electric field for a given charge
Assigning incorrect signs to potential differences
Misinterpreting the relationship between electric field and potential gradient
Failing to account for the reference point when calculating potential

top_down_rules.title: Check dimensional and unit consistency
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that all quantities used in calculations (electric field, potential, charge density, permittivity) have consistent units and dimensions.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that formulas have consistent dimensions (e.g., electric field E = V/m, potential V in volts, charge density in C/m^2 or C/m^3). Ensure that unit conversions are correctly applied when necessary.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for charge density or electric field
Mixing SI units with non-SI units (e.g., Gaussian units)
Forgetting to convert permittivity to correct units when using ε_0
Failing to check unit consistency in intermediate steps of calculations

top_down_rules.title: Apply the superposition principle correctly
top_down_rules.description: The net electric field or potential at a point is the vector sum of contributions from all charges. This principle applies to both conductors and insulators.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the electric field or potential is calculated as the sum of contributions from all individual charges, considering their signs, magnitudes, and distances. Verify that vector addition is performed correctly.
common_errors: Forgetting to include all charge contributions in the summation
Incorrectly adding vector components without proper direction
Neglecting the role of symmetry in simplifying calculations
Failing to account for the relative positions of charges when summing contributions

top_down_rules.title: Check electric field uniformity near conductor surfaces
top_down_rules.description: For a large, flat conductor, the electric field near the surface is uniform and proportional to the surface charge density. This approximation holds far from edges.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the electric field near a large conductor is calculated as E = σ/ε_0 and that deviations occur only near edges or irregular shapes. Ensure that the approximation is not applied to curved or small surfaces.
common_errors: Assuming uniform fields near edges of a conductor
Using incorrect formulas for surface charge density
Misapplying the uniform field approximation to non-flat surfaces
Failing to account for edge effects in field calculations

top_down_rules.title: Verify electric field inside a hollow conductor
top_down_rules.description: The electric field inside the cavity of a hollow conductor is zero if no charges are present inside the cavity. This is a direct consequence of Gauss's Law.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the electric field inside the cavity of a hollow conductor is set to zero when no charges are present. Verify that any charges inside the cavity are correctly accounted for in field calculations.
common_errors: Incorrectly assuming a nonzero electric field inside an empty cavity
Failing to account for charges placed inside the cavity
Misapplying Gauss's Law to regions inside the cavity

top_down_rules.title: Verify application of Gauss's Law equation
top_down_rules.description: Gauss's Law states that the electric flux through a closed surface is equal to the enclosed charge divided by the permittivity of free space. This is expressed as Φ = Q_enc/ε₀.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the student correctly applies Gauss's Law, using Φ = ∮E·dA = Q_enc/ε₀. Ensure the surface is closed and the integration is performed correctly.
common_errors: Misapplying Gauss's Law to non-closed surfaces
Forgetting to divide by ε₀
Incorrect integration of E·dA

top_down_rules.title: Check sign convention for electric field
top_down_rules.description: The electric field vector should point outward for positive charges and inward for negative charges when calculating net electric flux.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify the direction of the electric field vectors relative to the enclosed charge. Ensure the sign of the charge is correctly accounted for in determining the field direction.
common_errors: Incorrect direction of field vectors
Ignoring the influence of charge sign on field direction

top_down_rules.title: Determine applicability of Gauss's Law
top_down_rules.description: Gauss's Law is best applied to problems with high symmetry (spherical, cylindrical, planar). Ensure the environment complies with these conditions before application.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the problem exhibits spherical, cylindrical, or planar symmetry suitable for Gauss's Law. Verify that the symmetry simplifies the calculation of the electric field.
common_errors: Applying Gauss's Law to asymmetric charge distributions
Not recognizing symmetry to simplify calculations

top_down_rules.title: Check dimensional consistency of calculations
top_down_rules.description: Ensure dimensionally consistent equations by verifying units of electric flux (N·m²/C) and charge (C).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all terms are dimensionally consistent with N·m²/C for flux and C for charge. Check intermediate steps for unit consistency.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for electric flux
Mixing up charge and electric field units

top_down_rules.title: Ensure correct use of coordinate systems
top_down_rules.description: Students should correctly choose and apply spherical, cylindrical, or Cartesian coordinates based on the symmetry and geometry of the charge or field.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify the appropriate coordinate system is used and correctly implemented based on the problem's symmetry. Ensure the limits of integration match the chosen coordinate system.
common_errors: Selecting inappropriate coordinate systems
Miscalculating due to coordinate system misapplication

top_down_rules.title: Evaluate surface choice for Gauss's Law application
top_down_rules.description: Choose surfaces that simplify calculations, typically spheres for point charges, cylinders for line charges, and planes for sheet charges.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Examine the selection of Gaussian surfaces to ensure they facilitate calculation based on enclosed symmetry. Verify that the chosen surface aligns with the charge distribution.
common_errors: Complicating calculations with arbitrary surface selections
Ignoring simpler symmetrical surface choices

top_down_rules.title: Validate assumption of electrostatic condition
top_down_rules.description: Gauss's Law assumes stationary charges. Verify the problem involves electrostatics, not electrodynamics.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the charge configuration is static or changes slowly enough to treat as electrostatic. Verify that no time-varying magnetic fields are present.
common_errors: Applying Gauss's Law in non-static scenarios
Not verifying electrostatic assumptions prior to application

top_down_rules.title: Verify boundary conditions at interfaces
top_down_rules.description: Ensure correct application of boundary conditions for electric fields at the interface of two materials with different permittivities.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that the perpendicular component of the electric field accounts for the discontinuity in charge density, and the parallel component remains continuous across the boundary.
common_errors: Ignoring discontinuity in the perpendicular component of the electric field
Incorrectly assuming the parallel component of the field is discontinuous

top_down_rules.title: Validate use of superposition principle
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the principle of superposition is correctly applied when multiple charge distributions are present.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the net electric field or flux is calculated as the vector sum of contributions from all charge distributions.
common_errors: Failing to account for all charge distributions
Incorrectly summing vector components

top_down_rules.title: Check polarity of induced EMF
top_down_rules.description: Lenz's Law states that the direction of the induced EMF opposes the change in magnetic flux that causes it. This ensures conservation of energy and applies universally to electromagnetic induction.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if the induced current's direction (or EMF polarity) is such that it creates a magnetic field opposing the change in magnetic flux (e.g., increasing flux induces a current creating a magnetic field in the opposite direction). Use the right-hand rule to confirm the direction of the induced current.
common_errors: Incorrect direction of induced current or EMF.
Forgetting to apply the opposition principle of Lenz's Law.
Confusing the direction of magnetic flux change with the field direction.

top_down_rules.title: Verify magnetic flux rate of change in Faraday's Law
top_down_rules.description: Faraday's Law of Induction relates the magnitude of the induced EMF to the rate of change of magnetic flux through a loop. The induced EMF is given by E = -dΦ/dt.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the magnetic flux Φ is calculated correctly as the product of the magnetic field, area, and cosine of the angle between them (Φ = B·A·cosθ). Then, compute the time derivative accurately, ensuring the correct sign convention is applied.
common_errors: Miscalculating the magnetic flux (e.g., not considering the angle θ or area).
Incorrect differentiation of flux with respect to time.
Using the wrong sign convention for induced EMF.

top_down_rules.title: Check for resistance in eddy current paths
top_down_rules.description: Eddy currents are induced in conductive materials when there is a change in magnetic flux. The magnitude of these currents depends on the material's electrical resistance and the rate of flux change.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the material's resistivity, thickness, and geometry are considered when calculating the magnitude of eddy currents (e.g., I ∝ 1/R, where R is resistance). Ensure that the induced currents form closed loops within the material.
common_errors: Neglecting the resistive properties of the material.
Assuming eddy currents form without considering the conductive path geometry.
Ignoring the proportionality to the rate of flux change.

top_down_rules.title: Check conservation of energy in induced currents
top_down_rules.description: The work done by the induced current must equal the energy associated with the changing magnetic flux. This ensures no energy is created or destroyed, consistent with Lenz's Law.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if the power dissipated in resistive losses (P = I²R) matches the rate of energy transfer due to the changing flux (|dΦ/dt|). Ensure that energy conservation is maintained in the system.
common_errors: Ignoring energy conservation when analyzing the system.
Miscalculating resistive power losses.
Neglecting the energy associated with the magnetic flux change.

top_down_rules.title: Verify sign convention for flux change
top_down_rules.description: The sign of the induced EMF depends on whether the magnetic flux is increasing or decreasing. Positive flux change induces a negative EMF, and negative flux change induces a positive EMF.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the sign of dΦ/dt is correctly determined based on the flux direction and whether it is increasing or decreasing. Confirm that the negative sign in Faraday's Law is applied correctly.
common_errors: Forgetting the negative sign in Faraday's Law.
Misinterpreting the direction of flux change.
Using incorrect signs for induced EMF or current.

top_down_rules.title: Confirm applicability for non-static fields
top_down_rules.description: Lenz's Law and Faraday's Law apply only when the magnetic field is dynamic (changing with time). Static magnetic fields do not induce currents.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the magnetic field is time-varying. If the field is static (dB/dt = 0), no EMF or current should be induced. Ensure that any assumptions about field dynamics are explicitly stated.
common_errors: Applying Lenz's or Faraday's Law to static magnetic fields.
Assuming induced EMF in the absence of flux change.
Forgetting to check the time-dependence of the field.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure correct use of coordinate system for flux direction
top_down_rules.description: The direction of the magnetic flux and the induced current must be analyzed using a consistent coordinate system. Use the right-hand rule to determine the direction of the induced current.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the right-hand rule is applied correctly, where the thumb points in the direction of the magnetic flux and the curled fingers indicate the induced current direction. Ensure the coordinate system is consistent throughout the analysis.
common_errors: Using the left-hand rule instead of the right-hand rule.
Inconsistent coordinate system for flux and current analysis.
Misinterpreting the relationship between flux direction and current.

top_down_rules.title: Check dimensional consistency of induced EMF
top_down_rules.description: The induced EMF should have the correct units of volts (V), which are equivalent to Weber per second (Wb/s). This ensures consistency in Faraday's Law calculations.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the units of dΦ/dt are Weber per second (Wb/s) and match the units of EMF (volts). Verify that all intermediate calculations maintain dimensional consistency.
common_errors: Forgetting to use consistent units for flux and time.
Mixing up units of area, magnetic field, or angle when calculating flux.
Failing to verify dimensional consistency in intermediate calculations.

top_down_rules.title: Verify mutual inductance in coupled circuits
top_down_rules.description: When two circuits are magnetically coupled, a change in current in one circuit induces an EMF in the other. The mutual inductance M quantifies this coupling.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the mutual inductance M is calculated correctly using the formula M = (N2Φ2)/I1, where N2 is the number of turns in the secondary coil, Φ2 is the flux linkage, and I1 is the current in the primary coil. Verify that the induced EMF in the secondary coil is E2 = -M(dI1/dt).
common_errors: Incorrect calculation of mutual inductance.
Neglecting the coupling factor between the circuits.
Forgetting to account for the time rate of change of current in the primary coil.

top_down_rules.title: Verify magnetic dipole moment calculation
top_down_rules.description: The magnetic dipole moment of a current loop is given by the equation μ = I × A, where I is the current and A is the area vector (A = area × normal unit vector). Ensure the direction of the dipole moment follows the right-hand rule.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if μ = I × A is used, ensuring current magnitude and area are consistent with their respective units (Amperes, square meters). Verify that the direction of μ is perpendicular to the plane of the loop and follows the right-hand rule.
common_errors: Using incorrect magnitude for current or area
Not applying the right-hand rule for the direction of μ
Forgetting to include the normal vector direction in the area calculation

top_down_rules.title: Check magnetic field from a dipole formula
top_down_rules.description: The magnetic field due to a dipole at a point in space is derived from B = (μ₀ / 4π) × [(3(μ·r̂)r̂ - μ) / r³], where μ is the magnetic dipole moment, r̂ is the unit vector pointing from the dipole to the observation point, and r is the distance. This applies only for r >> dipole size.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the formula for B is used correctly, with proper vector operations, and ensure r is much larger than the size of the dipole. Confirm that the unit vector r̂ is correctly normalized.
common_errors: Forgetting the r³ factor in the denominator
Incorrectly calculating dot and cross products between vectors
Using the formula for distances comparable to the dipole size
Not normalizing the unit vector r̂

top_down_rules.title: Validate sign conventions for coordinate systems
top_down_rules.description: The direction of the magnetic dipole moment μ and magnetic field B is determined by standard sign conventions, typically using the right-hand rule for current loops or coordinate systems like Cartesian or spherical coordinates.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that all directions of vectors (μ, B) are consistent with the right-hand rule. Ensure the chosen coordinate system (Cartesian, spherical, or cylindrical) is explicitly stated and consistently applied throughout the problem.
common_errors: Using left-hand rule instead of the right-hand rule
Mixing Cartesian and spherical coordinate systems without proper transformation
Incorrectly defining unit vectors in spherical or cylindrical systems

top_down_rules.title: Ensure boundary conditions for magnetic materials
top_down_rules.description: At the boundary between two magnetic materials, the tangential components of H (magnetic field intensity) are continuous, and the normal components of B (magnetic flux density) follow the relation B₁n/μ₁ = B₂n/μ₂.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify continuity conditions for the tangential component of H and the normal component of B. Ensure proper use of material permeabilities and confirm that the boundary is clearly defined.
common_errors: Neglecting the continuity of H's tangential components
Not accounting for the ratio of B₁n and B₂n based on material permeability
Confusing the roles of H and B in the boundary conditions

top_down_rules.title: Validate energy stored in a magnetic dipole in an external field
top_down_rules.description: The potential energy of a magnetic dipole μ in an external magnetic field B is given by U = -μ·B. This is a scalar product, and the energy depends on the relative orientation of μ and B.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that U = -μ·B is used, with the correct scalar product and orientation between μ and B. Ensure the angle between μ and B is correctly calculated.
common_errors: Forgetting the negative sign in U = -μ·B
Using vector multiplication instead of scalar multiplication
Incorrectly calculating the angle between μ and B

top_down_rules.title: Verify hysteresis loop characteristics
top_down_rules.description: The hysteresis loop of a magnetic material shows the relationship between B and H during magnetization and demagnetization. Key values like coercivity, retentivity, and saturation magnetization should be correctly identified.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the hysteresis loop is correctly plotted and interpreted. Ensure values for coercivity, retentivity, and saturation are appropriately labeled and measured. Confirm that the loop shape matches the expected behavior for the material type.
common_errors: Mislabeling or misinterpreting coercivity and retentivity
Incorrectly plotting the hysteresis loop
Neglecting the saturation magnetization value
Failing to account for material-specific loop characteristics

top_down_rules.title: Ensure dimensional consistency in magnetic equations
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that all equations used in magnetic dipole and magnetic material problems are dimensionally consistent. For example, μ (Am²), B (T), H (A/m), and energy (J) must align with their respective units.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify the dimensional consistency of all terms in the equations used, ensuring units are correctly converted and consistent. Check for adherence to the SI unit system unless otherwise specified.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for μ, B, H, or energy
Mixing up unit systems (e.g., SI and CGS)
Neglecting unit conversions for area or distance in calculations

top_down_rules.title: Check validity conditions for magnetic dipole approximation
top_down_rules.description: The magnetic dipole approximation assumes the observation point is far from the dipole compared to the size of the dipole. This condition is essential for the formulas to hold.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the distance r from the dipole to the observation point satisfies r >> size of the dipole. Confirm that the dipole size is explicitly stated or estimated.
common_errors: Applying the dipole approximation to points too close to the dipole
Ignoring the spatial extent of the dipole in the approximation
Using dipole formulas without verifying the far-field condition

top_down_rules.title: Verify nonlinearity in magnetic materials
top_down_rules.description: Magnetic materials often exhibit nonlinear behavior, where B is not proportional to H. This is especially true near saturation or in ferromagnetic materials.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the nonlinearity of the B-H curve is accounted for, particularly near saturation. Ensure that any approximations assume linearity only in the appropriate range.
common_errors: Assuming linearity in the B-H relationship near saturation
Neglecting hysteresis effects in ferromagnetic materials
Using linear approximations without specifying the valid range

top_down_rules.title: Verify Lorentz Force Equation Application
top_down_rules.description: The Lorentz force equation, F = q(E + v × B), applies to a charged particle moving in electric and magnetic fields. It calculates the force on the particle due to these fields.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the force is calculated as the vector sum of qE (electric force) and q(v × B) (magnetic force). Verify that the cross product is calculated correctly and that the electric and magnetic contributions are combined as vectors.
common_errors: Omitting one of the terms (qE or q(v × B)).
Using scalar multiplication instead of the vector cross product for v × B.
Incorrectly calculating the direction of the cross product using the right-hand rule.

top_down_rules.title: Check Dimensional Consistency for Magnetic Field Units
top_down_rules.description: The magnetic field (B) is measured in Tesla (T), which is equivalent to N/(A·m). Ensure calculations respect these units and are dimensionally consistent.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that B is derived or expressed in consistent units, and that related physical quantities (force, velocity, charge, etc.) align dimensionally. Ensure that derived units are converted correctly when necessary.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for B, e.g., treating it as a scalar without units.
Failure to include the current (A) factor when converting derived units.
Mixing up units for related quantities like force or velocity.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Use of Right-Hand Rule for Cross Products
top_down_rules.description: The direction of the magnetic force (q(v × B)) is determined using the right-hand rule: point fingers along v, curl toward B, and thumb gives the force direction for a positive charge.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the cross product direction is determined correctly using the right-hand rule for the given vectors. Ensure the rule is reversed for negative charges.
common_errors: Using the left-hand rule instead of the right-hand rule.
Incorrectly swapping the order of v and B in the cross product (v × B ≠ B × v).
Forgetting to reverse the direction for negative charges.

top_down_rules.title: Check Magnetic Force Does No Work
top_down_rules.description: The magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity of the charged particle, meaning it does no work (W = F · d = 0).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the magnetic force is perpendicular to the velocity vector (v · F = 0), and ensure no work is calculated for it. Confirm that any work done is attributed to other forces, such as the electric force.
common_errors: Incorrectly assuming the magnetic force does work on the particle.
Failing to check the orthogonality of v and F.
Misattributing work done by other forces to the magnetic force.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Consistency in Coordinate System Orientation
top_down_rules.description: Magnetic fields and forces often involve three-dimensional vector calculations. Ensure the coordinate system used follows a right-handed convention.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that the coordinate axes follow the right-hand rule (x × y = z). Verify that all vector calculations are consistent with this orientation.
common_errors: Using a left-handed coordinate system.
Mixing up coordinate axes when calculating cross products.
Failing to verify the orientation of the coordinate system in complex setups.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Correct Radius for Circular Motion in Magnetic Fields
top_down_rules.description: For a charged particle moving in a uniform magnetic field, the magnetic force provides centripetal acceleration. The radius is r = mv/(qB).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that the radius is calculated using r = mv/(qB), with the direction of the motion forming a circle perpendicular to the magnetic field. Verify that the velocity is perpendicular to the magnetic field for circular motion.
common_errors: Using incorrect formulas for radius.
Forgetting velocity must be perpendicular to the magnetic field for circular motion.
Ignoring the charge sign when determining motion direction.

top_down_rules.title: Check Validity for Static Charges
top_down_rules.description: The Lorentz force equation does not apply to static charges since v = 0 eliminates the magnetic force (q(v × B) = 0).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the velocity is non-zero if applying the magnetic force component of the Lorentz force equation. Verify that only the electric force qE acts on a stationary charge.
common_errors: Applying q(v × B) to static charges.
Failing to recognize that only the electric force qE acts on a stationary charge.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Conditions for Biot-Savart Law Application
top_down_rules.description: The Biot-Savart law calculates the magnetic field B due to a current element. It applies to steady currents and must integrate over the entire current distribution.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the current is steady and the law is applied to infinitesimal current elements (dL) before integrating. Verify that the contributions from all current elements are summed correctly.
common_errors: Applying the Biot-Savart law to time-varying currents.
Failing to integrate over the entire current distribution.
Incorrectly calculating the vector contributions (direction or magnitude) from each current element.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Application of Ampere's Circuital Law
top_down_rules.description: Ampere's circuital law relates the line integral of the magnetic field around a closed loop to the current passing through the loop (∮B·dl = μ₀I).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the law is applied to closed loops and that the current enclosed by the loop is correctly calculated. Verify that the magnetic field is tangential to the loop at every point.
common_errors: Applying the law to open loops.
Incorrectly calculating the enclosed current.
Failing to account for symmetry when simplifying the integral.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Faraday's Law and Lenz's Law Application
top_down_rules.description: Faraday's law states that a changing magnetic flux induces an electromotive force (EMF), and Lenz's law determines the direction of the induced current (EMF = -dΦ/dt).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the EMF is calculated as the negative rate of change of magnetic flux. Verify that the induced current opposes the change in flux, consistent with Lenz's law.
common_errors: Ignoring the negative sign in Faraday's law.
Incorrectly determining the direction of the induced current.
Failing to account for all contributions to the changing flux.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Gauss's Law for Electric Fields
top_down_rules.description: Gauss's Law states that the total electric flux through a closed surface equals the total charge enclosed divided by the permittivity of free space (ε_0). This law applies in both static and dynamic scenarios involving electric fields.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the integral of the electric field dot product with the normal surface area vector equals the enclosed charge divided by ε_0.
common_errors: Failing to account for all enclosed charges.
Using incorrect surface normals for the flux calculation.
Omitting the permittivity constant (ε_0).
Misinterpreting open surfaces as closed surfaces.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Gauss's Law for Magnetism
top_down_rules.description: Gauss's Law for magnetism states that the total magnetic flux through any closed surface is always zero, indicating the non-existence of magnetic monopoles.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that the integral of the magnetic field dot product with the normal surface area vector equals zero for any closed surface.
common_errors: Assuming non-zero flux for magnetic fields through closed surfaces.
Incorrectly applying this law to open surfaces.
Improperly handling vector directions for normal components.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Faraday's Law of Induction
top_down_rules.description: Faraday's Law states that the electromotive force (EMF) around a closed loop equals the negative rate of change of the magnetic flux through the loop. This law is relevant for time-varying magnetic fields.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the line integral of the electric field around the loop equals the negative time derivative of the magnetic flux through the loop.
common_errors: Neglecting the negative sign (Lenz's Law).
Mixing up integration limits for the loop.
Forgetting to calculate the rate of change of magnetic flux.
Omitting contributions from time-varying magnetic fields.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Ampere-Maxwell's Law
top_down_rules.description: Ampere-Maxwell's Law states that the line integral of the magnetic field around a closed loop equals the permeability of free space (μ_0) times the sum of conduction current and displacement current through the loop.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the line integral of the magnetic field equals μ_0 times the sum of conduction current and the time derivative of the electric flux density through the loop.
common_errors: Failing to include displacement current in time-varying cases.
Omitting the permeability constant (μ_0).
Using incorrect integration paths for the loop.
Ignoring contributions from non-uniform current densities.

top_down_rules.title: Check Sign Conventions in Maxwell's Equations
top_down_rules.description: The signs in Maxwell's equations depend on orientation rules, mainly the right-hand rule for vector cross products. Incorrect sign conventions lead to errors in calculations.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the surface normals, loop directions, and vector cross products adhere to the right-hand rule and match the chosen coordinate system.
common_errors: Using left-hand rule instead of right-hand rule.
Reversing the orientation of surface normals.
Flipping the direction of closed loop integration.

top_down_rules.title: Validate Boundary Conditions for Fields
top_down_rules.description: At the boundary between two media, tangential components of the electric and magnetic fields must be continuous, while normal components depend on surface charge and surface current densities.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure boundary conditions are satisfied for both electric and magnetic fields across the interface between two media.
common_errors: Assuming continuity of normal electric fields when surface charges are present.
Neglecting surface currents when analyzing magnetic field boundaries.
Failing to consider dielectric properties of the media.

top_down_rules.title: Check Dimensional and Unit Consistency
top_down_rules.description: Each term in Maxwell's equations must exhibit consistent dimensions and units, including flux, fields, charge density, and current density.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure all terms in the equations have consistent units (e.g., electric field in V/m, magnetic field in T, charge density in C/m³, etc.).
common_errors: Incorrectly converting between units (e.g., from Gauss to Tesla).
Omitting unit conversions when using derived quantities.
Using incompatible units across terms in the equations.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Validity Conditions for Maxwell's Equations
top_down_rules.description: Maxwell's equations assume classical conditions like non-relativistic speeds and neglect quantum effects. They also assume continuous media without abrupt discontinuities unless explicitly accounted for.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the problem context is within the classical regime and that media are continuous unless specified otherwise.
common_errors: Applying Maxwell's equations to quantum-scale systems.
Neglecting relativistic corrections at high speeds.
Using Maxwell's equations without considering boundary conditions in discontinuous media.

top_down_rules.title: Verify the definition of the Poynting vector
top_down_rules.description: The Poynting vector is defined as S = (1/μ₀) (E × B), where E is the electric field, B is the magnetic field, and μ₀ is the permeability of free space. It represents the energy flux density of an electromagnetic wave.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the Poynting vector S is computed using the cross product of E and B, scaled by 1/μ₀, and that the direction is consistent with the right-hand rule.
common_errors: Using a dot product instead of a cross product between E and B.
Missing the scaling factor 1/μ₀.
Incorrectly computing the direction of S due to improper application of the right-hand rule.

top_down_rules.title: Check the formula for radiation pressure
top_down_rules.description: Radiation pressure is given by P = S/c for perfectly absorbing surfaces and P = 2S/c for perfectly reflecting surfaces, where S is the magnitude of the Poynting vector and c is the speed of light in a vacuum.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the formula for radiation pressure correctly uses S/c or 2S/c depending on the nature of the surface (absorbing or reflecting), and ensure that the speed of light c is correctly substituted.
common_errors: Using the wrong factor (e.g., using 2S/c instead of S/c for an absorbing surface).
Forgetting to divide S by c.
Incorrect substitution of the speed of light c.

top_down_rules.title: Verify energy conservation in electromagnetic waves
top_down_rules.description: The energy density of an electromagnetic wave is split equally between the electric and magnetic fields, with total energy density given by u = (ε₀E² + B²/μ₀)/2. The Poynting vector should represent the flow of this energy.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the total energy density u is correctly computed, the contributions from both electric and magnetic fields are included, and the Poynting vector aligns with the energy flow direction.
common_errors: Incorrect computation of energy density (e.g., forgetting the factor of 1/2).
Ignoring the contribution from either the electric or magnetic field.
Misalignment between the direction of S and the wave propagation direction.

top_down_rules.title: Check dimensional consistency of Poynting vector and radiation pressure
top_down_rules.description: The Poynting vector must have units of energy flux density (W/m²), and radiation pressure must have units of force per unit area (N/m²).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the units of S are W/m² and the units of P are N/m² in the final expressions, and ensure proper unit conversions if non-SI units are used.
common_errors: Mixing up units of electric and magnetic fields in calculations.
Forgetting to include μ₀ or c, leading to incorrect units for S or P.
Incorrect unit conversions when working in non-SI units.

top_down_rules.title: Verify the direction of the Poynting vector
top_down_rules.description: The direction of the Poynting vector is given by the right-hand rule applied to E × B. It must point in the direction of energy propagation in the electromagnetic wave.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that the cross product of E and B is computed correctly, the right-hand rule is applied, and the resulting vector points in the expected direction of wave propagation.
common_errors: Using the left-hand rule instead of the right-hand rule.
Incorrectly determining the orientation of E or B.
Misinterpreting the direction of the wave propagation.

top_down_rules.title: Check boundary conditions for E, B, and S at interfaces
top_down_rules.description: At the boundary between two media, the normal component of B and the tangential component of E must be continuous (assuming no surface currents or charges). The Poynting vector must adjust to match the energy flow across the interface.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that boundary conditions are applied correctly to E and B, and ensure that the Poynting vector is consistent with these conditions, accounting for reflection and refraction effects.
common_errors: Ignoring continuity conditions for E and B at boundaries.
Incorrectly computing the Poynting vector in the second medium.
Forgetting to account for reflection or refraction effects at the interface.

top_down_rules.title: Verify validity conditions for applying the Poynting vector
top_down_rules.description: The Poynting vector formulation assumes linear, isotropic, and non-dispersive media. It may not be accurate in plasmas, anisotropic materials, or dispersive media.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the problem specifies conditions (e.g., linear and isotropic media) under which the Poynting vector can be applied, and verify that corrections are made for non-linear or dispersive media if necessary.
common_errors: Applying the Poynting vector in dispersive or anisotropic media without appropriate corrections.
Ignoring material properties that affect E and B relationships.
Using the Poynting vector in scenarios involving significant material non-linearities.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure consistency in coordinate system usage
top_down_rules.description: The electric field (E), magnetic field (B), and Poynting vector (S) must all be defined in a consistent coordinate system, with directions clearly stated and aligned.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that all vector components are expressed in the same coordinate system and that transformations, if any, are correctly applied.
common_errors: Mixing Cartesian and spherical coordinates without proper transformation.
Defining E and B in different coordinate systems without converting one to match the other.
Neglecting clear specification of the coordinate system in the problem setup.

top_down_rules.title: Verify time-averaged Poynting vector for sinusoidal waves
top_down_rules.description: For sinusoidal electromagnetic waves, the time-averaged Poynting vector is given by ⟨S⟩ = (1/2μ₀) Re(E₀ × B₀*), where E₀ and B₀ are the complex amplitudes of the electric and magnetic fields, and * denotes the complex conjugate.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the time-averaged Poynting vector is computed correctly using the complex amplitudes of E and B, and verify that the factor of 1/2 is included.
common_errors: Forgetting the factor of 1/2 for time-averaged quantities.
Incorrectly handling the complex conjugate of B₀.
Using instantaneous fields instead of complex amplitudes.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) for RL Circuits
top_down_rules.description: Kirchhoff's Voltage Law states that the sum of potential differences (voltage) in a closed loop is zero. For an RL circuit, this means the sum of the voltage across the resistor and the inductor must equal the applied EMF (if present).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that V_R + V_L = V_source (if no source is present, ensure V_R + V_L = 0).
common_errors: Forgetting to include the self-induced EMF across the inductor (L di/dt).
Incorrect sign for the voltage across the inductor due to improper orientation.
Treating the inductor as a resistor and using Ohm's Law incorrectly.

top_down_rules.title: Verify RC Circuit Time Constant Calculation
top_down_rules.description: The time constant of an RC circuit is given by τ = RC. It characterizes the rate at which the capacitor charges or discharges to about 63% of its final voltage value.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the time constant is calculated as the product of resistance (R) and capacitance (C), and ensure units are in seconds.
common_errors: Using the reciprocal of RC instead of the product.
Misinterpreting the time constant as the time for full charge/discharge instead of 63%.
Incorrect units for time constant (should be seconds).

top_down_rules.title: Verify Resonance Frequency Calculation in RLC Circuits
top_down_rules.description: The resonance frequency (f₀) in an RLC circuit is determined by the formula f₀ = 1 / (2π√(LC)), where L is the inductance and C is the capacitance.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that the resonance frequency is computed using the correct formula, and verify that the units of L and C are consistent.
common_errors: Forgetting the 2π factor in the denominator.
Using incorrect or mismatched units for L or C (e.g., H vs. mH or F vs. μF).
Confusing angular frequency (ω₀) with resonance frequency (f₀).

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Proper Sign Convention for Voltages in Circuits
top_down_rules.description: Voltages should follow the passive sign convention: current entering the positive terminal of a passive element corresponds to a voltage drop.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that voltage drops across resistors, inductors, and capacitors are consistent with current direction and follow the passive sign convention.
common_errors: Reversing the voltage sign for a resistor or inductor.
Incorrectly assuming the same voltage drop direction for all elements in the circuit.
Neglecting to account for the polarity of the voltage source.

top_down_rules.title: Check Energy Conservation in RC and RL Circuits
top_down_rules.description: Energy conservation should hold true in RC and RL circuits. Energy is stored in the capacitor for RC circuits and in the inductor for RL circuits. The energy supplied by sources must equal the energy dissipated and stored.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the supplied energy equals the sum of dissipated (I²R) and stored energy (1/2 CV² for capacitors or 1/2 LI² for inductors).
common_errors: Neglecting the energy stored in the capacitor or inductor.
Incorrectly calculating dissipated energy using P = IV instead of P = I²R.
Ignoring the work done by the source.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency in RLC Circuit Calculations
top_down_rules.description: Each equation in RLC circuit analysis must be dimensionally consistent. For example, the terms in V = IR + L(di/dt) or V = Q/C must all have units of voltage (V).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that all terms in equations have consistent units, particularly for voltage, current, resistance, capacitance, inductance, and charge.
common_errors: Using mismatched units like ohms with millihenries or microfarads without converting.
Forgetting to convert time units when using derivatives (e.g., di/dt).
Failing to ensure that all terms in voltage equations are expressed in volts.

top_down_rules.title: Validate Conditions for Phasor Analysis in AC Circuits
top_down_rules.description: Phasor analysis is valid only for sinusoidal steady-state AC signals. It cannot be applied to transient or non-sinusoidal waveforms.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the circuit operates in steady-state AC with sinusoidal sources before applying phasor analysis.
common_errors: Applying phasor methods to DC circuits or transient states.
Ignoring the need for sinusoidal sources.
Using incorrect angular frequency (ω) in phasor calculations.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Initial and Final Conditions for RC and RL Circuits
top_down_rules.description: In RC and RL circuits, the initial and final conditions of the capacitor voltage and inductor current are critical. A capacitor's voltage cannot change instantaneously, and an inductor's current cannot change instantaneously due to energy-storage properties.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the initial capacitor voltage and inductor current are used correctly and that changes occur gradually based on the circuit's time constant.
common_errors: Assuming instant changes in capacitor voltage or inductor current.
Neglecting to account for initial conditions when solving differential equations.
Confusing the behavior of capacitors and inductors during switching events.

top_down_rules.title: Apply Fundamental Inductance Equations
top_down_rules.description: Self-inductance describes the voltage induced in a coil due to a change in current through the same coil. It is given by V = -L*(dI/dt), whereas mutual inductance describes the induced voltage in a coil due to a change in current in another coil, represented by V_2 = -M*(dI_1/dt).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if the voltage induced in a coil is calculated using the correct form of the inductance equation: self-inductance for the same coil and mutual inductance for different coils. Ensure the equations are applied to the correct physical context.
common_errors: Using mutual inductance formula for self-inductance problems
Neglecting the negative sign indicating induced emf opposes the change
Confusing the roles of L (self-inductance) and M (mutual inductance)

top_down_rules.title: Verify Inductance Sign Convention
top_down_rules.description: The negative sign in both self and mutual inductance equations represents Lenz's Law, indicating that the induced emf will oppose the change in current that caused it.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the negative sign is included and correctly applied in all calculations involving induced emf, and verify that the opposition to the change in current is consistent with Lenz's Law.
common_errors: Omitting the negative sign
Incorrect application leading to opposition of current increase
Misinterpreting the physical meaning of the negative sign

top_down_rules.title: Check Validity for Inductance Formulas Application
top_down_rules.description: Inductance formulas are valid under conditions where the system can be considered linear, magnetic fields can be approximated as uniform on short time scales, and the materials involved do not exhibit hysteresis or saturation effects.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Determine if the system's assumptions regarding linearity, uniform magnetic fields, and material properties hold true for the context of the problem.
common_errors: Applied in nonlinear regimes without correction
Assuming uniform fields where large spatial gradients exist
Ignoring material saturation or hysteresis effects

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency in Induction Calculations
top_down_rules.description: The unit of inductance is Henry (H), which corresponds to Volts per Ampere-second. Ensure calculations maintain dimensional consistency with respect to time, current, and induced voltage.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all inductance-related formulas maintain dimensional consistency, and ensure proper unit conversions are applied where necessary.
common_errors: Incorrect unit conversion in voltage calculations
Mistaking inductance units as simple power or energy units
Mixing incompatible units in intermediate steps

top_down_rules.title: Assess Geometric Constraints on Inductance
top_down_rules.description: Inductance depends on geometric factors such as the number of coil turns, cross-sectional area, and core permeability. These factors must be explicitly considered and consistent with the setup described in the problem.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure calculations consider the actual geometry of the coils involved, including the number of turns, cross-sectional area, and the material properties of the core.
common_errors: Neglecting the effect of core permeability
Incorrect counting of coil turns
Assuming ideal geometry without verifying physical constraints

top_down_rules.title: Account for Mutual Inductance in Multiple-Coil Systems
top_down_rules.description: Mutual inductance between coils depends on their relative positions, orientations, and the magnetic coupling factor between them.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Validate the assumptions concerning coil orientation, distance, and coupling factor when calculating mutual inductance. Ensure that misalignments or weak coupling are accounted for.
common_errors: Ignoring mutual interference effects
Assuming mutual inductance is unaffected by coil misalignment
Overestimating coupling factor in loosely coupled systems

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Kinematic Consistency in Time-Changed Current
top_down_rules.description: Consistency between time rates of change (dI/dt for current change) and induced emf is crucial, particularly when mechanical motion influences magnetic flux change.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check equations to ensure proper correlation between mechanical motion variables (e.g., velocity, displacement) and electromagnetic induction. Verify that dynamic effects, such as frequency dependence, are correctly incorporated.
common_errors: Failing to relate mechanical motion with current change rate
Ignoring dynamic frequency effects
Neglecting induced emf contributions from moving conductors

top_down_rules.title: Verify Energy Storage in Inductors
top_down_rules.description: Inductors store energy in their magnetic fields, given by the formula U = (1/2)*L*I^2 for self-inductance. Ensure energy storage calculations are consistent with the inductance and current values.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that energy storage calculations use the correct inductance and current values, and ensure the formula is applied correctly.
common_errors: Using incorrect inductance or current values
Neglecting energy contributions in coupled systems
Misinterpreting energy storage as power dissipation

top_down_rules.title: Ensure calibration curve follows the correct mathematical model
top_down_rules.description: The calibration curve relates the instrument output (e.g., voltage, reading) to the true physical quantity being measured. Verify that the chosen mathematical model (linear, polynomial, logarithmic, etc.) fits the expected physical relationship and experimental data.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Use statistical methods, such as linear regression or non-linear curve fitting techniques, to compare experimental data points to the selected model and evaluate goodness-of-fit using measures like R² (coefficient of determination).
common_errors: Using an incorrect model for the calibration curve (e.g., linear instead of exponential).
Not verifying the goodness-of-fit of the model to the data.

top_down_rules.title: Verify consistency in sign conventions for physical quantities
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the sign conventions for all physical quantities (e.g., positive/negative voltage, displacement, current) are consistent throughout the calibration process. This is especially important for measurements involving directional quantities.
