top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that all measurements respect the defined sign convention for the experiment, and conduct a review for consistency across all phases of calibration (e.g., upward voltage is positive, leftward displacement is negative).
common_errors: Inverting the sign of measurements.
Using different conventions for the same quantity in different parts of the calculation.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure proper alignment and positioning of the instrument during calibration
top_down_rules.description: For accurate calibration, the instrument must be properly aligned with the reference standard or source. Misalignment introduces systematic errors.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Use geometric tools such as spirit levels, laser alignment devices, or computer-aided alignment systems to verify that the instrument is aligned (e.g., level, perpendicular, or at the correct angle) per the setup requirements.
common_errors: Instrument not leveled properly.
Angle of incidence not matching the setup requirements.

top_down_rules.title: Verify operating range of the instrument
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the instrument is calibrated within its specified operating range (e.g., voltage, temperature, pressure). Operating outside this range can cause non-linear responses or damage.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that the calibration data points lie within the manufacturer's specified range for the instrument, consulting technical specifications to determine appropriate parameters.
common_errors: Calibrating the instrument outside its operational range.
Assuming linearity beyond the specified range.

top_down_rules.title: Check dimensional consistency of calibration equation
top_down_rules.description: The calibration equation must respect dimensional consistency. For example, if the input is a length (m) and the output is a force (N), the calibration constant should have appropriate dimensions.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Use dimensional analysis to ensure that all terms in the calibration equation balance dimensionally, and inspect units for compatibility across all calculations.
common_errors: Ignoring the units of the calibration constant.
Mixing units inconsistently (e.g., mm with m).

top_down_rules.title: Evaluate uncertainty in calibration measurements
top_down_rules.description: Calibration should include an evaluation of the uncertainties associated with both the instrument being calibrated and the standard/reference. This includes random and systematic errors.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Calculate uncertainty using standard propagation of uncertainty formulas, identify all significant sources of uncertainty, and ensure it is within acceptable limits for the application.
common_errors: Neglecting to calculate uncertainty in calibration.
Ignoring systematic errors in the uncertainty calculation.

top_down_rules.title: Verify the accuracy of the reference standard
top_down_rules.description: The reference standard used for calibration must itself be calibrated and traceable to a recognized metrological standard (e.g., NIST).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that the reference standard has a valid calibration certificate and document its traceability to a national or international standard, reviewing certificates for expiration dates and recent upgrades.
common_errors: Using an uncalibrated or expired reference standard.
Not verifying traceability of the reference standard.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure environmental conditions are within acceptable limits
top_down_rules.description: Calibration must be conducted under controlled environmental conditions (e.g., temperature, humidity) as specified by the instrument manufacturer to avoid errors.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Use environmental monitoring equipment to check that the environmental parameters during calibration are within the specified range for the instrument and document any fluctuations.
common_errors: Calibrating in an environment with significant temperature or humidity fluctuations.
Ignoring the effects of environmental drift during calibration.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure consistency through repeated measurements
top_down_rules.description: Conduct multiple measurements across different trials to assess variability and ensure reliability and consistency in calibration results.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Perform repeated measurements and analyze resultant data for variance or deviation, standard deviation can be used as a consistency metric.
common_errors: Failure to perform repeat measurements leading to increased uncertainty.
Ignoring outliers or discrepancies across trials and datasets.

top_down_rules.title: Define and Maintain Control Variables
top_down_rules.description: Control variables are constants in experimental setups that should remain unaltered to prevent confounding effects. Proper definition and maintenance of these variables is essential for reproducibility.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that control variables are explicitly identified and kept constant during all trials to ensure valid results.
common_errors: Failure to define control variables
Accidental variation of control parameters during experiment

top_down_rules.title: Check Reproducibility with Independent Replications
top_down_rules.description: Reproducibility requires that an experiment can be repeated with consistent results. Using independent replications ensures reliability by reducing errors and inherent biases.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure at least three independent replications are conducted with identical methodologies and consistent result reporting.
common_errors: Insufficient number of replications
Discrepancies in methodological approaches across replications

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Dimensional and Unit Consistency
top_down_rules.description: All measurements should consistently adhere to specified units and dimensions across the experimental setup for clarity and comparability of data.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all physical quantities are reported in consistent units and dimensions, ensuring calculations respect dimensional consistency.
common_errors: Mixing units (e.g., cm with inches)
Omitting units in calculations or results

top_down_rules.title: Adhere to Geometric Constraints
top_down_rules.description: Geometric constraints influence the organization of elements in an experiment and must be adhered to for accurate interpretation.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that the experimental setup adheres to geometric constraints related to control variables and measurement instruments to prevent misalignment.
common_errors: Ignoring spatial alignment requirements
Misalignment of measurement tools

top_down_rules.title: Observe Kinematic Constraints for Repeatability
top_down_rules.description: Kinematic constraints on motion parameters must be consistently applied in repeated experiments to ensure reproducibility.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the movement parameters of any experimental machinery or subject remain consistent across all trials, documenting any necessary alterations.
common_errors: Variable speed in kinematic setups
Changing trajectory without documenting alterations

top_down_rules.title: Consistent Application of Sign Conventions
top_down_rules.description: Sign conventions should be consistently applied to avoid misinterpretation of results, especially when dealing with vector quantities or directional measurements.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure all vector quantities have clearly defined sign conventions that are applied consistently across all trials.
common_errors: Inconsistent sign application for vector directions
Confusion between positive and negative axis identifiers

top_down_rules.title: Evaluate Validity Conditions for Experimental Laws
top_down_rules.description: Ensure the laws or models applied in the experiment are valid under the specific conditions (e.g., temperature, pressure, environment).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that the experimental conditions align with the assumptions of the theoretical framework or model being used.
common_errors: Applying laws outside their valid range
Ignoring environmental factors that affect law applicability

top_down_rules.title: Standardize Data Collection Protocols
top_down_rules.description: The procedures followed for data collection should be standardized to ensure repeatability and consistent data acquisition.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that data collection methods are clearly defined, standardized, and consistently followed across all trials.
common_errors: Variable data collection techniques
Inconsistent parameters during data acquisition

top_down_rules.title: Conduct Thorough Error Analysis
top_down_rules.description: Error analysis identifies potential discrepancies or inaccuracies in experimental results, ensuring reliable interpretation.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure all potential sources of error are accounted for, documented, and analyzed consistently across experimental trials.
common_errors: Failure to account for measurement error
Inadequate analysis of data variability

top_down_rules.title: Ensure entropy decreases with temperature in ideal systems
top_down_rules.description: For cryogenics, entropy in a system decreases as the temperature is reduced, following the Third Law of Thermodynamics. This holds unless external entropy sources (e.g., heat influx or system imperfections) are present.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the entropy S approaches zero as the temperature T approaches absolute zero, provided no residual entropy is present. Ensure that any deviations are justified by material-specific properties or external factors.
common_errors: Incorrectly assuming entropy is zero at non-zero temperatures.
Ignoring residual entropy due to material imperfections or quantum effects.

top_down_rules.title: Verify thermal conductivity decreases with lower temperatures
top_down_rules.description: In cryogenic systems, thermal conductivity of most materials decreases as temperature drops, except for superconductors or specific materials showing anomalous behavior.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the thermal conductivity κ decreases with temperature for conventional materials. Ensure exceptions for superconductors and materials with known anomalous behavior are handled correctly.
common_errors: Failing to account for material-specific thermal conductivity behavior.
Applying high-temperature thermal conductivity models to cryogenic ranges.

top_down_rules.title: Check dimensionless group consistency in cryogenic equations
top_down_rules.description: Many cryogenic equations involve dimensionless quantities, such as Reynolds number, Knudsen number, or Biot number. Ensure consistency in their definitions and application.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the variables in dimensionless groups are correctly substituted and have no dimensional inconsistencies. Ensure that the physical meaning of the dimensionless group is preserved in the context of cryogenic systems.
common_errors: Using incorrect definitions for dimensionless groups.
Mixing incompatible unit systems when calculating dimensionless numbers.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure correct handling of liquid-gas transitions at low temperatures
top_down_rules.description: During liquid-gas transitions in cryogenic systems, the Clausius-Clapeyron equation governs the relationship between pressure and temperature.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the Clausius-Clapeyron equation is applied correctly for phase transitions, and the latent heat is treated as temperature-dependent. Ensure that vapor pressure changes are accurately modeled at cryogenic temperatures.
common_errors: Assuming latent heat is constant across the temperature range.
Ignoring changes in vapor pressure at cryogenic temperatures.

top_down_rules.title: Verify correct sign convention for heat flow
top_down_rules.description: In cryogenics, heat flow direction is critical. Heat flow into the system is positive, while heat flow out is negative.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that heat flow terms in equations are consistent with the sign convention. Verify that the direction of heat flow is correctly interpreted in thermal balance equations.
common_errors: Reversing the sign of heat flow when calculating cooling power.
Misinterpreting heat flow direction in thermal balance equations.

top_down_rules.title: Check criteria for superfluid transition in helium-4
top_down_rules.description: Helium-4 undergoes a superfluid transition at the lambda point (~2.17 K). Verify that equations and models account for the unique properties of superfluid helium below this temperature.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the temperature is below 2.17 K and superfluid-specific properties (e.g., zero viscosity, quantized vortices, second sound) are considered. Verify that normal fluid dynamics are not applied to superfluid helium.
common_errors: Applying normal fluid dynamics to superfluid helium.
Ignoring the unique heat transport properties of superfluid helium (e.g., second sound).

top_down_rules.title: Verify conditions for adiabatic demagnetization cooling
top_down_rules.description: Adiabatic demagnetization is used for cooling in cryogenics. The process relies on isolating the system thermally and applying/removing magnetic fields.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that the system is thermally insulated and the magnetic field variation is slow enough to maintain quasi-equilibrium. Verify that the entropy change corresponds to the expected cooling effect.
common_errors: Ignoring thermal insulation requirements.
Assuming instantaneous magnetic field changes, violating adiabatic conditions.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure unit consistency in cryogenic parameters
top_down_rules.description: Cryogenic systems often involve parameters like temperature (K), pressure (Pa), and energy (J). Ensure all units are consistent to avoid calculation errors.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all equations use consistent units (SI units are preferred unless specified otherwise). Ensure that unit conversions are correctly applied where necessary.
common_errors: Using temperature in Celsius instead of Kelvin.
Mixing units (e.g., bar for pressure and SI energy units).

top_down_rules.title: Verify material property data at cryogenic temperatures
top_down_rules.description: Material properties such as specific heat, thermal expansion, and electrical resistivity can vary significantly at cryogenic temperatures. Ensure accurate data is used.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that material property data is sourced from reliable cryogenic-specific references. Ensure that temperature-dependent variations are accounted for in calculations.
common_errors: Using room-temperature material properties for cryogenic calculations.
Ignoring temperature-dependent variations in material properties.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure proper vacuum insulation in cryogenic systems
top_down_rules.description: Vacuum insulation is critical to minimize heat transfer in cryogenic systems. Verify that the vacuum level and insulation design meet the required specifications.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that the vacuum pressure is sufficiently low to minimize conduction and convection. Verify that insulation materials and designs are appropriate for cryogenic applications.
common_errors: Using inadequate vacuum levels, leading to excessive heat transfer.
Failing to account for material outgassing or thermal bridging in insulation design.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure the regression model matches the expected equation form
top_down_rules.description: Verify that the chosen regression model (linear, quadratic, exponential, etc.) aligns with the physical principles governing the underlying experimental data. For example, linear regression is suitable for a linear trend, while exponential regression is appropriate for decay processes.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the functional form of the regression model matches the anticipated theoretical or experimental relationship, referencing existing literature or theoretical models.
common_errors: Using a linear model for non-linear data trends.
Choosing a higher-order polynomial unnecessarily, leading to overfitting.
Ignoring the underlying physics to select the regression model.

top_down_rules.title: Verify unit consistency in regression parameters
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the coefficients and constants in the regression equation have physically consistent units when interpreting the model or equation. The units of the dependent variable must match the computed units from the regression equation.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify the dimensional consistency of terms in the regression equation by performing unit analysis.
common_errors: Assigning unitless coefficients to terms with units.
Mismatching units due to inconsistent data scaling or transformations.
Failing to check the units of derived regression constants.

top_down_rules.title: Analyze residuals to ensure model adequacy
top_down_rules.description: Residuals should be randomly distributed around zero. If they exhibit non-random patterns (e.g., systematic trends or clustering), it indicates the model is inadequate for the data.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Perform a residual plot analysis and check for randomness by examining whether residuals show systematic deviations or patterns.
common_errors: Interpreting systematic patterns as noise.
Ignoring large residuals that indicate poor model fitting.
Failing to examine residuals in nonlinear models.

top_down_rules.title: Evaluate goodness-of-fit metrics
top_down_rules.description: Verify the model's fit to the data using metrics such as R-squared, adjusted R-squared, or reduced chi-squared, ensuring they meet the acceptable thresholds without being artificially inflated by overfitting.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Compute and interpret goodness-of-fit metrics. Ensure they indicate a sufficient fit by evaluating them alongside residual analysis.
common_errors: Misinterpreting R-squared as a sole indicator of fit quality.
Relying on adjusted R-squared without considering residual analysis.
Overfitting the model to maximize R-squared.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure correct data transformations
top_down_rules.description: Verify that any transformations (e.g., logarithmic, reciprocal) applied to the data are appropriate and consistent with the underlying physics.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Validate that the transformation is justified by the theoretical model or experimental setup. Cross-examine transformations with the expected outcomes.
common_errors: Applying transformations without justification.
Failing to revert transformations when interpreting results.
Using inconsistent transformation methods for different variables.

top_down_rules.title: Account for measurement uncertainties in regression
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that measurement uncertainties in the dependent and independent variables are incorporated into the regression analysis, where applicable. Consider weighted regression if uncertainties are non-uniform.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure uncertainties are included in the regression analysis and that weights are applied correctly based on uncertainty quantification.
common_errors: Ignoring measurement uncertainties in fitting.
Incorrectly weighting data points with smaller uncertainties.
Failing to propagate errors through transformed variables.

top_down_rules.title: Check boundary and limiting conditions
top_down_rules.description: Verify that the regression model satisfies known boundary or limiting cases of the physical system. For example, a linear model should pass through the origin if the system requires it.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Compare the regression model's behavior at boundaries with the expected behavior based on theory or previous experimental data.
common_errors: Forgetting to enforce boundary conditions in the model.
Using regression models that yield non-physical results at limits.
Ignoring known asymptotic behavior in the data.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure proper sign conventions and coordinate system usage
top_down_rules.description: Verify that the regression analysis respects the sign conventions and coordinate systems defined in the experimental setup. Misaligned conventions can lead to incorrect parameter interpretation.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that regression parameters align with the selected coordinate system and sign conventions, ensuring consistency across the analysis.
common_errors: Misinterpreting the sign of slope or intercept in a linear regression.
Ignoring coordinate system transformations before fitting the data.
Failing to standardize sign conventions across all variables.

top_down_rules.title: Check for multicollinearity in regression analysis
top_down_rules.description: Verify that the independent variables in the regression model are not excessively correlated, as multicollinearity can affect the reliability of the parameter estimates.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Identify and assess multicollinearity using variance inflation factors or correlation coefficients among independent variables.
common_errors: Overlooking multicollinearity among predictors that can inflate standard errors.
Interpreting correlation without accounting for combined predictive effects.
Failing to diagnose multicollinearity in complex models with multiple predictors.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure correctness of fundamental statistical equations
top_down_rules.description: Verify the proper use of fundamental statistical equations such as mean ([3mbc = a3x/N[0m), standard deviation ([3mc3 = sqrt(a3(x-bc)^2/N)[0m), and variance ([3mc3�b2 = a3(x-bc)^2/N[0m). These equations form the basis of statistical analysis in experimental physics.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the student used the correct formula for mean, variance, or standard deviation. Ensure all terms (e.g., N, x, bc) are properly defined and consistently used. Verify whether the equations are applied to the correct dataset (e.g., population vs. sample).
common_errors: Dividing by N-1 instead of N for population statistics
Using a3x^2 instead of a3(x-bc)^2 when calculating variance
Forgetting to take the square root when calculating standard deviation from variance

top_down_rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency in statistical calculations
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that all the quantities in statistical computations maintain consistent units. For example, if the data points x are measured in meters, then the mean and standard deviation must also have units of meters.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the units of output (mean, standard deviation) match the units of the input dataset. Verify that unit conversions, if any, are performed correctly.
common_errors: Failing to include units in final results
Mixing incompatible units (e.g., adding meters to seconds)
Incorrect unit conversions during intermediate steps

top_down_rules.title: Verify adherence to sign conventions in error analysis
top_down_rules.description: In experimental error analysis, absolute errors are always positive, while signed deviations can be either positive or negative depending on the direction of the deviation from the true value.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if absolute errors are always reported as positive values and if signed deviations respect the proper sign convention relative to the reference value. Ensure clarity in distinguishing between absolute and percentage errors.
common_errors: Reporting absolute errors as negative
Misinterpreting the direction of deviation (e.g., swapping the sign of signed errors)
Mixing absolute error and percentage error without proper clarity

top_down_rules.title: Check validity of curve fitting models
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the chosen curve fitting model appropriately represents the data based on the underlying physical principles and the type of data distribution (e.g., linear for straight-line trends, exponential for decay processes).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the student justifies the choice of the fitting model based on data characteristics. Verify if the residuals are randomly distributed, indicating a good fit. Ensure that overfitting or underfitting is avoided.
common_errors: Applying a linear fit to non-linear data without justification
Ignoring residual analysis to validate the fit
Using an over-complicated model (e.g., higher-order polynomial) for simple data trends

top_down_rules.title: Validate proper application of error propagation rules
top_down_rules.description: Error propagation must follow specific rules depending on the operations: addition/subtraction (94z = sqrt(94x^2 + 94y^2)) and multiplication/division (94z/z = sqrt((94x/x)^2 + (94y/y)^2)).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the correct error propagation equations are applied for the given operations and ensure consistency with the data's uncertainty values. Verify that intermediate steps in calculations also account for propagated errors.
common_errors: Using incorrect formulas for error propagation in non-linear operations
Forgetting to propagate uncertainties for intermediate calculations
Mixing relative and absolute uncertainties without proper conversion

top_down_rules.title: Ensure correct calculation and interpretation of correlation coefficient
top_down_rules.description: The correlation coefficient (r) quantifies the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two variables. It ranges from -1 to +1. Ensure that students use the correct formula and interpret the result appropriately.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the correlation coefficient is calculated correctly using r = a3((x-bcx)(y-bcy))/(Nc3xc3y) and if its value is within the range [-1, 1]. Verify that the interpretation of r aligns with the data's characteristics.
common_errors: Incorrectly computing the mean or standard deviation during calculation
Reporting a correlation coefficient outside the valid range [-1, 1]
Misinterpreting the value of r (e.g., confusing strong negative correlation with no correlation)

top_down_rules.title: Check methodology for outlier detection
top_down_rules.description: Outliers are data points that deviate significantly from the rest of the dataset. Ensure that the student uses appropriate statistical methods (e.g., Z-scores, IQR method) to identify and justify the treatment of outliers.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the student calculates Z-scores (Z = (x-bc)/c3) or uses the IQR method (outliers are 1.5�d7IQR beyond Q1 and Q3). Verify if the treatment of outliers is justified and documented.
common_errors: Failing to define thresholds for identifying outliers
Arbitrarily removing outliers without statistical justification
Confusing measurement errors with genuine outliers

top_down_rules.title: Verify normalization of histograms
top_down_rules.description: Normalized histograms represent probability distributions and should integrate to 1. Ensure that students normalize the histogram if presenting it as a probability density function.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the sum of the histogram bin heights multiplied by bin widths equals 1 for normalized histograms. Verify that bin widths are consistent or appropriately accounted for.
common_errors: Presenting unnormalized histograms as probability distributions
Using inconsistent bin widths without adjusting bin heights
Incorrectly calculating the total area under the histogram

top_down_rules.title: Check for sampling bias in data collection
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the dataset used for analysis is representative of the population being studied. Identify and address any potential sampling biases that could affect the validity of the results.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the sampling method is described and justified. Verify that the sample size is sufficient and that the data is not skewed due to selection bias or other systematic errors.
common_errors: Using a sample that is not representative of the population
Failing to account for systematic errors in data collection
Ignoring the impact of small sample sizes on statistical reliability

topics.topic: Design of Experiments and Hypothesis Testing

top_down_rules.title: Correct Equation Selection for Hypothesis Testing
top_down_rules.description: Ensure the use of the correct statistical equation for hypothesis testing, such as z-tests, t-tests, chi-squared tests, based on the data characteristics and sample size.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the choice of statistical test aligns with the data type (continuous, categorical), sample size, and distribution assumptions (e.g., normality for t-tests).
common_errors: Using a t-test for large samples when z-test should be used
Applying chi-squared test on continuous data without categorization
Using parametric tests without verifying distribution assumptions

top_down_rules.title: Coordinate System Integrity
top_down_rules.description: In an experiment, ensure all measurements are consistent with the stated coordinate system. This often applies to direction conventions or sign conventions relevant to measurements like velocity or displacement.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if all reported measurements maintain consistency in sign and direction relative to the declared coordinate system. Verify transformations between coordinate systems are explicitly stated and correctly applied.
common_errors: Inverting sign for vector components
Applying multiple systems without transformation explanations
Misinterpreting coordinate system origin or axes orientation

top_down_rules.title: Verification of Geometric Constraints
top_down_rules.description: When designing experiments, ensure any geometric constraints imposed by the setup are adhered to, such as alignment of optical components in a laser experiment.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the setup conforms to geometric constraints like parallel alignment, correct angular displacement, or specified distances between components.
common_errors: Ignoring beam diameter impacting optical alignment
Misalignment of equipment leading to errors in measurements
Failure to account for thermal expansion affecting alignment

top_down_rules.title: Application Validity Conditions
top_down_rules.description: Ensure the laws applied within the experimental design hold under the given conditions, such as assuming linear response for small perturbations.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if the application conditions (e.g., small angle approximation, ideal gas conditions, linearity assumptions) are satisfied before applying specific laws. Document any deviations and their potential impact on results.
common_errors: Using small angle approximation for angles >15 degrees
Applying ideal gas law without low density considerations
Assuming linear response in a nonlinear regime

top_down_rules.title: Dimensional Consistency Verification
top_down_rules.description: Ensure all equations and calculations used in the experiment are dimensionally consistent, adhering to the principle that physical laws must hold regardless of unit systems.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check the dimensional consistency of all derived equations and ensure units match expected dimensions when substituting specific values. Verify unit conversions are correctly applied.
common_errors: Mismatch in units leading to erroneous dimension analysis
Incorrect conversion between unit systems
Failure to verify derived equations for dimensional consistency

top_down_rules.title: Selection of Appropriate Test Statistic
top_down_rules.description: Choose the appropriate test statistic for evaluating hypotheses based on the experimental design and data type, such as ANOVA for comparing more than two groups.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the test statistic matches the structure of hypothesis, data type, number of groups or conditions, and experimental design (e.g., paired vs unpaired data).
common_errors: Confusion between one-way and two-way ANOVA
Inappropriate use of tests for paired vs unpaired data
Using parametric tests without verifying assumptions like homogeneity of variance

top_down_rules.title: Comprehensive Error Analysis
top_down_rules.description: Include detailed error analysis in experiment design, accounting for systematic, random, and human-induced errors.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if error analysis covers all possible error sources, quantifies their impact, and includes strategies for mitigation or acknowledgment. Ensure error propagation is calculated where applicable.
common_errors: Ignoring human measurement error in precision experiments
Failure to account for environmental variations impacting results
Omitting error propagation in derived quantities

top_down_rules.title: Sampling Strategy Verification
top_down_rules.description: Ensure the sampling strategy is appropriate for the experimental goals, data type, and population characteristics.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the sampling method (e.g., random, stratified, systematic) aligns with the experimental objectives and minimizes bias. Check if the sample size is sufficient for statistical power.
common_errors: Using a biased sampling method leading to unrepresentative data
Insufficient sample size for detecting meaningful effects
Failure to account for population heterogeneity in sampling

top_down_rules.title: Control Variable Management
top_down_rules.description: Ensure all relevant control variables are identified and managed to isolate the effect of the independent variable.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that control variables are explicitly stated, consistently maintained, and monitored throughout the experiment. Check for unintended confounding variables.
common_errors: Failure to identify critical control variables
Inconsistent application of control conditions
Overlooking confounding variables impacting results

top_down_rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency of the equation
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that all terms in the equation have the same dimensions. Dimensional consistency is a required condition for the physical validity of an equation.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Compare the dimensions of all terms across the equation, ensuring the left-hand side matches the right-hand side. Utilize fundamental dimensions (M, L, T, etc.) for this comparison.
common_errors: Adding or equating quantities with incompatible dimensions (e.g., length added to time)
Using incorrect units for physical constants like gravitational constant or speed of light
Forgetting to account for derived quantities, like velocity (L/T) or acceleration (L/T^2)

top_down_rules.title: Validate correct unit conversions
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that proper unit conversions are applied when switching between different unit systems (e.g., SI and CGS).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all quantities are consistently converted using accurate conversion factors (e.g., 1 m = 100 cm).
common_errors: Incorrectly converting units, such as using an inverse factor (e.g., 1/100 instead of 100)
Mixing unit systems without applying conversion factors
Failing to square or cube unit conversions for area or volume (e.g., 1 m^2 ≠ 100 cm^2)

top_down_rules.title: Verify correctness of derived dimensions
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that derived quantities (e.g., velocity, force, energy) are expressed correctly in terms of fundamental dimensions (M, L, T).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Validate that the derived dimensions reflect the expected relationships, such as velocity = L/T, force = M·L/T^2.
common_errors: Misidentifying the dimensions of a derived quantity (e.g., treating energy as L·T instead of M·L^2/T^2)
Confusing related quantities (e.g., mistaking force for momentum)

top_down_rules.title: Verify scaling relations using dimensional analysis
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that a scaling relation between quantities derived via dimensional analysis remains dimensionally consistent and matches the physical scenario.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Assess the proportionality constants and exponents in the scaling relation to confirm their dimensions are compatible with the system's parameters.
common_errors: Using incorrect exponents in the scaling relation
Excluding dimensionless constants where appropriate
Deriving incorrect relations by disregarding system constraints or symmetry

top_down_rules.title: Ensure consistency of coordinate systems
top_down_rules.description: Verify that the chosen coordinate system aligns with the physical geometry of the problem and that all components respect the defined axes and sign conventions.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify vector components align with the coordinate axes, and confirm conversions between coordinate systems (e.g., Cartesian to polar) are accurately executed.
common_errors: Misinterpreting the direction of vector components
Using incorrect sign conventions for specific axes
Mixing coordinate systems without proper transformations

top_down_rules.title: Check dimensional homogeneity of physical constants
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that physical constants used in equations have consistent dimensions within their specific context.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify dimensions of constants like G (gravitational constant), c (speed of light) are appropriately used within the equation.
common_errors: Using incorrect dimensions for constants (e.g., treating G as L^3/T^2 instead of M^-1L^3T^-2)
Applying constants in inappropriate contexts without checking dimensions

top_down_rules.title: Validate the equation against limiting cases
top_down_rules.description: Analyze whether the equation remains valid in extreme or limiting cases (e.g., as a variable approaches zero or infinity).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Substitute extreme values into the equation and verify whether the results are dimensionally consistent and conceptually reasonable.
common_errors: Creating equations that fail in limiting cases (e.g., neglecting terms that dominate at small or large values)
Overlooking dimensionless parameters' limits (e.g., Reynold's number in fluid dynamics)

top_down_rules.title: Verify geometric constraints in scaling problems
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that properties like length, area, and volume scale appropriately with changes in system size.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that geometric properties scale correctly with length, area, and volume dimensions (e.g., area scales as length^2, volume scales as length^3).
common_errors: Using incorrect scaling factors (e.g., assuming volume scales linearly with length)
Ignoring dimensional changes when scaling (e.g., treating 2D and 3D objects interchangeably)

top_down_rules.title: Ensure validity of dimensionless quantities and numbers
top_down_rules.description: Check that dimensionless quantities derived within equations are valid and serve their intended comparative function.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that dimensionless numbers such as coefficients or ratios (e.g., Reynolds number, Pi term) are correctly derived and applied.
common_errors: Incorrect calculation or definition of dimensionless numbers
Misapplication of dimensionless quantities that leads to invalid comparisons

top_down_rules.title: Verify correct formula application for absolute, relative, and percentage errors
top_down_rules.description: The relationships between absolute error, relative error, and percentage error are fundamental. Absolute error is the difference between the measured and true values. Relative error is the ratio of the absolute error to the true value, while percentage error is the relative error multiplied by 100.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the student uses: Relative Error = Absolute Error / True Value and Percentage Error = Relative Error * 100. Verify that the true value is not zero to avoid division errors.
common_errors: Confusing relative error and absolute error formulas
Omitting the multiplication by 100 for percentage error
Using measured value instead of true value in relative error calculation
Dividing by zero when true value is zero

top_down_rules.title: Check sign conventions in error calculation
top_down_rules.description: Errors are always positive by convention, as they represent the magnitude of deviation. Subtraction to calculate errors must not yield a negative result.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all reported error values are positive, regardless of whether the measured value is higher or lower than the true value. If a negative value is reported, ensure it is corrected to its absolute value.
common_errors: Reporting negative values for absolute error
Incorrect sign when subtracting true value from measured value

top_down_rules.title: Ensure validity of error analysis assumptions
top_down_rules.description: Error analysis assumes that the true value is known or reasonably estimated, and that the measurement process is unbiased and repeatable. These conditions must be satisfied for the calculated errors to be meaningful.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the problem provides a true value or a reliable estimate. If not, errors cannot be computed. Verify that the measurement process is described as unbiased and repeatable.
common_errors: Computing relative error or percentage error without a true value
Ignoring the need for repeatability in measurements
Assuming a biased measurement process is valid for error analysis

top_down_rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency in error formulas
top_down_rules.description: Absolute error, relative error, and percentage error have specific dimensional requirements. Absolute error must have the same units as the quantity being measured. Relative error and percentage error are dimensionless.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that absolute error has the same units as the measured value, and relative and percentage errors are unitless. Verify that unit conversions, if any, are correctly applied.
common_errors: Using mismatched units for absolute error and measured value
Reporting relative or percentage errors with units
Failing to convert units when necessary for consistency

top_down_rules.title: Check error propagation rules for addition and multiplication
top_down_rules.description: When combining quantities with errors, specific rules apply: for addition/subtraction, absolute errors are added; for multiplication/division, relative errors are added.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that for addition/subtraction, the total error is the sum of absolute errors. For multiplication/division, the total error is the sum of relative errors. Verify that the correct error type is used for the operation.
common_errors: Using relative errors for addition/subtraction
Using absolute errors for multiplication/division
Forgetting to convert relative error to percentage error or vice versa when required

top_down_rules.title: Verify the significance of percentage error
top_down_rules.description: Percentage error quantifies the significance of the error relative to the true value. A high percentage error implies low accuracy, while a low percentage error indicates high accuracy.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the student interprets percentage error correctly in terms of accuracy and significance. Verify that percentage error is compared to a benchmark or threshold for meaningful interpretation.
common_errors: Misinterpreting a high percentage error as high accuracy
Failing to compare percentage error to a benchmark or threshold for significance

top_down_rules.title: Ensure error values are consistent with the coordinate system
top_down_rules.description: When dealing with vector quantities, errors in different components (e.g., x, y, z) must be treated independently unless combined to find total error using geometric addition.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that errors in vector components are combined using the Pythagorean theorem when calculating total error. Ensure that directional components are not ignored in vector error analysis.
common_errors: Adding vector component errors directly without squaring and summing
Ignoring directional components in vector error analysis

top_down_rules.title: Check for appropriate rounding in error reporting
top_down_rules.description: Errors should be reported with an appropriate number of significant figures, usually matching the precision of the measurement instrument.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure errors are rounded to the same decimal place or significant figure as the original measurement. Verify that rounding is consistent across all reported values.
common_errors: Over-reporting precision in error values
Rounding errors inconsistently with the original data
Using different rounding rules for similar measurements

top_down_rules.title: Ensure proper format for error reporting
top_down_rules.description: Errors should be reported in a clear and standardized format, typically as ± the error value alongside the measured value.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that errors are reported in the format: Measured Value ± Error. Ensure that the error value is appropriately rounded and matches the precision of the measured value.
common_errors: Reporting errors without the ± symbol
Inconsistent formatting of error values
Mismatch between the precision of the error and the measured value

experience_rules.topic: Experimental Physics / Dimensional Analysis and Scaling
experience_rules.title: 量纲齐次性验证规则
experience_rules.trigger: 题目要求确定物理公式中未知幂次项（如 α, β, γ）时
experience_rules.check_logic: 列出等式两边基本量（M, L, T）的量纲幂次方程组，求解线性方程组确保两端量纲一致。

experience_rules.topic: Experimental Physics / Dimensional Analysis and Scaling
experience_rules.title: 量纲分析符号一致性检查
experience_rules.trigger: 使用量纲分析法（Dimensional Analysis）求解幂次方程时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查待求量（如长度x）与自变量（如时间t）的物理趋势是否一致；若结果出现负幂次导致随时间增加而减小，需重新核对各物理量的基本量纲定义。

experience_rules.topic: Experimental Physics / Dimensional Analysis and Scaling
experience_rules.title: 复合物理量量纲拆解
experience_rules.trigger: 出现线性密度 λ、角速度 ω 等导出物理量时
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须先将其还原为基本量纲组合（如 λ=M·L⁻¹，ω=T⁻¹）再代入指数方程，避免直接代入导致维度缺失。

experience_rules.topic: Experimental Physics / Dimensional Analysis and Scaling
experience_rules.title: 颗粒材料强度标度律
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及颗粒体积（V）与宏观破坏力（F）的标度关系时
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证是否遵循 F ∝ V^(-1/3) 关系。逻辑链：强度 ∝ 接触点密度 × 单点力；接触点密度 ∝ V^(-1)，单点力（毛细力） ∝ 粒径 ∝ V^(1/3)；综合得 F ∝ V^(-2/3) 或 V^(-1/3) 取决于具体失效模型。

experience_rules.topic: Experimental Physics / Dimensional Analysis and Scaling
experience_rules.title: 热学量纲组合校验
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及比热容 c 和热导率 k 的量纲推导时
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证 [k] = [M][L][T]^-3[K]^-1 以及 [c] = [L]^2[T]^-2[K]^-1。注意热导率包含功率维度，比热容不含质量维度（若为质量比热）。

experience_rules.topic: Experimental Physics / Uncertainty Propagation
experience_rules.title: 多变量定位几何校验
experience_rules.trigger: 题目同时出现观测角(θ)、时间差(τ)和地球半径(R)时
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须建立包含仰角θ的余弦定理或三角几何方程，不能简化为一维垂直模型。检查路径长度L是否满足 L² = R² + (R+H)² - 2R(R+H)cos(φ) 或类似包含θ的关系。

experience_rules.topic: Experimental Physics / Uncertainty Propagation
experience_rules.title: 光速量级常识熔断
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及电磁波/光信号传播时间误差转距离误差时
experience_rules.check_logic: 执行快速量级估算：ΔL ≈ c * Δτ。若计算出的距离误差远小于此量级（如本题中10ns对应3米，预测却给出10^-8米），则判定公式推导或单位换算错误。

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Correct Data Transformation for Logarithmic Scales
top_down_rules.description: Logarithmic scales require data that is positive and spans several orders of magnitude. The transformation typically involves the logarithm (base 10 or natural log) of the original data values.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify all data points are positive and span several orders of magnitude before applying a logarithmic transformation. Confirm the appropriate choice of logarithm base (common or natural).
common_errors: Attempting to log-transform zero or negative values
Choosing an incorrect base for the logarithm transformation

top_down_rules.title: Verify Unit Consistency in Graphical Representation
top_down_rules.description: Units must remain consistent throughout the dataset, and correct units should be represented on the axes. For logarithmic scales, ensure logs of dimensionless quantities or ratios are consistent.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that units on axes are consistent and appropriately labeled. Ensure dimensionless variables or correctly dimensioned ratios are used in logarithmic transformations.
common_errors: Mislabeling axes with incorrect units
Logarithm of a variable with dimensions not appropriately handled

top_down_rules.title: Validate Linear Regression Application
top_down_rules.description: Linear regression should only be applied when data naturally forms a straight line or can be transformed to do so. Inspect for linear trends and absence of systematic deviations.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the dataset's behavior suggests a linear relationship, either intrinsically or through suitable transformations. Examine residuals for systematic deviations.
common_errors: Incorrect assumption of linear relationship in inherently nonlinear data
Ignoring residuals that indicate poor fit

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Validity for Logarithmic Plot Usage
top_down_rules.description: Logarithmic plots are suited for data following power laws, exponential growth, and other multiplicative phenomena. The data must cover several orders of magnitude.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that the dataset spans multiple orders of magnitude and the underlying phenomena justify a logarithmic plot, such as power law or exponential behavior.
common_errors: Using logarithmic plots for data that varies linearly
Failing to confirm phenomenon matches power law or exponential behavior

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Proper Axis Sign Convention
top_down_rules.description: Axes must properly represent the inherent sign conventions with respect to data. Coordinate systems should be consistently applied and labeled correctly.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure axes are labeled with the correct sign conventions and directionality is accurately represented across the plot.
common_errors: Labeling the wrong direction for data trends
Ignoring negative values in contexts where they are valid

top_down_rules.title: Check Integration of Error Bars in Graphical Data
top_down_rules.description: Error bars indicate measurement uncertainty and must be included for accuracy unless proven negligible. They should give clear visual insight into the reliability of represented data.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm error bars are present for datasets where measurement variability exists, and verify their scale and representation are appropriate.
common_errors: Failing to include error bars in graphs
Misrepresenting the scale or size of error bars

top_down_rules.title: Conduct Dimensional Analysis on Plotted Parameters
top_down_rules.description: All parameters plotted should be dimensionally consistent, ensuring derived quantities follow coherent dimensional rules.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify dimensional consistency across plotted data and confirm that derived scales, like logarithmic, maintain proper unit coherence.
common_errors: Plotting dimensionally inconsistent quantities against one another
Overlooking units during dimensional transformation (especially logarithmic)

top_down_rules.title: Address Zero Handling in Logarithmic Plots
top_down_rules.description: Logarithmic transformations cannot handle zero values. Ensure data preprocessing addresses any zero values appropriately, such as using log1p or adding small offsets.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that zero values are handled correctly before log transformation through methods like adding a constant or using log1p for natural logs.
common_errors: Applying logarithmic transformation directly to zero values
Neglecting to preprocess zero values in datasets

top_down_rules.title: Verify consistency with equations of motion
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the measured displacement, velocity, and acceleration in high-speed motion analysis obey the equations of motion under constant acceleration. These include: v = u + at, s = ut + 0.5at^2, and v^2 = u^2 + 2as.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if the provided displacement, velocity, and acceleration data satisfy all applicable equations of motion under the assumption of constant acceleration. Ensure that time intervals are correctly accounted for.
common_errors: Incorrect substitution of values in equations
Assuming constant acceleration when it is not valid
Ignoring time intervals during high-speed imaging analysis

top_down_rules.title: Check adherence to sign conventions
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the chosen coordinate system and sign conventions (e.g., positive for motion in the rightward or upward direction) are consistently applied throughout the analysis.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all vector quantities (e.g., displacement, velocity, acceleration) have been assigned signs consistently with the chosen coordinate system. Check for consistency across all time intervals and reference frames.
common_errors: Inconsistent use of positive and negative signs for direction
Mixing up coordinate axes for 2D or 3D motion analysis
Forgetting to invert signs when switching reference frames

top_down_rules.title: Verify frame rate sufficiency
top_down_rules.description: The frame rate of the imaging system must be high enough to capture motion without significant temporal aliasing (i.e., the Nyquist criterion for temporal sampling must be met).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the frame rate is at least twice the highest frequency component of the motion being analyzed. Validate that the frame rate is sufficient to avoid motion blur and aliasing.
common_errors: Using a frame rate that is too low to capture high-speed motion
Ignoring motion blur caused by insufficient temporal resolution

top_down_rules.title: Verify geometric constraints in motion paths
top_down_rules.description: In high-speed imaging, the motion path must conform to expected geometric constraints (e.g., circular paths for rotating objects, straight-line paths for linear motion).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Compare the trajectory derived from the imaging data with the expected geometric constraints (e.g., radius of curvature for circular motion). Account for potential distortions caused by camera misalignment or lens distortion.
common_errors: Assuming perfect straight-line motion when there is curvature
Ignoring deviations from expected geometry due to camera misalignment or distortion
Forgetting to account for 3D motion in projected 2D data

top_down_rules.title: Check dimensional and unit consistency
top_down_rules.description: Ensure all quantities in the analysis have consistent dimensions and units, particularly for derived quantities like velocity (m/s) and acceleration (m/s^2).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all equations and intermediate steps maintain dimensional consistency and that units are correctly converted where necessary. Ensure that derived quantities are expressed in the correct units.
common_errors: Mixing unit systems (e.g., using cm for displacement and m/s for velocity)
Forgetting to square or cube units in derived quantities
Incorrect conversion between FPS and SI units

top_down_rules.title: Verify projection and perspective effects
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the imaging system's perspective (e.g., camera angle, distance) does not distort the measurement of motion parameters, particularly in 3D to 2D projections.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if corrections for perspective and projection distortions have been applied to the motion data when required. Check for foreshortening, parallax, and other projection-related distortions.
common_errors: Ignoring foreshortening effects in projected motion
Neglecting the parallax effect in multi-camera setups
Assuming a flat plane for 3D motion without projection corrections

top_down_rules.title: Verify appropriate lighting conditions
top_down_rules.description: Ensure the lighting conditions during high-speed imaging are sufficient to avoid motion blur and ensure clear object definition in each frame.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the exposure time is short enough relative to the object's speed to avoid motion blur, and that the object is adequately illuminated. Check for uniform lighting across the field of view.
common_errors: Using long exposure times leading to motion blur
Insufficient lighting causing poor object visibility
Ignoring the effect of variable lighting on image clarity

top_down_rules.title: Check validity of high-speed imaging assumptions
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the assumptions of high-speed imaging are met, such as negligible air resistance in vacuum-like conditions or the absence of significant external forces.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the environmental and experimental setup meets the assumptions required for the analysis (e.g., no abrupt changes in environmental conditions). Check for external forces or environmental factors that could invalidate the assumptions.
common_errors: Ignoring air resistance in high-speed motion
Assuming constant acceleration when external forces are present
Neglecting temperature effects on high-speed imaging accuracy

top_down_rules.title: Verify calibration of imaging system
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the imaging system (e.g., cameras, lenses) is properly calibrated to avoid errors in motion analysis.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the imaging system has been calibrated for lens distortion, alignment, and scaling factors. Check that calibration data is up-to-date and consistent with the experimental setup.
common_errors: Using uncalibrated cameras leading to scaling errors
Ignoring lens distortion in high-speed imaging
Using outdated calibration data for the experimental setup

top_down_rules.title: Check for noise and data artifacts
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the motion data is free from significant noise or artifacts that could affect the analysis.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that noise reduction techniques (e.g., filtering) have been applied to the data. Check for artifacts caused by sensor errors or environmental interference.
common_errors: Ignoring noise in high-speed motion data
Failing to apply appropriate filters to reduce artifacts
Misinterpreting sensor errors as valid motion data

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Appropriate Safety Equipment Use
top_down_rules.description: Verify that the proper safety equipment, such as goggles, gloves, and lab coats, is used consistently to protect against chemical spills, biological exposure, or mechanical hazards.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure safety equipment is mentioned and used according to the type of experiment being conducted. Verify that the equipment is appropriate for the specific hazards involved.
common_errors: Failure to mention eye protection when handling chemicals.
Not wearing gloves when handling biological samples.
Omitting lab coat usage in hazardous experiments.
Using inappropriate safety equipment for the specific hazard (e.g., thin gloves for handling corrosive chemicals).

top_down_rules.title: Verify Correct Sign Conventions
top_down_rules.description: Make sure laboratory settings align with standard sign conventions for vector quantities, such as force, velocity, and acceleration, based on the chosen coordinate system.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure forces, velocities, and accelerations are labeled with the correct sign based on the chosen coordinate system. Verify consistency between experimental setup, data collection, and analysis.
common_errors: Using incorrect sign for vector quantities like force or acceleration.
Misalignment between reported results and coordinate system orientation.
Failure to document the chosen coordinate system clearly.

top_down_rules.title: Check Spatial and Geometric Constraints
top_down_rules.description: Experimental setups must adhere to geometric constraints such as angles, distances, and alignments for precision measurements.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify experiment layout ensures angles, alignments, and distances conform to the protocol specifications. Ensure that any deviations are documented and accounted for in the analysis.
common_errors: Misalignment of optical components in laser experiments.
Incorrect distance setup for parallax error minimization.
Failure to calibrate alignment tools before setup.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Kinematic Constraint Adherence
top_down_rules.description: Verify moving parts in experimental setups do not violate expected motion constraints, ensuring accurate data collection.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure all moving components are constrained as per experiment design (e.g., linear vs. rotational motion). Verify that unexpected motion (e.g., vibrations or unintended rotations) is minimized or accounted for.
common_errors: Incorrect interpretation of sliding vs. rolling motion.
Ignoring constraints leading to erroneous velocity measurements.
Failure to account for unintended vibrations or oscillations.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Validity Condition Compliance
top_down_rules.description: Confirm that experiments are conducted within conditions required by applicable laws and equations, such as temperature, pressure, or vacuum levels.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify environment conditions match the assumptions for theoretical models used. Ensure that deviations from ideal conditions are documented and accounted for in the analysis.
common_errors: Ignoring temperature limits in thermodynamic experiments.
Applying laws of motion in non-inertial reference frames without adjustments.
Failure to monitor and record environmental conditions during the experiment.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Dimensional and Unit Consistency
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that all measurements and equations maintain dimensional consistency and unit correctness throughout the experiment.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that units are consistently applied in calculations, maintaining dimensional consistency. Verify that unit conversions are correctly performed where necessary.
common_errors: Using mismatched units without proper conversion.
Calculating derived quantities with dimensionally inconsistent equations.
Failure to document units clearly in data logs and reports.

top_down_rules.title: Check Energy Conservation Application
top_down_rules.description: Verify conservation of energy principle is correctly applied in experiments involving mechanical systems, accounting for friction, air resistance, and other dissipative forces.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure energy calculations account for all forms of energy input and output, including dissipative forces. Verify that energy losses are measured or estimated where applicable.
common_errors: Neglecting energy lost to friction or heat.
Incorrectly summing kinetic and potential energy contributions.
Failure to account for energy dissipation in non-ideal systems.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Accurate Data Recording
top_down_rules.description: Verify that all experimental data is collected and recorded with precision, including units, time stamps, and environmental conditions, ensuring reproducibility and analysis accuracy.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm data sheets and logs contain all necessary information for analysis, with appropriate uncertainty estimates. Verify that data is recorded in real-time and that calibration states of equipment are documented.
common_errors: Omitting critical environmental conditions from data logs.
Incorrectly estimated uncertainty or failure to record equipment calibration states.
Failure to record data in real-time, leading to potential loss of information.

top_down_rules.title: Perform Comprehensive Uncertainty Analysis
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that all measurements and derived quantities include an uncertainty estimate, and that the sources of uncertainty are identified and minimized where possible.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that uncertainty estimates are calculated for all measurements and derived quantities. Ensure that sources of uncertainty are documented and minimized where feasible.
common_errors: Failure to include uncertainty estimates in reported results.
Ignoring systematic errors in uncertainty analysis.
Using inappropriate methods to calculate uncertainty.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Equipment Calibration
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that all measurement instruments are properly calibrated before use, and that calibration records are maintained.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that all instruments are calibrated according to manufacturer specifications or experimental requirements. Verify that calibration records are up-to-date and accessible.
common_errors: Using uncalibrated instruments for critical measurements.
Failure to document calibration procedures and results.
Ignoring calibration drift over time.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure measurement equation consistency
top_down_rules.description: Verify if the equation or formula used aligns with the measurement being conducted. For example, using a ruler to measure length aligns with linear distance measurements, while a stopwatch applies to time.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the chosen method or device corresponds to the physical quantity being measured (e.g., mass measured with a balance, length measured with a ruler or caliper). Ensure the measurement method is appropriate for the physical property being quantified.
common_errors: Using a stopwatch to measure distance directly
Using a balance to determine volume without converting mass and density.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure unit and dimensional consistency
top_down_rules.description: Verify that all physical quantities and derived results follow dimensional consistency. Units for length, time, and mass must correspond to their respective SI or chosen systems.
top_down_rules.check_logic: For any derived result, verify that the dimensions match the expected outcome (e.g., velocity = length/time, density = mass/volume). Ensure unit conversions are performed correctly when necessary.
common_errors: Adding or subtracting quantities with different units
Forgetting to convert units to a common system before solving.
Reporting time in meters or mass in seconds.

top_down_rules.title: Check adherence to sign conventions
top_down_rules.description: Ensure proper sign conventions are followed, especially when using coordinate systems or directional measurements (e.g., positive direction for length or displacement).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if measurements taken in opposite directions are assigned opposite signs in the coordinate system (e.g., left as negative, right as positive). Ensure the reference point or coordinate origin is clearly defined.
common_errors: Assigning the same sign to measurements in opposite directions
Ignoring the reference point or coordinate origin.

top_down_rules.title: Verify precision and accuracy adherence
top_down_rules.description: Check if the measurement tool used has adequate precision for the required measurement and if the results are within expected tolerances.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if the instrument error or least count is recorded and if the measurement's uncertainty is accounted for in the final result. Ensure results are not rounded off prematurely.
common_errors: Ignoring the least count of measurement tools
Rounding off results before the final step of calculation
Exceeding the precision limit of the instrument.

top_down_rules.title: Account for environmental conditions
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that environmental factors such as temperature, pressure, and humidity, which may affect the measurement, are controlled or accounted for.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the experimental setup mentions controlling or accounting for environmental variables that can impact the measurement (e.g., thermal expansion affecting length measurements). Verify if corrections for environmental effects are applied where necessary.
common_errors: Ignoring thermal expansion in metal rulers
Neglecting air buoyancy corrections for mass measurements
Performing measurements at varying temperatures without noting the change.

top_down_rules.title: Verify instrument calibration
top_down_rules.description: Check if the measurement instruments are calibrated correctly before use. Calibration ensures the instrument provides accurate readings.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if calibration procedures are mentioned and applied (e.g., zeroing a balance, calibrating a stopwatch). Ensure calibration is performed at regular intervals or before critical measurements.
common_errors: Using uncalibrated equipment for precise measurements
Ignoring the need to zero the instrument before measurement.

top_down_rules.title: Check for repeated trials and averaging
top_down_rules.description: Verify if measurements were taken multiple times and averaged to minimize random errors.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the experiment states repeated trials and if the final result is an average value. Ensure the number of trials is sufficient to reduce random errors significantly.
common_errors: Relying on a single measurement without replication
Not averaging multiple trials to reduce error.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure geometric constraints in measurement
top_down_rules.description: Confirm that the geometric alignment of the measurement tool aligns with the property being measured (e.g., placing a ruler properly along the object).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the tool orientation matches the required measurement (e.g., perpendicular placement of a caliper for diameter, parallel placement of a ruler for length). Ensure corrections are applied for curved or irregular surfaces.
common_errors: Placing the measurement tool at an incorrect angle
Measuring a curved length with a straight ruler without correction.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure proper data recording and documentation
top_down_rules.description: Verify that all measurements are recorded systematically and with sufficient detail to allow reproducibility.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the recorded data includes units, uncertainty, and conditions under which the measurement was taken. Ensure no data points are omitted or misrepresented.
common_errors: Failing to record units alongside measurements
Omitting uncertainty or environmental conditions in the data
Recording data in an inconsistent or unclear format.

top_down_rules.title: Verify dynamic measurement techniques
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that appropriate methods are used for measurements involving moving objects or changing conditions.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the measurement technique accounts for motion or time-dependent changes (e.g., using high-speed cameras for fast events, or averaging over time for fluctuating quantities).
common_errors: Using static measurement tools for dynamic systems
Ignoring time-dependent variations in the measurement.

top_down_rules.title: Verify voltage and time scale settings
top_down_rules.description: Ensure the voltage (vertical) and time (horizontal) scales are correctly set to display the signal without clipping or excessive zoom. This allows the waveform to be properly analyzed within the oscilloscope's display range.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the peak-to-peak voltage of the signal fits within the vertical scale range (without clipping at the top or bottom) and ensure the waveform's period fits within the horizontal scale range.
common_errors: Setting voltage scale too small, causing the signal to be clipped.
Setting time scale too narrow, making only part of the waveform visible.
Setting voltage or time scale too large, zooming out unnecessarily and losing detail.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure proper trigger settings for a stable waveform
top_down_rules.description: Proper trigger settings stabilize the display of repetitive waveforms. Ensure the oscilloscope is successfully stabilizing the signal display.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify the trigger source is correctly selected (e.g., correct channel or external trigger), the trigger level is within the signal's amplitude range, and the correct trigger edge (rising or falling) is chosen for signal stabilization.
common_errors: Forgetting to select the correct trigger source.
Setting the trigger level outside the signal amplitude range, resulting in instability.
Using the wrong trigger edge for the signal type.

top_down_rules.title: Validate frequency and period calculations
top_down_rules.description: The frequency of a periodic signal is the reciprocal of its period. Check for consistency between the calculated frequency and the displayed signal.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Measure the waveform's period using the horizontal scale and calculate frequency using f = 1/T. Verify the calculated frequency matches the signal's displayed frequency.
common_errors: Incorrectly measuring the time period between peaks or troughs.
Forgetting the frequency and period's reciprocal relationship.
Not applying the time scale factor when measuring the period.

top_down_rules.title: Verify AC/DC coupling settings
top_down_rules.description: Ensure the correct coupling mode (AC or DC) is used based on the signal's nature to prevent distortion or inaccurate representation.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify AC coupling is used for signals with a DC offset to block it and prevent distortion from low frequencies, and use DC coupling for full signal representation including DC offsets.
common_errors: Using AC coupling for low-frequency signals, resulting in distortion.
Using DC coupling and incorrectly interpreting the DC offset as part of the signal.
Not comprehending the difference between AC and DC coupling effects.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure signal integrity and noise minimization
top_down_rules.description: Verify the displayed signal's integrity by minimizing noise and distortion through proper grounding and probe settings.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the probe is correctly grounded, check the probe attenuation matches the oscilloscope's settings, and confirm the probe bandwidth supports the signal's frequency.
common_errors: Failing to ground the probe correctly, leading to noise.
Mismatch between probe attenuation and oscilloscope settings.
Using a probe that lacks the required bandwidth for high-frequency signals.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure dimensional and unit consistency
top_down_rules.description: Verify that voltage, time, and frequency measurements are reported in correct units and dimensionally consistent throughout calculations.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm voltage is in volts (V), time in seconds (s), and frequency in hertz (Hz). Ensure consistent units in calculations involving f = 1/T.
common_errors: Using incorrect units such as millivolts instead of volts.
Mixing units (e.g., milliseconds without converting to seconds).
Failing to convert units as needed for calculations.

top_down_rules.title: Check waveform symmetry and shape
top_down_rules.description: For periodic signals, compare the waveform shape and symmetry with the expected signal type such as sinusoidal or square.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Evaluate the displayed waveform's shape against expected patterns. Verify symmetry, such as equal peaks for sinusoidal waves, and inspect for distortions.
common_errors: Overlooking distortion or waveform clipping.
Misjudging waveform shape due to wrong time or voltage scales.
Neglecting waveform asymmetry caused by circuit issues or external interference.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure oscilloscope bandwidth is sufficient
top_down_rules.description: The oscilloscope's bandwidth should be at least five times the highest frequency component of the signal to capture accurate waveforms.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify the oscilloscope's bandwidth exceeds five times the highest signal frequency. Check and adjust the bandwidth limit setting as necessary.
common_errors: Using an oscilloscope that lacks sufficient bandwidth, leading to loss of details.
Enabling bandwidth limiting without understanding its impact.
Neglecting limited bandwidth effects on signal accuracy.

top_down_rules.title: Verify probe calibration
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the oscilloscope probes are properly calibrated for accurate signal measurements.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Perform probe compensation by connecting the probe to the oscilloscope's calibration signal and adjusting until the displayed waveform (usually a square wave) is properly square and stable.
common_errors: Failing to perform probe calibration leading to inaccurate readings.
Improper adjustment causing waveform distortion.
Ignoring regular calibration checks as part of routine maintenance.

top_down_rules.title: Preserving Significant Figures in Addition/Subtraction
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the result of an addition or subtraction retains the least number of decimal places of any number involved in the calculation. This rule helps maintain the precision of the measurement.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Identify the number with the fewest decimal places in the operation and round the result to match that precision. Ensure intermediate calculations do not introduce additional decimal places.
common_errors: Using more decimal places than warranted by the least precise number
Incorrectly rounding off intermediate calculations

top_down_rules.title: Preserving Significant Figures in Multiplication/Division
top_down_rules.description: Ensure the result of a multiplication or division retains the smallest number of significant figures of any number involved in the calculation.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Identify the number with the least significant figures in the operation and round the result to match that precision. Avoid introducing additional significant figures during intermediate steps.
common_errors: Using more significant figures than warranted
Ignoring significant figures in intermediate calculations

top_down_rules.title: Correct Rounding of Significant Figures
top_down_rules.description: Apply proper rounding rules when a calculated result needs adjustment to match the required number of significant figures, ensuring no bias over multiple operations.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Round up if the digit past the last significant figure is 5 or greater, round down otherwise. Ensure rounding is applied consistently across all steps of the calculation.
common_errors: Rounding all digits up without considering specific rounding thresholds
Incorrectly rounding leading to precision loss

top_down_rules.title: Dimensional and Unit Consistency Check
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that units are consistent and correctly maintained in a calculation involving significant figures, and that the final result retains proper physical meaning.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify units before applying significant figures rules to ensure dimensional correctness. Perform unit conversions where necessary before applying significant figure rules.
common_errors: Applying significant figure rules without checking unit consistency
Ignoring unit conversions affecting significant figures
