Applying boundary conditions inconsistent with the physical setup

top_down_rules.title: Confirm Fraunhofer Diffraction Condition Validity
top_down_rules.description: Fraunhofer diffraction applies when both source and screen are effectively at infinity regarding the aperture, typically involving plane wavefronts hitting the aperture and observed at far-field.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that the condition a^2 / (λ * d) << 1 for Fraunhofer diffraction is met, indicating far-field approximation. Ensure that the aperture size, wavelength, and distance are in the same units.
common_errors: Incorrectly applying Fraunhofer conditions for near-field scenarios
Neglecting the plane and far-field conditions required for Fraunhofer diffraction
Using inconsistent units for aperture size, wavelength, and distance

top_down_rules.title: Verify Intensity Distribution Calculations
top_down_rules.description: Diffraction patterns consist of intensity distributions across observation screens. Verify mathematical models and integrals used to compute these distributions correctly describe physical phenomena observed.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that intensity distribution calculations incorporate the correct aperture function and utilize appropriate mathematical methods (e.g., integrals or Fourier transforms). Verify that the limits of integration and the aperture function are consistent with the physical setup.
common_errors: Using incorrect integration limits or methods in intensity calculations
Misapplying aperture functions leading to skewed intensity results
Failing to account for the physical dimensions of the aperture in calculations

top_down_rules.title: Validate Diffraction Grating Equation Application
top_down_rules.description: For diffraction gratings, ensure the grating equation is applied correctly to determine the angles of diffraction maxima. Verify that the grating spacing and wavelength are consistent with the observed diffraction pattern.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that the grating equation d * sin(θ) = m * λ is used correctly, where 'd' is the grating spacing, 'θ' is the diffraction angle, 'm' is the diffraction order, and 'λ' is the wavelength. Ensure units are consistent and that the diffraction order is an integer.
common_errors: Using incorrect grating spacing or wavelength units
Misidentifying diffraction orders
Failing to account for higher-order diffraction maxima

top_down_rules.title: Verify Young's Double-Slit Equation
top_down_rules.description: Ensure the equation for determining constructive and destructive interference in Young's Double-Slit experiment is correctly used: d*sin(θ) = m*λ for constructive interference and d*sin(θ) = (m+1/2)*λ for destructive interference. Here, d is the slit separation, θ is the angle to the maxima/minima, m is the order of the fringe, and λ is the wavelength.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if d*sin(θ) is equal to m*λ for constructive interference or (m+1/2)*λ for destructive interference. Ensure all variables are defined, consistent, and correctly substituted.
common_errors: Using m*λ for destructive interference instead of (m+1/2)*λ.
Incorrect substitution of slit separation (d) or wavelength (λ).
Forgetting to calculate the sine of the angle θ.

top_down_rules.title: Check Path Difference for Interference
top_down_rules.description: Verify that the path difference between the two waves is correctly calculated as ΔL = d*sin(θ). This path difference determines whether the interference is constructive or destructive.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the path difference ΔL is computed as d*sin(θ) and used consistently in subsequent calculations. Ensure the relationship between ΔL and interference type is correctly applied.
common_errors: Path difference calculated incorrectly, e.g., using d*cos(θ) instead of d*sin(θ).
Missing or wrong sign conventions for angles in the calculation.
Not accounting for the order of the fringe (m).

top_down_rules.title: Verify Phase Shift in Thin Film Interference
top_down_rules.description: In thin-film interference, ensure that the phase shift of π (or λ/2 path difference) is correctly applied when light reflects off a medium of higher refractive index. This phase shift affects whether constructive or destructive interference occurs.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if a phase shift of λ/2 is added when reflection occurs at a higher refractive index boundary and validate its impact on the interference condition. Ensure the phase shifts for both reflections are correctly accounted for.
common_errors: Ignoring the phase shift when light reflects off a higher refractive index medium.
Incorrectly applying the phase shift for both reflections.
Misinterpreting the conditions for constructive and destructive interference due to phase shift.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency in Interference Equations
top_down_rules.description: Verify that all terms in the equations for interference (e.g., d*sin(θ) = m*λ) have consistent units: d and λ should be in the same unit (e.g., meters), and sin(θ) is dimensionless.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that slit separation (d) and wavelength (λ) are expressed in the same units and that the sine function has no units. Ensure any unit conversions are correctly performed.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for d and λ (e.g., meters for d and nanometers for λ).
Forgetting to convert angles to radians if required for trigonometric functions.

top_down_rules.title: Validate Geometric Constraints in Young's Experiment
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the geometric constraints of the experimental setup are adhered to, such as the screen distance (L) being much greater than the slit separation (d) for the small angle approximation (sin(θ) ≈ tan(θ) ≈ y/L) to hold.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that L >> d and that the small angle approximation is applied only when θ is small (θ < 15 degrees approximately). Ensure that y (fringe displacement on the screen) and L are correctly calculated.
common_errors: Using sin(θ) ≈ tan(θ) when θ is not small.
Incorrectly calculating θ or y (fringe displacement on the screen).
Ignoring the condition L >> d.

top_down_rules.title: Validate Use of Refractive Indices in Thin Film Interference
top_down_rules.description: In thin-film interference, ensure that the refractive indices (n1, n2, n3) are correctly used to determine the effective wavelength within the medium (λ_medium = λ/n).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the wavelength in the medium (λ/n) is correctly calculated using the medium's refractive index and if it is consistent with the interference conditions. Ensure the correct refractive index is used for each medium.
common_errors: Forgetting to modify the wavelength in the medium using λ/n.
Using the wrong refractive index for the medium.
Misinterpreting which medium is associated with which refractive index.

top_down_rules.title: Check Validity Conditions for Interference Equations
top_down_rules.description: Verify that the conditions for interference are met: the light source must be coherent and monochromatic, and the slits or thin film must allow for consistent path differences.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the problem explicitly states or implies coherent and monochromatic light. Ensure that the slits or thin film are properly aligned and uniform. Verify that the experimental setup supports stable interference patterns.
common_errors: Attempting to use interference equations for incoherent or non-monochromatic light.
Ignoring misalignment or non-uniformity of the slits or thin film.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Sign Conventions for Path Differences
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the path difference ΔL is correctly signed based on the geometry of the problem. The positive or negative sign of ΔL determines the type of interference (constructive or destructive).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if ΔL is correctly signed based on the relative path lengths of the two waves and if the sign convention is used consistently in calculations. Ensure the relationship between ΔL and interference type is clearly stated.
common_errors: Incorrectly assigning the sign of ΔL based on the geometry.
Using inconsistent sign conventions across multiple calculations.
Misinterpreting the relationship between path difference and interference type.

top_down_rules.title: Account for Multiple Reflections in Thin Film Interference
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that multiple reflections within the thin film are considered when calculating the overall interference pattern, especially for thicker films.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if the problem accounts for additional phase shifts and path differences caused by multiple reflections within the thin film. Ensure that these contributions are included in the interference condition.
common_errors: Ignoring the effects of multiple reflections in thicker films.
Incorrectly summing the contributions of multiple reflected waves.
Overlooking phase shifts introduced by additional reflections.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Laser Rate Equations
top_down_rules.description: Ensure laser rate equations for population inversion and gain are correctly applied. These equations describe the change in upper and lower laser energy levels and the gain for a laser medium.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify the use of rate equations: dN2/dt = N1 * B12 * ρ(ν) - N2 * B21 * ρ(ν) - N2 * A21 for the upper energy level and corresponding equations for the lower energy level.
common_errors: Omitting spontaneous emission term A21
Confusing stimulated absorption B12 with stimulated emission B21

top_down_rules.title: Check Sign Conventions
top_down_rules.description: Confirm the sign conventions used in laser optics for beam propagation and gain medium properties, which are vital for accurate direction and orientation of the laser beam.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the beam propagation direction aligns with the positive axis and gain is specified as positive, while loss is negative.
common_errors: Incorrect beam direction
Gain or loss discrepancies within cavity calculations

top_down_rules.title: Evaluate Laser Cavity Geometry Constraints
top_down_rules.description: Lasers require specific geometric arrangements to achieve resonance and feedback. Check if cavity length and mirror positioning are within acceptable tolerances for stable operation.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that laser cavity mirrors are positioned to support longitudinal modes according to L = mλ/2, where m is an integer.
common_errors: Miscounting the number of longitudinal modes
Incorrect application of boundary conditions for mirrors

top_down_rules.title: Assess Validity of Electric Field Approximation
top_down_rules.description: Laser equations rely on a coherent, monochromatic electric field approximation. Verify where this approximation holds, especially concerning the coherence length and time of the laser.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm coherence time is greater than pulse duration in pulsed lasers, and coherence length is longer than cavity length for continuous-wave lasers.
common_errors: Ignoring temporal coherence limits in pulse modeling
Confusing coherence length with pulse width

top_down_rules.title: Dimensional Consistency of Laser Equations
top_down_rules.description: Ensure dimensions are consistent across laser equations, particularly for gain, intensity, and emission processes.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify units for population inversion densities (m^-3), gain coefficients (m^-1), and intensity (W/m^2) are consistently used.
common_errors: Mixed units for spatial density and volume
Inconsistent dimensional usage between gain and loss coefficients

top_down_rules.title: Verify Spatial Profile Calculations
top_down_rules.description: Laser beams often exhibit a Gaussian intensity distribution described by laser modes. Ensure the spatial profile calculations apply the correct mathematical form and parameters.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Use the Gaussian beam intensity profile I(r) = I0 * exp(-2 * r^2/w0^2), ensuring proper beam waist (w0) definition.
common_errors: Incorrect beam waist calculation
Omission of the factor of 2 in the Gaussian profile exponent

top_down_rules.title: Laser Threshold Conditions
top_down_rules.description: Verify the laser operates above the threshold condition, where gain exactly balances losses within the laser cavity.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if gain coefficient g is greater than or equal to total losses (including output coupling and intrinsic losses).
common_errors: Ignoring losses from non-ideal cavity elements
Misestimating output coupling value

top_down_rules.title: Verify mirror and lens equation usage
top_down_rules.description: The mirror and lens equation is given by 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, where f is the focal length, v is the image distance, and u is the object distance. This equation applies to both mirrors and lenses, provided the paraxial approximation holds (small angles and rays close to the optical axis).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the given distances (u, v, f) satisfy the equation 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. Ensure that the paraxial approximation is valid (small angles and rays close to the optical axis).
common_errors: Forgetting to use the reciprocal values (1/u, 1/v, 1/f) and directly adding distances.
Incorrect substitution of object distance or image distance.
Applying the equation when the paraxial approximation is not valid (large angles or off-axis rays).

top_down_rules.title: Verify sign convention adherence for spherical mirrors and lenses
top_down_rules.description: The sign convention for mirrors and lenses depends on the Cartesian coordinate system: distances measured in the direction of incident light are positive, and those measured against it are negative. For concave mirrors and converging lenses, focal length is positive; for convex mirrors and diverging lenses, focal length is negative.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the signs of u, v, and f are consistent with the sign convention and the type of mirror or lens provided. Verify that the sign convention is applied consistently across all calculations.
common_errors: Using the wrong sign for the focal length of convex mirrors or diverging lenses.
Reversing the sign of object distance and image distance.
Incorrectly assigning positive or negative signs to distances for specific cases.

top_down_rules.title: Validate the magnification formula usage
top_down_rules.description: The magnification (m) is given by m = -v/u for mirrors and m = v/u for lenses. It represents the ratio of the image height to the object height. This formula holds under the paraxial approximation.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if the magnification formula is correctly applied, ensuring the correct formula is used for mirrors versus lenses. Confirm that the sign conventions for v and u are respected.
common_errors: Forgetting the negative sign in the magnification formula for mirrors.
Confusing the formulas for mirrors and lenses.
Improperly calculating the image or object height relative to magnification.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure geometric constraints on focal point location
top_down_rules.description: The focal point of a mirror or lens must lie at a fixed distance (f) from the mirror's pole or lens' optical center. For mirrors, this is f = R/2, where R is the radius of curvature.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the focal length f is consistent with the given radius of curvature R (f = R/2). Ensure that the geometry of the optical system is consistent with the given parameters.
common_errors: Using an incorrect formula for focal length based on radius of curvature.
Confusing radius of curvature (R) with diameter or focal length directly.
Applying the formula for lenses to mirrors or vice versa.

top_down_rules.title: Verify application under paraxial approximation
top_down_rules.description: The laws of mirrors and lenses (mirror equation, lens equation, magnification formula) are valid only under the paraxial approximation, where incident rays make small angles with the optical axis, and distances are measured close to the axis.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the angles involved are small and the rays are near the optical axis. Check for any mention of large angles, off-axis rays, or aberrations.
common_errors: Applying the mirror or lens equation to situations where the paraxial approximation is violated.
Neglecting the effects of aberrations for large angles or rays far from the optical axis.

top_down_rules.title: Check dimensional consistency of optical equations
top_down_rules.description: In the mirror and lens equations, all distances (u, v, f) must have the same units, typically in meters or centimeters. Magnification is unitless as it is a ratio of heights or distances.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all distances in the equation have consistent units (e.g., meters or centimeters) and that magnification is dimensionless.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for object distance, image distance, or focal length.
Treating magnification as if it has units.

top_down_rules.title: Validate real and virtual image criteria
top_down_rules.description: For mirrors and lenses, real images occur when light rays converge, and virtual images occur when they appear to diverge. Real images have positive image distances, while virtual images have negative image distances.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the image distance (v) is positive for real images and negative for virtual images, consistent with the type of mirror or lens. Ensure that the interpretation of real and virtual images aligns with the optical system's geometry.
common_errors: Misidentifying the type of image (real or virtual) based on the sign of v.
Confusing the properties of real and virtual images for mirrors versus lenses.

top_down_rules.title: Verify ray diagram consistency with optical laws
top_down_rules.description: Ray diagrams for mirrors and lenses must follow the laws of reflection or refraction. For example, reflected rays must obey the law of reflection, and refracted rays must adhere to Snell's law at the lens surfaces.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the drawn rays follow the laws of reflection and refraction. Verify that the image location in the diagram matches the calculated one using the lens or mirror equation.
common_errors: Drawing rays that do not pass through the focal point for specific cases.
Violating the law of reflection for mirrors (angle of incidence ≠ angle of reflection).
Not using Snell's law for refracted rays at a lens surface.

top_down_rules.title: Check for spherical and chromatic aberrations
top_down_rules.description: Spherical aberration occurs when rays far from the optical axis do not converge at the same focal point. Chromatic aberration occurs in lenses due to the dispersion of light, causing different colors to focus at different points.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if the optical system accounts for spherical and chromatic aberrations, especially for large apertures or wide-angle lenses. Check if corrective measures (e.g., aspherical lenses or achromatic doublets) are mentioned.
common_errors: Ignoring spherical aberration for wide-aperture systems.
Neglecting chromatic aberration in lenses with significant dispersion.
Failing to mention corrective measures for aberrations in high-precision systems.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Maxwell's equations in nonlinear media
top_down_rules.description: Check if the governing Maxwell's equations in nonlinear media are correctly applied. In nonlinear optics, the displacement field D includes higher-order terms of the electric field E, such as P = χ^(1)E + χ^(2)E^2 + χ^(3)E^3. These nonlinear terms are responsible for phenomena like harmonic generation and self-focusing.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the polarization terms (χ^(n)E^n) are included in the displacement field, and the wave equation is correctly derived from Maxwell's equations. Confirm that the nonlinear terms are appropriately incorporated into the wave equation derivation.
common_errors: Ignoring higher-order polarization terms (χ^(2), χ^(3)) for nonlinear processes.
Incorrectly deriving the wave equation from Maxwell's equations.
Using linear susceptibility instead of nonlinear susceptibility for nonlinear media.

top_down_rules.title: Check energy conservation in harmonic generation
top_down_rules.description: In harmonic generation, the energy of the generated harmonic wave must come from the fundamental wave. Energy conservation dictates that the sum of the energies (or frequencies) of the interacting waves remains constant.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the frequencies and energy of the generated harmonics match the sum or difference of the interacting fundamental wave frequencies. Ensure that the depletion of the fundamental wave is accounted for in energy transfer calculations.
common_errors: Mismatching the input and output frequencies in energy conservation.
Ignoring the depletion of the fundamental wave due to energy transfer to harmonics.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure phase-matching condition is satisfied
top_down_rules.description: For efficient harmonic generation or nonlinear interactions, the phase-matching condition (k1 ± k2 ± ... = kn) must be satisfied, where k denotes the wavevector of interacting waves. This ensures constructive interference and maximized conversion efficiency.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the wavevectors satisfy the phase-matching condition in the given geometry and medium. Verify that material dispersion, birefringence, and crystal orientation are correctly accounted for in the calculations.
common_errors: Not accounting for material dispersion when calculating wavevectors.
Using incorrect refractive indices for the interacting frequencies.
Neglecting contributions from birefringence or crystal orientation in anisotropic media.

top_down_rules.title: Verify sign conventions for wave propagation
top_down_rules.description: In nonlinear optics, the sign convention for wave propagation direction, electric field, and polarization must be consistent. Incorrect sign conventions can lead to errors in phase-matching and energy flow calculations.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the propagation direction and polarization vectors follow the right-hand rule and are consistent with the chosen coordinate system. Confirm that the sign conventions are uniformly applied across all equations.
common_errors: Using inconsistent wavevector or polarization sign conventions across equations.
Incorrectly assigning negative signs to forward or backward propagating waves.
Ignoring handedness of coordinate systems in anisotropic or birefringent media.

top_down_rules.title: Check medium constraints for nonlinear effects
top_down_rules.description: Nonlinear optical effects like second-harmonic generation (SHG) or self-focusing require specific material properties, such as non-centrosymmetric crystal structure for SHG or a positive nonlinear refractive index for self-focusing.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the medium properties (e.g., non-centrosymmetry, nonlinear coefficients) are suitable for the observed nonlinear effect. Confirm that material absorption and saturation effects are considered at high intensities.
common_errors: Applying SHG in a centrosymmetric material.
Using incorrect or unrealistic nonlinear refractive indices.
Ignoring material absorption or saturation effects at high intensities.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure validity conditions for nonlinear equations
top_down_rules.description: Nonlinear equations assume certain conditions, such as the slowly varying envelope approximation (SVEA) and negligible depletion of the pump wave. These assumptions must hold for the equations to be valid.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the intensity of the pump wave is high enough for nonlinear effects but low enough to maintain the SVEA and negligible depletion. Verify that the pulse duration and beam parameters are consistent with the assumptions.
common_errors: Violating the SVEA by using extremely short pulses.
Ignoring pump depletion in high-efficiency nonlinear processes.
Overestimating nonlinear effects in weak-field regimes.

top_down_rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency in equations
top_down_rules.description: All equations in nonlinear optics must be dimensionally consistent, particularly when dealing with nonlinear susceptibility terms (e.g., χ^(2), χ^(3)). These terms have specific units that depend on the order of nonlinearity and the electric field's units.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the units of χ^(2), χ^(3), and other nonlinear terms are correctly applied in calculations, and the resulting units match physical expectations. Confirm that the unit systems (e.g., SI or Gaussian) are consistently used.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for nonlinear susceptibility terms.
Mixing SI and Gaussian unit systems in equations.
Ignoring the unit scaling of electric fields in nonlinear interactions.

top_down_rules.title: Check self-focusing threshold intensity
top_down_rules.description: Self-focusing occurs when the intensity of a laser beam exceeds a critical threshold, determined by the nonlinear refractive index and beam parameters. Below this threshold, self-focusing does not occur.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the input beam intensity exceeds the critical self-focusing threshold for the given medium and beam geometry. Ensure that the beam parameters, such as spot size and wavelength, are correctly included in the threshold calculation.
common_errors: Miscalculating the critical intensity for self-focusing.
Ignoring beam parameters like spot size and wavelength in threshold calculations.
Predicting self-focusing in media with negligible nonlinear refractive index.

top_down_rules.title: Check group velocity mismatch in nonlinear interactions
top_down_rules.description: Group velocity mismatch (GVM) between interacting waves can limit the efficiency of nonlinear processes, especially for ultrafast pulses. GVM arises due to differences in group velocities of the interacting waves in the medium.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the group velocity mismatch is calculated and its impact on the interaction efficiency is assessed. Ensure that pulse durations and medium dispersion are considered.
common_errors: Ignoring group velocity mismatch in ultrafast pulse interactions.
Using incorrect group velocity values for the interacting waves.
Neglecting the effect of dispersion on pulse overlap.

top_down_rules.title: Verify coherence length using the wavelength and bandwidth
top_down_rules.description: The coherence length is given by L_c = c / Δν, where c is the speed of light and Δν is the spectral bandwidth. It describes the spatial extent over which a wavefront remains coherent.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the coherence length L_c is calculated using the formula L_c = c / Δν, ensuring that Δν (bandwidth) is provided in units of Hz and c is in m/s.
common_errors: Using the source wavelength instead of the bandwidth in the formula
Incorrect unit conversion for spectral bandwidth
Confusing coherence length with wavelength

top_down_rules.title: Verify phase difference calculation in interferometers
top_down_rules.description: The phase difference Δϕ in an interferometer setup is given by Δϕ = (2π/λ) ΔL, where λ is the wavelength of light and ΔL is the path length difference.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the phase difference is calculated using Δϕ = (2π/λ) ΔL, ensuring consistent units for ΔL (meters) and λ (meters).
common_errors: Forgetting the factor 2π in the formula
Using the absolute path length instead of the path difference
Mismatch in units for ΔL and λ

top_down_rules.title: Verify sign convention for path length difference
top_down_rules.description: In an interferometer, the path length difference ΔL is positive if the path in one arm is longer than the other and negative if shorter. This sign convention affects the interference pattern.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the sign of ΔL is correctly assigned based on the physical geometry of the interferometer setup and ensure it is consistently applied in phase difference calculations.
common_errors: Using inconsistent signs for ΔL
Ignoring the sign of path length differences leading to incorrect phase difference calculations

top_down_rules.title: Ensure light sources are coherent for interference
top_down_rules.description: Interference phenomena in interferometers require coherent light sources, meaning the sources should have a fixed phase relationship and similar wavelengths.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that the light sources used are described as coherent and that they meet the criteria for producing an interference pattern. Verify that the coherence length of the source is sufficient for the experimental setup.
common_errors: Attempting to calculate interference without ensuring coherence
Using light sources with vastly differing wavelengths
Ignoring the coherence length of the source

top_down_rules.title: Check dimensional consistency of optical coherence equations
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that all terms in equations related to coherence (e.g., L_c = c / Δν) are dimensionally consistent. For instance, c must be in m/s and Δν in Hz to result in L_c in meters.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the units of all quantities in the equation are consistent, particularly with L_c resulting in units of length. Ensure proper unit conversions where necessary.
common_errors: Using mixed units (e.g., nm for wavelength and Hz for frequency)
Forgetting to convert bandwidth to Hz

top_down_rules.title: Ensure correct conditions for constructive and destructive interference
top_down_rules.description: Constructive interference occurs when Δϕ = 2mπ (m is an integer), and destructive interference occurs when Δϕ = (2m+1)π. This depends on the path length difference and wavelength.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that the conditions for constructive and destructive interference are applied correctly using Δϕ and the appropriate equations. Verify that ΔL and λ are consistent with the calculated Δϕ.
common_errors: Misapplying constructive/destructive conditions
Using incorrect multiples of π in phase difference calculations
Confusing Δϕ with ΔL directly

top_down_rules.title: Verify Michelson Interferometer arm lengths and path difference
top_down_rules.description: In a Michelson Interferometer, the path length difference is 2ΔL due to the reflection of beams. ΔL is the difference in arm lengths.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that the path length difference is calculated as 2ΔL and that the arm lengths are correctly measured and substituted. Ensure that the factor of 2 is included due to the reflection.
common_errors: Forgetting the factor of 2 due to reflection
Using incorrect arm length measurements
Misinterpreting the geometry of the interferometer

top_down_rules.title: Ensure small angles for approximations in interferometers
top_down_rules.description: For many interferometer setups, small-angle approximations (e.g., sinθ ≈ θ) are used for simplicity. These approximations are valid only when θ is small (in radians).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the small-angle approximation is applied and verify that θ is indeed small (e.g., θ < 10 degrees or approximately 0.174 radians). Ensure proper unit conversion if θ is provided in degrees.
common_errors: Applying small-angle approximations to large angles
Using θ in degrees instead of radians without conversion

top_down_rules.title: Verify frequency-wavelength relationship for light
top_down_rules.description: The relationship between frequency (ν), wavelength (λ), and the speed of light (c) is given by c = λν.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that the relationship c = λν is used correctly, ensuring consistent units (e.g., c in m/s, λ in meters, and ν in Hz). Verify proper conversions if units are mixed.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for c, λ, or ν
Forgetting to convert wavelength from nm to meters

top_down_rules.title: Apply Lensmaker's Equation for Focal Length
top_down_rules.description: The Lensmaker's Equation calculates the focal length of a lens based on its radius of curvature and the refractive index. It applies to thin lenses under the paraxial approximation.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the focal length is calculated using 1/f = (n - 1) * (1/R1 - 1/R2), where R1 and R2 are the radii of curvature of the lens surfaces, and n is the refractive index of the lens material.
common_errors: Using wrong sign for radii of curvature
Incorrect refractive index value in the equation

top_down_rules.title: Adhere to Sign Conventions for Lens Formulas
top_down_rules.description: In optics, sign conventions dictate the positive or negative assignment for distances. For converging lenses, distances measured against the direction of incident light (left to right) are negative.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that object distances, image distances, and focal lengths adhere to the sign conventions based on lens type and orientation. For example, for a converging lens, focal length is positive, and for a diverging lens, it is negative.
common_errors: Incorrect sign for object distance when using lens formulas
Wrong sign in focal length application in calculations

top_down_rules.title: Calculate Magnification Correctly
top_down_rules.description: Magnification for optical instruments is defined as the ratio of the image height to the object height. Ensure calculations reflect this definition.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Calculate magnification using M = -di/do for lenses and telescopes, ensuring the negative sign indicates inverted images. For microscopes, ensure the total magnification is the product of the objective and eyepiece magnifications.
common_errors: Forgetting to include negative sign for inverted images
Misinterpreting object and image distances
Omitting the contribution of the eyepiece in total magnification for microscopes

top_down_rules.title: Maintain Geometric Alignment Constraints
top_down_rules.description: Geometric alignment in optical instruments is critical to their functioning. Ensure lenses, mirrors, and other components are appropriately aligned.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that all components of the optical instrument are aligned along the principal axis or the intended optical path. Check for tilt, decentering, or misalignment that could cause aberrations or distortions.
common_errors: Misaligned lenses causing distortion
Improper orientation of mirrors in telescopes
Failure to align the optical axis with the principal axis

top_down_rules.title: Validate Conditions for Ray Optics
top_down_rules.description: Ray optics applies when the wavelength is much smaller than the size of the optical elements, allowing simplification using geometric optics equations.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check that the wavelength of light is significantly smaller than the aperture size or lens diameter before applying ray optics principles. If not, wave optics principles should be used instead.
common_errors: Applying ray optics to setups not satisfying wavelength-to-aperture proportion
Using ray optics equations for phenomena requiring wave optics

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency in Equations
top_down_rules.description: Optical instruments involve several dimensional quantities (distance, height, radius). Ensure units are consistent when substituting into formulas.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all quantities, especially distances, focal lengths, and radii of curvature, are in compatible units (commonly meters or centimeters) before calculations. Perform unit conversions if necessary.
common_errors: Mismatch in units between focal length and object/image distances
Ignoring conversion of units prior to mathematical operations

top_down_rules.title: Consider Eyepiece Accommodation in Telescopes
top_down_rules.description: The eyepiece of a telescope adjusts the focal points for viewing. Ensure calculations consider the influence of eyepiece characteristics.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the telescope's eyepiece focal length is used correctly in image formation and determining overall magnification. Ensure the eye relief distance is accounted for in practical setups.
common_errors: Overlooking the effect of eye relief distance
Inaccurate use of eyepiece focal length causing miscalculation of magnification

top_down_rules.title: Apply Object-Image Distance Equation Correctly
top_down_rules.description: For optical instruments, the relation 1/f = 1/do + 1/di governs the relationship between object and image distances with focal length.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that object distance (do) and image distance (di) are correctly placed in the equation and solved for their respective values. Ensure proper unit consistency during calculations.
common_errors: Mixing up object and image distances when substituting into the equation
Improper conversion of units resulting in incorrect solution

top_down_rules.title: Account for Optical Aberrations
top_down_rules.description: Optical aberrations such as spherical aberration, chromatic aberration, and astigmatism can affect image quality. Ensure these are minimized in design and calculations.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the lens or mirror design accounts for aberrations. For chromatic aberration, verify if an achromatic doublet or similar correction is used. For spherical aberration, ensure the lens shape is optimized.
common_errors: Ignoring chromatic aberration in multi-wavelength setups
Failure to account for spherical aberration in high-precision instruments

top_down_rules.title: Consider Diffraction Limit in Resolution
top_down_rules.description: The resolution of optical instruments is limited by diffraction, which depends on the aperture size and wavelength of light.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the resolution calculation considers the diffraction limit using the formula θ = 1.22 * λ/D, where λ is the wavelength and D is the aperture diameter.
common_errors: Overestimating resolution by ignoring diffraction effects
Using incorrect aperture size in diffraction limit calculations

topics.topic: Optics / Diffraction (Single Slit, Double Slit, Gratings)

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Diffraction (Single Slit, Double Slit, Gratings)
experience_rules.title: 三维斜入射光栅建模校验
experience_rules.trigger: 题目涉及光栅衍射且入射光与光栅刻线方向不垂直（存在偏角φ）
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查光程差计算是否仅简单乘以cosφ。在三维空间中，衍射角与入射角的关系通常涉及方向余弦的平方差开方，而非简单的三角函数乘积。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Diffraction (Single Slit, Double Slit, Gratings)
experience_rules.title: 探测器受限分辨率判据
experience_rules.trigger: 题目同时给出分光元件参数（如光栅长度）和探测器参数（如pixel/mm）时
experience_rules.check_logic: 需比较本征分辨率（Δλ_intrinsic = λ/mN）与几何分辨率（Δλ_pixel = Δy / (f * dθ/dλ)），取较大值作为最终分辨率。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Diffraction (Single Slit, Double Slit, Gratings)
experience_rules.title: 色散系统链式映射检查
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及光谱投影至CCD或屏上的物理过程
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否建立了“波长差 -> 衍射角差 -> 线性位移 -> 像素数”的完整映射链：Δx = f * (dθ/dλ) * Δλ。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Diffraction (Single Slit, Double Slit, Gratings)
experience_rules.title: 衍射主极大宽度反比律
experience_rules.trigger: 计算多缝衍射主极大宽度（两个相邻极小值间距）时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查宽度公式是否满足 Δx = 2 * lambda * L / (N * d)。若分子出现π或分母缺少N，则建模错误。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Diffraction (Single Slit, Double Slit, Gratings)
experience_rules.title: 光栅参数单位转换校验
experience_rules.trigger: 题目给出单位长度内的周期结构数量 n (slit density) 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须确认光栅常数 d = 1/n，并检查 n 的单位是否为长度的倒数（如 m^-1），防止在衍射公式 d sinθ = mλ 中代错位置。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Diffraction (Single Slit, Double Slit, Gratings)
experience_rules.title: 衍射角正弦值有界性检查
experience_rules.trigger: 求解衍射角 β 或证明 sin^-1 形式的表达式时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查参数组合 |nmλ| 是否小于等于 1。若 nmλ > 1，则该级次衍射条纹在物理上不存在，需注意定义域限制。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Diffraction (Single Slit, Double Slit, Gratings)
experience_rules.title: 多缝干涉极大位置与缝数无关律
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及多缝衍射或光栅（N个狭缝，间距d）的主极大位置计算时
experience_rules.check_logic: 核实主极大位置公式中，分母应仅包含间距d，不应包含总缝数N；N仅决定条纹的锐度（宽度）。

topics.topic: Optics / Interference (Young's Double Slit, Thin Films)

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Interference (Young's Double Slit, Thin Films)
experience_rules.title: 平行介质层干涉不变性
experience_rules.trigger: 光束穿过平行平板介质（如玻璃窗、流体管）发生干涉时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否错误地将波长替换为 λ/n。根据折射定律 n1*sinθ1 = n2*sinθ2，空间频率（k_x）在穿过平行界面时保持不变，条纹间距仅取决于入射时的波长和夹角。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Interference (Young's Double Slit, Thin Films)
experience_rules.title: 介质板相位延迟符号判定
experience_rules.trigger: 在干涉路径中引入折射率为 μ、厚度为 w 的介质板
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查光程差公式中介质项的符号。若介质在路径1，则该路径相位滞后，光程差 ΔL = L2 - (L1 + (μ-1)w)，符号应与几何路程差相反。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Interference (Young's Double Slit, Thin Films)
experience_rules.title: 强度表达式常数项完整性
experience_rules.trigger: 题目给出强度与电场平方的比例常数（如 β）
experience_rules.check_logic: 核实最终表达式是否包含该常数。注意时间平均 ⟨cos²(ωt)⟩ = 1/2，若 E=2E0cos(φ/2)，则 I = β * ⟨E²⟩ = 2βE0²cos²(φ/2)。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Interference (Young's Double Slit, Thin Films)
experience_rules.title: 波长与缝宽量级校验
experience_rules.trigger: 当缝宽 d 与波长 λ 处于同一量级（d/λ < 10）且干涉级次 n > 0 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 严禁直接使用小角近似（sinθ≈θ, cosθ≈1），必须先通过 sinθ = nλ/d 计算确切的 cosθ 值。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Interference (Young's Double Slit, Thin Films)
experience_rules.title: 微分法求角宽度校验
experience_rules.trigger: 要求计算波长微变引起的角度变化 Δθ 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 对 d*sinθ = nλ 两边求导得 d*cosθ*Δθ = n*Δλ，需检查 Δθ 是否包含了 cosθ 分母项。

topics.topic: Optics / Laws of Mirrors and Lenses

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Laws of Mirrors and Lenses
experience_rules.title: 区分液滴的光学模型
experience_rules.trigger: 题目涉及液滴、天花板光源及下方接收面时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是利用液滴的折射成像（透镜）还是表面反射成像（面镜）。若光源与观察点在同侧，应使用反射定律及 R=2f。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Laws of Mirrors and Lenses
experience_rules.title: 球冠几何一致性校验
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及曲率半径 R、弦径 D 和接触角 α 时
experience_rules.check_logic: 校验几何关系是否符合 sin(α) = D / (2R) 或 h = R(1 - cos α)。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Polarization of Light
experience_rules.title: 庞加莱球几何相位关系
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及偏振态在庞加莱球上的演化路径或球面三角形面积 S 与相位差 α 的关系
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证相位差 α 是否等于球面三角形所对固体角（面积）的一半，即 S = 2α 或 α = S/2

topics.topic: Optics / Snell's Law and Critical Angle

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Snell's Law and Critical Angle
experience_rules.title: 光线轨迹微分方程构建
experience_rules.trigger: 题目要求求解光线传播距离或轨迹曲线
experience_rules.check_logic: 利用 dx/dz = tan(θ) 或 ds²=dx²+dz² 结合折射定律构造微分方程，积分区间应对应光线从源点到全反射点或观测点。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Snell's Law and Critical Angle
experience_rules.title: 连续介质折射定律应用
experience_rules.trigger: 折射率随坐标连续变化（如 n(z)）且涉及光线轨迹
experience_rules.check_logic: 必须使用分层介质斯涅尔定律不变性 n(z)sinθ(z)=n₀sinθ₀，其中 θ 是光线与法线（梯度方向）的夹角。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Snell's Law and Critical Angle
experience_rules.title: 变折射率介质传播时间积分
experience_rules.trigger: 要求计算光在非均匀介质中的传播时间 tau
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证积分式是否为 tau = (1/c) * integral(n(s) ds)，并需通过守恒律将 ds 转化为单一坐标变量（如 dz 或 dx）的函数。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Snell's Law and Critical Angle
experience_rules.title: 梯度折射率光路守恒律
experience_rules.trigger: 出现折射率随坐标连续变化（如 n=n(x)）的介质时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否应用了斯涅尔定律的微分形式或不变式：n(x) * cos(phi(x)) = Constant，其中 phi 为光线与对称轴的夹角。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Total Internal Reflection
experience_rules.title: 复数波矢实部提取校验
experience_rules.trigger: 涉及全反射、衰减波或复数折射率的电磁波表达式推导
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查波函数是否满足 E = Re{E0 * exp(i(k·r - ωt))}。若kz为纯虚数iδ，则必须产生exp(-δz)的实数衰减项，且相位项仅保留实数波矢分量。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Total Internal Reflection
experience_rules.title: 法拉第电磁感应定律复数形式一致性
experience_rules.trigger: 从电场强度E推导磁感应强度B的矢量表达式
experience_rules.check_logic: 验证 B = (k × E) / ω 是否正确处理了k的复数特性。若k包含虚部，B的各分量间会产生相位差（sin与cos混用）。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Wavefronts and Huygens' Principle
experience_rules.title: 零能量约束下的势能符号判定
experience_rules.trigger: 已知总能量 E = T + V = 0 且动能 T > 0
experience_rules.check_logic: 势能 E_p 必须始终为负值，且其绝对值等于动能。检查表达式是否包含负号及平方项。

experience_rules.topic: Optics / Wavefronts and Huygens' Principle
experience_rules.title: 光学-力学类比中的速度正相关规则
experience_rules.trigger: 题目要求将光线路径类比为保守场中总能量为零的质点轨迹时
experience_rules.check_logic: 检查是否满足 v(r) ∝ n(r)。若误用物理光速定义 v = c/n 则判定为建模错误。

top_down_rules.title: Verify intensity of polarized light using Malus’s Law
top_down_rules.description: Malus’s Law states that the transmitted intensity of polarized light through an analyzer is given by I = I0 * cos²(θ), where θ is the angle between the light's polarization direction and the analyzer's transmission axis. It applies when light is linearly polarized and passes through an ideal polarizer.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the intensity is calculated as I = I0 * cos²(θ), where θ is the correct angle between the polarization and transmission axes. Verify that the incoming light is linearly polarized.
common_errors: Forgetting to square the cosine term.
Using sine instead of cosine.
Using the wrong angle (e.g., complementary angle instead of θ).
Not considering whether the incoming light is already polarized.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Brewster’s angle calculation
top_down_rules.description: Brewster’s angle is the angle of incidence at which light is completely polarized upon reflection. It is given by tan(θB) = n2/n1, where n1 and n2 are the refractive indices of the two media. This applies to unpolarized or partially polarized light striking a dielectric surface.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if θB is calculated using tan(θB) = n2/n1, and verify the refractive indices used. Ensure the calculation is applied to dielectric surfaces and not metallic ones.
common_errors: Using sin or cos instead of tan.
Incorrect assignment of n1 and n2 (e.g., swapping media).
Applying Brewster’s law to metallic surfaces or total internal reflection conditions.

top_down_rules.title: Verify conditions for converting linearly polarized light to circularly polarized light
top_down_rules.description: Linearly polarized light can be converted to circularly polarized light using a quarter-wave plate. The condition is that the linear polarization must be at 45° to the fast or slow axis of the quarter-wave plate, and the plate must introduce a phase difference of π/2.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the polarization direction is at 45° relative to the wave plate's axis and the plate introduces a phase difference of π/2 (or λ/4). Verify the wave plate is correctly oriented and of the correct thickness.
common_errors: Not orienting the linear polarization at 45° to the wave plate axis.
Using a wave plate of incorrect thickness (not λ/4).
Confusing quarter-wave plates with half-wave plates.

top_down_rules.title: Check consistency of Snell’s Law for refracted polarized light
top_down_rules.description: Snell’s Law applies to light passing between two media: n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2). For polarized light, this law holds when considering the angle of refraction at the boundary.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2) holds true for the given angles and refractive indices. Ensure the calculation excludes cases of total internal reflection.
common_errors: Incorrect calculation of sin(θ) for given angles.
Using approximate values of refractive indices without justification.
Applying Snell’s Law to cases involving total internal reflection.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Stokes parameters for describing polarized light
top_down_rules.description: The Stokes parameters (I, Q, U, V) describe the state of polarization of light. I is the total intensity, Q and U describe linear polarization, and V describes circular polarization. These parameters must satisfy physical constraints: I² ≥ Q² + U² + V².
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the calculated Stokes parameters satisfy I² ≥ Q² + U² + V² and if the parameters are consistent with the given polarization state. Verify the interpretation of Q, U, and V for the specific polarization type.
common_errors: Violating the inequality I² ≥ Q² + U² + V².
Misinterpreting the signs of Q, U, or V for specific polarization states.
Assigning incorrect values to Q, U, or V for circularly polarized light.

top_down_rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency of light intensity
top_down_rules.description: Intensity of light is defined as power per unit area and is measured in W/m². For polarization problems, the intensity values must have consistent units throughout calculations.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that all intensity values are expressed in W/m² and units are consistent in equations like I = I0 * cos²(θ). Verify that power and area are correctly defined if intensity is derived.
common_errors: Using arbitrary or undefined units for intensity.
Mixing up power (W) with intensity (W/m²).
Failing to check unit consistency when using derived equations for intensity.

top_down_rules.title: Verify reflection and polarization angle consistency
top_down_rules.description: According to the law of reflection, the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. For polarized light, the reflected and refracted components must respect polarization principles (e.g., Brewster's angle).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection and verify if Brewster's angle is correctly applied for polarization. Confirm the polarization state of the reflected light is consistent with the incident light.
common_errors: Using different angles for incidence and reflection.
Mixing up angles of refraction and reflection.
Failing to check the polarization state of reflected light.

top_down_rules.title: Verify refractive index limits in polarization problems
top_down_rules.description: Refractive indices must be real, positive, and typically greater than 1 for transparent materials. Cases involving polarization require refractive indices consistent with the medium’s nature.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that refractive indices used in equations like Brewster’s Law or Snell’s Law are within physical limits (n > 1 for transparent materials). Verify the refractive index values are appropriate for the given materials.
common_errors: Using refractive indices less than 1 for transparent media.
Assigning negative or imaginary values to refractive indices in polarization problems.
Failing to justify refractive index values for unknown materials.

top_down_rules.title: Verify conditions for partial polarization of light
top_down_rules.description: Partial polarization occurs when unpolarized light becomes partially polarized upon reflection or scattering. The degree of polarization depends on the angle of incidence and the material properties.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify if the degree of polarization is calculated correctly based on the Fresnel equations or experimental data. Ensure the angle of incidence and material properties are considered.
common_errors: Ignoring the dependence of polarization on the angle of incidence.
Failing to account for material properties in partial polarization.
Confusing partial polarization with complete polarization.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Rayleigh Scattering Intensity Relation
top_down_rules.description: Rayleigh scattering intensity I is proportional to 1/λ^4 where λ is the wavelength of light. This implies shorter wavelengths scatter more strongly. This relation is crucial for understanding phenomena like blue skies and red sunsets.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that I ∝ 1/λ^4 in calculations involving Rayleigh scattering.
common_errors: Incorrect dependency on wavelength, e.g., 1/λ^3 or 1/λ^2
Confusing Rayleigh scattering with Mie scattering which does not follow this law

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Small Particle Size Assumption
top_down_rules.description: Rayleigh scattering applies to particles much smaller than the wavelength of light (typically particles with dimensions less than 1/10th the wavelength).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the particle size is significantly smaller than the wavelength of incident light.
common_errors: Applying Rayleigh scattering to particles larger than the wavelength
Ignoring particle size constraints leading to inaccurate scattering predictions

top_down_rules.title: Check Applicability of Low-Refractive Index Particles
top_down_rules.description: Rayleigh scattering assumes the scatterers have a refractive index close to that of their surroundings (typically air). Large differences in refractive index alter scattering behavior.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Compare particle and medium refractive indices to ensure they are nearly similar.
common_errors: Using Rayleigh theory for high refractive contrast particles
Failing to consider the medium's effect on scattering

top_down_rules.title: Verify Dimensional Consistency in Scattering Equations
top_down_rules.description: Ensure all terms in the Rayleigh scattering equation are dimensionally consistent, particularly when calculating intensity and cross-sectional areas.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that intensity calculations yield dimensions of power per unit area, typically W/m².
common_errors: Incorrect units used for wavelength
Inconsistent units in scattering cross-section calculations

top_down_rules.title: Correct Sign Convention in Scattering Angle
top_down_rules.description: In Rayleigh scattering, the direction of scattered light must follow the convention that the phase angle increases from the incident direction. This affects the calculation of the scattering pattern.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that calculations related to scattering angles are performed with the correct sign convention.
common_errors: Using negative angles incorrectly
Mistaking backward and forward scattering definitions

top_down_rules.title: Evaluate Particle Velocity Relative to Light Speed
top_down_rules.description: Rayleigh scattering generally assumes stationary particles relative to the speed of light.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the particle's velocity is negligible compared to the speed of light.
common_errors: Including significant particle velocity impacts in stationary scattering models
Misinterpreting kinematic constraints leading to flawed applications

top_down_rules.title: Check Color Changes and Angles Relation
top_down_rules.description: Rayleigh scattering causes different colors to scatter at different intensities as a function of angle, affecting perceived sky color.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure calculations or explanations factor in the angle-wavelength dependency.
common_errors: Ignoring angle dependency on scattering color
Failing to consider the contribution of varying wavelengths

top_down_rules.title: Verify Law of Reflection
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection, measured with respect to the normal at the interface of the reflecting surface.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that θ_incidence = θ_reflection, where both angles are measured from the normal to the surface. Ensure proper units (radians or degrees) are used consistently.
common_errors: Measuring angles from the surface instead of the normal
Using incorrect units for angles (e.g., radians vs degrees)
Confusing angle of incidence with angle of reflection

top_down_rules.title: Validate Snell's Law
top_down_rules.description: Verify that Snell's Law (n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2)) is satisfied at the interface between two media with indices of refraction n1 and n2.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2), where θ1 and θ2 are angles of incidence and refraction measured from the normal. Confirm that trigonometric functions are applied correctly and units are consistent.
common_errors: Incorrectly identifying the media or their refractive indices
Using the wrong trigonometric function (e.g., cosine instead of sine)
Using degrees instead of radians in calculations without proper conversion

top_down_rules.title: Check Total Internal Reflection Condition
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that total internal reflection occurs only when light travels from a denser to a rarer medium and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that n1 > n2 and θ_incidence > θ_critical, where θ_critical = arcsin(n2/n1). Ensure that the refractive indices are valid and the critical angle is computed correctly.
common_errors: Incorrect computation of the critical angle
Attempting total internal reflection when light is traveling from a rarer to denser medium
Ignoring the condition θ_incidence > θ_critical

top_down_rules.title: Verify Sign Convention for Angles
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that all angles (incidence, reflection, refraction) are measured with respect to the normal to the surface and not the surface itself.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that the reference for angle measurement is the normal to the interface. Verify consistency in angle measurement across all calculations.
common_errors: Measuring angles from the surface instead of the normal
Using inconsistent reference directions for different angles
Misidentifying the normal direction in complex geometries

top_down_rules.title: Enforce Geometric Constraints for Ray Diagrams
top_down_rules.description: Verify that in ray diagrams, incident, reflected, and refracted rays obey geometric constraints such as alignment with the normal and proper angle relationships.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that reflected and refracted rays emerge from the point of incidence and maintain the correct angular relationships with the normal. Confirm that diagrams are consistent with physical laws.
common_errors: Misaligning rays with the point of incidence
Drawing rays that violate the law of reflection or Snell's Law
Incorrectly extending or tracing rays in diagrams

top_down_rules.title: Validate Physical Range of Refractive Indices
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the refractive indices (n1, n2) are greater than or equal to 1, as they represent the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to that in the medium.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that n1 ≥ 1 and n2 ≥ 1. Confirm that refractive indices are assigned correctly for common materials (e.g., air, water, glass).
common_errors: Using a refractive index less than 1 for a physical medium
Incorrectly assigning refractive indices for air (n ≈ 1) or vacuum (n = 1)
Failing to verify refractive indices for exotic materials

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency in Calculations
top_down_rules.description: Verify that all quantities in reflection and refraction equations (angles, refractive indices) have consistent and appropriate units.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that angles are in radians (or properly converted), refractive indices are dimensionless, and trigonometric functions are applied correctly. Ensure unit consistency throughout calculations.
common_errors: Using inconsistent angle units (degrees vs radians)
Applying trigonometric functions to values with incorrect units
Failing to confirm that refractive indices are dimensionless

top_down_rules.title: Verify Boundary Conditions at Interfaces
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that at the interface between two media, the incident, reflected, and refracted rays meet at the same point, and their directions satisfy the laws of reflection and refraction.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the point of incidence is common to all rays and angular relationships follow the laws of reflection and refraction. Confirm that rays are properly aligned in diagrams.
common_errors: Misplacing the point of incidence in ray diagrams
Violating angular relationships at the interface
Failing to align incident, reflected, and refracted rays properly

top_down_rules.title: Verify Critical Angle Calculation
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that the critical angle is calculated correctly for total internal reflection scenarios.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that the critical angle is computed as θ_critical = arcsin(n2/n1) and is only defined when n1 > n2. Verify that the calculation uses valid refractive indices.
common_errors: Using incorrect formula for critical angle
Attempting to calculate a critical angle when n1 ≤ n2
Failing to use valid refractive indices in the calculation

top_down_rules.title: Verify correct application of Snell's Law equation
top_down_rules.description: Snell's Law states that n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2), where n1 and n2 are the refractive indices of the first and second media, and θ1 and θ2 are the angles of incidence and refraction, respectively. This law applies when light passes between two transparent media.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the equation n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2) is used correctly with proper substitution of values for n1, n2, θ1, and θ2.
common_errors: Using incorrect values for refractive indices (n1 or n2).
Using degrees instead of radians in trigonometric functions.
Misinterpreting θ1 or θ2 as complementary angles.

top_down_rules.title: Validate formula for critical angle
top_down_rules.description: The critical angle (θc) occurs when light is incident from a denser medium to a less dense medium, and total internal reflection occurs. The formula for the critical angle is θc = arcsin(n2 / n1), where n1 > n2.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the critical angle is calculated using θc = arcsin(n2 / n1) and that n1 > n2 is satisfied.
common_errors: Using n1 < n2 when applying the formula for critical angle.
Forgetting to use arcsin or incorrectly calculating it.
Calculating the critical angle for an incorrect medium pair.

top_down_rules.title: Check angle sign convention
top_down_rules.description: Angles of incidence and refraction are always measured relative to the normal to the interface. Positive angles should be used for both θ1 and θ2.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that θ1 and θ2 are measured relative to the normal and are positive values.
common_errors: Measuring angles from the surface instead of the normal.
Using negative angles for θ1 or θ2.

top_down_rules.title: Verify conditions for total internal reflection (TIR)
top_down_rules.description: Total internal reflection occurs only when light travels from a medium with a higher refractive index (n1) to a medium with a lower refractive index (n2), and the angle of incidence (θ1) exceeds the critical angle (θc).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if n1 > n2 and θ1 > θc before concluding total internal reflection.
common_errors: Applying TIR when n1 < n2.
Using TIR incorrectly when θ1 is less than or equal to θc.
Confusing TIR with refraction.

top_down_rules.title: Check physical constraints on refractive indices
top_down_rules.description: Refractive indices (n) must always be greater than or equal to 1, as n = c/v, where c is the speed of light in a vacuum and v is the speed of light in the medium.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that n1 and n2 are ≥ 1 for all calculations involving Snell's Law or the critical angle.
common_errors: Using refractive indices less than 1.
Mixing up speed of light in the medium with speed of light in a vacuum.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure dimensional consistency of trigonometric functions
top_down_rules.description: The arguments of trigonometric functions (sin, cos, tan) must be dimensionless. Angles should be either in radians or degrees, depending on the calculator or system setup.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that arguments passed to sin(θ1) and sin(θ2) are dimensionless and consistent with the chosen unit system (radians or degrees).
common_errors: Using angles with incorrect units or dimensions.
Mixing radians and degrees in the same calculation.

top_down_rules.title: Check validity conditions for applying Snell's Law
top_down_rules.description: Snell's Law is valid only for isotropic, homogeneous, and transparent media. It does not apply to scattering, absorption, or birefringent media.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the media involved are isotropic, homogeneous, and transparent before applying Snell's Law.
common_errors: Applying Snell's Law to anisotropic or birefringent materials.
Ignoring scattering or absorption effects in the medium.

top_down_rules.title: Validate geometric constraints at the interface
top_down_rules.description: The angles of incidence and refraction must satisfy the boundary geometry, such that they lie on opposite sides of the normal at the interface.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that θ1 and θ2 are measured in accordance with the boundary geometry and lie on opposite sides of the normal.
common_errors: Placing θ1 and θ2 on the same side of the normal.
Misidentifying the normal or interface geometry.

top_down_rules.title: Verify critical angle calculation
top_down_rules.description: The critical angle is determined using Snell's Law when light moves from a medium with a higher refractive index to one with a lower refractive index. The critical angle is given by sin(θ_critical) = n2/n1, where n1 > n2.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that sin(θ_critical) = n2/n1, verify that n1 > n2, and confirm that the angle is calculated in consistent units (radians or degrees).
common_errors: Swapping n1 and n2 in the formula.
Using n1 < n2, which makes total internal reflection impossible.
Forgetting to ensure angles are in radians or degrees consistently.

top_down_rules.title: Confirm Snell's Law application before total internal reflection
top_down_rules.description: Snell's Law states that n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2). Verify that this relationship holds for angles below the critical angle.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2) for θ1 < θ_critical. Ensure that trigonometric functions are applied correctly and that refractive indices are accurate.
common_errors: Incorrectly applying Snell's Law when θ1 > θ_critical.
Using incorrect trigonometric functions (e.g., using cos instead of sin).
Miscalculating the angle or refractive indices.

top_down_rules.title: Verify angle of incidence exceeds critical angle
top_down_rules.description: Total internal reflection only occurs when the angle of incidence (θ1) is greater than the critical angle (θ_critical).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that θ1 > θ_critical before assuming total internal reflection occurs. Ensure the critical angle is calculated correctly beforehand.
common_errors: Assuming total internal reflection when θ1 < θ_critical.
Not calculating or verifying the critical angle before analyzing the situation.

top_down_rules.title: Check refractive index constraints for total internal reflection
top_down_rules.description: Total internal reflection is only possible if light passes from a medium with a higher refractive index (n1) into a medium with a lower refractive index (n2).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that n1 > n2. If n1 <= n2, total internal reflection cannot occur. Verify the direction of light propagation.
common_errors: Applying total internal reflection when light moves from a lower refractive index medium to a higher refractive index medium.
Neglecting to specify the direction of light propagation.

top_down_rules.title: Verify energy conservation during total internal reflection
top_down_rules.description: During total internal reflection, no energy is transmitted into the second medium, and all the light is reflected back into the first medium. This implies total reflectance.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Confirm that the transmitted intensity is zero and reflected intensity equals the incident intensity. Ensure no energy is lost during the process.
common_errors: Incorrectly assuming partial transmission occurs during total internal reflection.
Failing to equate reflected intensity to incident intensity.

top_down_rules.title: Check for phase shift during total internal reflection
top_down_rules.description: During total internal reflection, a phase shift occurs at the boundary, depending on polarization and angle of incidence. This phase shift does not affect energy conservation.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that a phase shift is considered when analyzing reflected waves during total internal reflection. Ensure the phase shift is not confused with energy loss.
common_errors: Ignoring the phase shift introduced during reflection.
Confusing phase shift with energy loss, which does not occur.

top_down_rules.title: Confirm dimensional consistency in equations
top_down_rules.description: Ensure that all terms in equations related to total internal reflection have consistent dimensions or units. For example, angles should be in radians or degrees consistently, and refractive indices are dimensionless.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that sin(θ), n1, and n2 are dimensionless and angle units are consistent. Ensure no unit mismatches in calculations.
common_errors: Mixing radians and degrees when calculating angles.
Using refractive indices with incorrect or inconsistent dimensions.

top_down_rules.title: Verify geometric path consistency
top_down_rules.description: The geometry of the incident and reflected rays must satisfy boundary conditions. The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection during total internal reflection.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that θ_incidence = θ_reflection and that the reflected ray lies entirely within the first medium. Confirm that the geometry aligns with total internal reflection principles.
common_errors: Setting θ_incidence ≠ θ_reflection.
Placing the reflected ray in the second medium, which contradicts total internal reflection.

top_down_rules.title: Verify polarization effects during total internal reflection
top_down_rules.description: During total internal reflection, the polarization of light can affect the phase shift and intensity distribution. This is particularly important for polarized light.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that polarization effects are considered, especially for s-polarized and p-polarized light. Verify that the phase shift is calculated correctly for each polarization type.
common_errors: Ignoring the impact of polarization on phase shift.
Failing to distinguish between s-polarized and p-polarized light.

top_down_rules.title: Verify wavefront continuity equation
top_down_rules.description: Huygens' Principle states that every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary spherical wavelets, and the new wavefront is the tangential surface to these secondary wavelets. Verify that the wavefront equation matches this principle.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the secondary wavelets are drawn as spherical or plane waves (based on medium properties) and whether the tangent to these wavelets forms the next wavefront. Ensure that the wavelets are spaced consistently with the speed of propagation in the medium.
common_errors: Not drawing the secondary wavelets at all.
Incorrect tangent drawn to wavelets misrepresenting the wavefront.
Wavelets not spaced consistently with the speed of propagation in the medium.

top_down_rules.title: Check wavefront propagation speed consistency
top_down_rules.description: The speed at which wavefronts propagate depends on the properties of the medium (e.g., refractive index). Verify that the wavefront speed is consistent with the equation v = c/n, where n is the refractive index of the medium.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the wavefront spacing corresponds to v = c/n, where c is the speed of light in vacuum and n is the refractive index. Confirm that the refractive index used matches the medium described in the problem.
common_errors: Incorrect wavefront spacing relative to medium speed.
Using the wrong refractive index for the specified medium.
Forgetting that c is only valid in vacuum and not adjusting for n.

top_down_rules.title: Verify applicability of Huygens' Principle
top_down_rules.description: Huygens' Principle is valid for isotropic and homogeneous media. It cannot be directly applied to anisotropic or inhomogeneous media without modifications. Ensure that the problem context satisfies these conditions.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the medium is isotropic (properties same in all directions) and homogeneous (properties constant throughout the medium). If the medium is anisotropic or inhomogeneous, verify that appropriate modifications to Huygens' Principle are applied.
common_errors: Applying Huygens' Principle to anisotropic media without justification.
Ignoring inhomogeneities in the medium that affect wavefront propagation.
Assuming medium properties are constant when they are explicitly variable.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure dimensional consistency in wavefront equations
top_down_rules.description: In the equations governing wavefronts, such as v = c/n or relationships between wavelength and frequency, all terms must have consistent units. Ensure that dimensions match for speed, refractive index, and other quantities.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the units of speed, refractive index, and wavelength-frequency relations are consistent across calculations. Ensure that derived quantities, such as wavefront spacing, are dimensionally correct.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for speed (e.g., mixing m/s with cm/s).
Forgetting that refractive index is unitless.
Mismatched wavelength and frequency units causing errors in derived values.

top_down_rules.title: Verify wavefront geometry based on source type
top_down_rules.description: Wavefronts from a point source are spherical, while wavefronts from a distant source are planar. Ensure that the wavefront geometry matches the source description.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the wavefronts are spherical for point sources and planar for distant sources, or conform to any specific source geometry mentioned in the problem. Verify that the curvature of spherical wavefronts is consistent with the distance from the source.
common_errors: Drawing planar wavefronts for a nearby point source.
Incorrect curvature of spherical wavefronts.
Ignoring the wavefront geometry in calculations.

top_down_rules.title: Verify wavefront bending at boundaries
top_down_rules.description: When a wavefront passes from one medium to another, it bends according to Snell's Law. Verify that the bending of the wavefront at the boundary satisfies the relationship n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2).
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure that the angles of incidence and refraction follow Snell's Law and that the wavefront orientation changes accordingly. Verify that the refractive indices used correspond to the respective media.
common_errors: Incorrect calculation of refraction angles.
Ignoring the refractive index difference between media.
Wavefronts drawn at incorrect angles post-refraction.

top_down_rules.title: Check for wavefront diffraction at obstacles
top_down_rules.description: Wavefronts bend around obstacles, creating diffraction effects. Ensure that the wavefronts are drawn bending into the region of the geometric shadow when diffraction is significant.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that wavefronts are not drawn as straight lines extending through an obstacle and correctly represent bending at edges. Confirm that the extent of diffraction matches the size of the obstacle and the wavelength of the wave.
common_errors: Ignoring diffraction effects entirely.
Drawing wavefronts as straight lines through the obstacle.
Incorrect representation of wave bending at sharp edges.

top_down_rules.title: Ensure consistency in coordinate system and sign conventions
top_down_rules.description: In problems involving wavefronts and Huygens' Principle, ensure that the coordinate system and sign conventions (e.g., positive directions for angles and distances) are consistently applied.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that all angles, distances, and directions are consistently measured with respect to the chosen coordinate system. Ensure that sign conventions are explicitly stated and followed throughout the solution.
common_errors: Switching between different coordinate systems mid-solution.
Using inconsistent sign conventions for angles or distances.
Confusion between clockwise and counterclockwise angle directions.

top_down_rules.title: Verify wavefront superposition in overlapping regions
top_down_rules.description: When wavefronts from multiple sources overlap, the resulting wavefront is determined by the principle of superposition. Ensure that the combined wavefront is correctly represented.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Check if the resultant wavefront is drawn as the constructive or destructive interference of overlapping wavefronts, depending on their phase relationship.
common_errors: Ignoring the effects of superposition in overlapping regions.
Incorrectly representing constructive or destructive interference.
Failing to account for phase differences between overlapping wavefronts.

top_down_rules.title: Verify Stefan-Boltzmann Law Application
top_down_rules.description: Ensure the formula for the Stefan-Boltzmann Law is correctly stated and applied: P = σAeT^4, where σ is the Stefan-Boltzmann constant, A is the area, e is the emissivity, and T is the temperature in Kelvin.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify that the power emitted is calculated using P = σAeT^4, with temperature in Kelvin and consideration of emissivity. Ensure all variables are correctly substituted and calculated.
common_errors: Using incorrect formula for power emitted
Confusing temperature units (Celsius instead of Kelvin)
Neglecting the emissivity factor

top_down_rules.title: Check Dimensional Consistency in Blackbody Equations
top_down_rules.description: Verify that units align correctly: Power emitted (P) should be in Watts.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Ensure the output of P = σAeT^4 has units of Watts (W). Confirm that all input variables have consistent units (e.g., area in square meters, temperature in Kelvin).
common_errors: Incorrect unit conversion leading to power not in Watts
Mismatch in units leading to incorrect calculations

top_down_rules.title: Ensure Temperature is in Kelvin
top_down_rules.description: Confirm that the temperature used in the Stefan-Boltzmann Law is in Kelvin, as this law requires absolute temperature scales.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify temperature input is in Kelvin before substituting into the Stefan-Boltzmann equation. If temperature is provided in Celsius, ensure it is converted to Kelvin using T(K) = T(°C) + 273.15.
common_errors: Using temperature in Celsius instead of Kelvin
Misconversion of temperature units

top_down_rules.title: Verify Wien's Law for Peak Wavelength
top_down_rules.description: Ensure Wien's Law is correctly applied to identify peak wavelength λ_peak = b/T, where b is Wien's displacement constant.
top_down_rules.check_logic: Verify λ_peak is calculated with λ_peak = b/T, and ensure b is correctly valued as approximately 2.898 × 10^-3 m·K. Confirm that T is in Kelvin.
common_errors: Incorrect calculation of the peak wavelength
Misapplication of Wien's displacement constant
Using temperature in incorrect units

top_down_rules.title: Check Validity of Blackbody Assumptions
top_down_rules.description: Confirm that the body assumed to be a blackbody is a perfect emitter or sufficiently close, such as stars or furnace cavities.
